children.title: Sparse Coordinate Relevance Models
children.top_down_role: Search models driven by a small set of influential coordinates.

children.title: Active-Variable Selection
children.top_down_role: Screening and adaptive selection of influential inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Variable Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential coordinate screening using posterior inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observations \(D_t=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^t\), binary relevance variables \(\gamma_j\in\{0,1\}\), and threshold \(\tau_t\in(0,1)\), compute \(p_{t,j}=\Pr(\gamma_j=1\mid D_t)\) and select \(S_t=\{j:p_{t,j}\ge \tau_t\}\). Fit the surrogate and maximize its acquisition function over coordinates in \(S_t\), holding coordinates outside \(S_t\) at a prescribed reference value. Evaluate the resulting point, append the observation to \(D_t\), and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted. Output the best evaluated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly select coordinates whose posterior relevance exceeds a threshold, optimize the acquisition function over them, update with the new observation, and return the best evaluated point.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\).
The relevance posterior \(\Pr(\gamma\mid D_t)\) is well defined.
Inactive coordinates have prescribed feasible reference values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t=\{j:\Pr(\gamma_j=1\mid D_t)\ge\tau_t\}\) determines the iteration-\(t\) search coordinates.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports Bayesian active-variable selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Active-Variable Selection container and is internally coherent, but the specific posterior-threshold screening and conditional Bayesian-optimization procedure has no supporting citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Sparse Axis-Aligned Surrogate Models
children.top_down_role: Surrogates whose relevance structure is aligned with input coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Axis-Aligned Surrogate Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-sparse Gaussian-process surrogate on a Euclidean search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\). A Gaussian-process surrogate is sparse and axis-aligned with active set \(S\) if its prior mean and covariance have the forms \(m(x)=m_S(x_S)\) and \(k(x,x')=k_S(x_S,x'_S)\), with \(|S|\ll d\). Under a likelihood whose observation model depends on an input only through the corresponding latent value, conditioning on data preserves this coordinate invariance: whenever \(x_S=x'_S\), the posterior predictive distributions at \(x\) and \(x'\) are identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse axis-aligned Gaussian-process surrogate has a mean and covariance that depend only on a small coordinate subset. With a compatible observation model, changing excluded coordinates leaves its posterior predictive distribution unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
\(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(|S|\ll d\).
The Gaussian-process mean and covariance depend on inputs only through \(x_S\).
The likelihood depends on each input only through its associated latent surrogate value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(x_S=x'_S\), then the posterior predictive distributions at \(x\) and \(x'\) are identical.

notation.meaning: restriction of x to coordinates in S

review_flags: No supplied citation or locator supports the definition and posterior-invariance claim.

children.title: Variable-Relevance Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Weak identifiability, interactions, and changing relevance during sequential search.

children.title: Relevance Posterior Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty about which coordinates materially influence the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Relevance Posterior Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of hard screening when inclusion probabilities remain diffuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_j=\Pr(\gamma_j=1\mid D)\) and let hard screening select \(S_\tau=\{j:p_j\ge\tau\}\). If some coordinate satisfies \(p_j\in(\delta,1-\delta)\) for a fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\), then neither the inclusion decision nor the exclusion decision has posterior error at most \(\delta\): their respective posterior error probabilities are \(1-p_j\) and \(p_j\). Any deterministic threshold \(\tau\in(\delta,1-\delta)\) nevertheless makes a hard decision, so conditional optimization on \(S_\tau\) discards unresolved model uncertainty. In particular, if thresholding excludes coordinate \(j\), the posterior probability that it is influential is \(p_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diffuse inclusion probabilities make hard variable screening uncertain: thresholding suppresses unresolved model uncertainty, and an excluded coordinate remains influential with its posterior inclusion probability.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma_j\in\{0,1\}\) denotes coordinate relevance.
\(p_j=\Pr(\gamma_j=1\mid D)\) exists.
Hard screening uses \(S_\tau=\{j:p_j\ge\tau\}\) with \(\tau\in(\delta,1-\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(p_j\in(\delta,1-\delta)\), both possible hard relevance decisions have posterior error greater than \(\delta\).
review_flags: No supplied citation or locator supports this posterior-screening failure boundary.

children.title: Interaction-Induced Relevance Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous relevance attribution caused by coordinate interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Induced Relevance Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure interactions defeat marginal relevance screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,X_2\) be independent and uniform on \(\{-1,1\}\), and define \(f(X_1,X_2)=X_1X_2\). Then \(\mathbb E[f\mid X_1]=0=\mathbb E[f]\) and \(\mathbb E[f\mid X_2]=0=\mathbb E[f]\), so screening based on either coordinate's marginal conditional mean assigns no relevance. Nevertheless, changing either coordinate while holding the other fixed reverses \(f\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(f)=1\). Thus marginal screening can reject every coordinate although the objective is entirely generated by their interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the product of two independent signs, each variable has zero marginal effect, yet both are essential through their interaction; marginal screening rejects them incorrectly.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) are independent uniform signs.
Relevance screening uses marginal conditional-mean effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero marginal effects do not imply coordinate irrelevance in the presence of interactions.
review_flags: Concrete calculation is self-contained, but no supporting source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction-only example is correct, self-contained, and appropriately classified as a counterexample, but the evidence contract still requires a source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Low-Order Additive Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Decompositions into components involving restricted coordinate groups.

children.title: Known Additive Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Search with prescribed component groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Additive Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive representation over prescribed coordinate groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be prescribed groups and \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). A known additive decomposition represents the objective as \(f(x)=c+\sum_{r=1}^m f_r(x_{G_r})\). If independent component Gaussian processes satisfy \(f_r\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k_r)\), then \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(c,k)\) with \(k(x,x')=\sum_{r=1}^m k_r(x_{G_r},x'_{G_r})\). The groups may overlap unless disjointness is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prescribed additive model sums functions of known coordinate groups; independent Gaussian-process components induce a covariance equal to the sum of component covariances.
assumptions_latex: \(G_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) are fixed before optimization.
Each component \(f_r\) depends only on \(x_{G_r}\).
Gaussian-process components are mutually independent when the covariance identity is used.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports additive Gaussian-process decompositions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes prescribed additive groups and the covariance of independent Gaussian-process components, but no source or locator supports these claims.

children.title: Learned Additive Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Search with inferred groups or interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned Additive Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint posterior learning of component groups and response functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite family of admissible group collections and assign prior \(\pi(G)\) to \(G\in\mathcal G\). Given \(D_t\), compute \(\pi(G\mid D_t)\propto p(D_t\mid G)\pi(G)\), where each model uses \(f(x)=\sum_{A\in G}f_A(x_A)\). Define the model-averaged acquisition \(\bar a_t(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}a_t(x;G)\pi(G\mid D_t)\), choose \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\bar a_t(x)\), observe the response, and update until the budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infer additive groupings from data, average the acquisition function over their posterior probabilities, evaluate its maximizer, and update both structure and components sequentially.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a finite set of admissible group collections.
The marginal likelihood \(p(D_t\mid G)\) is defined for every \(G\in\mathcal G\).
Each candidate model is additive over its groups.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}a_t(x;G)\pi(G\mid D_t)\).
review_flags: The exact learning rule is one coherent Bayesian formulation, but no supporting locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives one coherent Bayesian model-averaging algorithm for learned decompositions and fits the container, but this is a specific formulation rather than a universal definition. An authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Component Overlap Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Decompositions with shared variables or nested interaction groups.

children.title: Overlapping Components
children.top_down_role: Component decompositions in which variables participate in multiple groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive components whose coordinate groups are not pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an additive representation \(f(x)=\sum_{r=1}^m f_r(x_{G_r})\) with groups \(G_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the components are overlapping if there exist distinct indices \(r,s\) such that \(G_r\cap G_s\ne\varnothing\). A coordinate in \(G_r\cap G_s\) may affect both component functions; consequently, component effects are not uniquely attributable without additional centering, orthogonality, or identifiability constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive components overlap when two component groups share a coordinate; separating the shared coordinate's contribution then requires extra identifiability constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G_r\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition is overlapping exactly when \(G_r\cap G_s\ne\varnothing\) for some \(r\ne s\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports overlapping additive components.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of overlapping groups is precise and fits the leaf. The accompanying identifiability claim is nontrivial and has no supporting citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Hierarchical Components
children.top_down_role: Nested component structures spanning multiple interaction levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-heredity condition for additive interaction components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\subseteq 2^{\{1,\ldots,d\}}\) index the nonzero terms in \(f(x)=\sum_{A\in\mathcal H}f_A(x_A)\). The decomposition satisfies strong hierarchy when, for every \(A\in\mathcal H\), every nonempty subset \(B\subset A\) also belongs to \(\mathcal H\). Equivalently, an interaction component may be present only if all of its lower-order parent components are present. Under weak hierarchy, the corresponding requirement is relaxed to at least one immediate parent \(A\setminus\{j\}\) being present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong hierarchy permits an interaction only when every lower-order subcomponent is included; weak hierarchy requires at least one immediate parent.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) indexes precisely the nonzero components.
Each \(f_A\) depends only on coordinates in \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong hierarchy holds iff \(A\in\mathcal H\) and \(\varnothing\ne B\subset A\) imply \(B\in\mathcal H\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports hierarchical interaction conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong- and weak-hierarchy conditions are coherent and the condition content kind fits, but hierarchy terminology can be convention dependent and no supporting source locator is supplied.

children.title: Shared-Variable Attribution
children.top_down_role: Allocation of explanatory influence when components reuse coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonidentifiability of component attribution on shared coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(G_1\cap G_2\ne\varnothing\), choose \(j\in G_1\cap G_2\), and write \(f(x)=f_1(x_{G_1})+f_2(x_{G_2})\). For any nonzero function \(h\) of \(x_j\), define \(\tilde f_1=f_1+h\) and \(\tilde f_2=f_2-h\). Then \(\tilde f_1(x_{G_1})+\tilde f_2(x_{G_2})=f(x)\), although the contribution assigned to each component changes. Hence shared-variable attribution is not identifiable from the summed response alone unless normalization, orthogonality, or other separating constraints are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function of any shared coordinate can be transferred between overlapping components without changing their sum, so component-level attribution is nonidentifiable without constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G_1\cap G_2\ne\varnothing\).
The observations identify only the summed response \(f_1+f_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The component pair \((f_1,f_2)\) is not identifiable under unrestricted transfers \((f_1+h,f_2-h)\).

notation.meaning: arbitrary transfer function of a shared coordinate

review_flags: The nonidentifiability construction is self-contained, but no supporting source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer construction correctly demonstrates nonidentifiability and fits Shared-Variable Attribution as a failure boundary, but it lacks the required citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Misspecified Additivity
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes dominated by neglected interactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Misspecified Additivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreducible approximation error from omitted cross-group interactions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_X\) be an input distribution and let \(\mathcal A=\{c+\sum_{r=1}^m g_r(x_{G_r}):g_r\in L^2(P_{X_{G_r}})\}\) be the prescribed additive class. For a square-integrable objective \(f\), define \(f_{\mathcal A}\) as its \(L^2(P_X)\) projection onto the closure of \(\mathcal A\), and let \(r=f-f_{\mathcal A}\). If \(\lVert r\rVert_{L^2(P_X)}>0\), no surrogate restricted to \(\mathcal A\) can recover \(f\) exactly, even with noiseless dense data; neglected interactions impose irreducible model bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective has a nonzero component outside the prescribed additive function class, additive surrogates retain irreducible approximation bias even with unlimited noiseless data.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate is restricted to the closure of \(\mathcal A\).
The indicated orthogonal projection exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{g\in\overline{\mathcal A}}\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(P_X)}=\lVert r\rVert_{L^2(P_X)}>0\).

notation.meaning: best additive projection of the objective

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports additive-model misspecification in this form.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hilbert-space approximation statement precisely captures misspecified additivity and uses an appropriate failure-boundary kind, but no source locator supports the projection-based formulation or its modeling interpretation.

children.title: Low-Dimensional Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Search through latent subspaces or manifolds of a high-dimensional domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of a high-dimensional objective through a lower-dimensional linear projection, including the axis-alignment limitation of coordinatewise relevance scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A low-dimensional linear-embedding model has the form \(f(x)=g(Ax)\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times n}\), \(g:\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R\), and typically \(k\ll n\). Coordinatewise relevance scaling can effectively suppress axes having sufficiently long length scales but is restricted to axis-aligned subspaces; allowing an arbitrary matrix \(A\) permits non-axis-aligned subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-dimensional objective can be modeled through a much lower-dimensional linear projection. Coordinatewise relevance scaling can suppress irrelevant axes but is restricted to axis-aligned subspaces, whereas an arbitrary projection can represent non-axis-aligned influential directions.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n
A\in\mathbb R^{k\times n}
g:\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R
k\ll n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathcal X,\quad f(x)=g(Ax).

children.title: Random Embedding Methods
children.top_down_role: Latent search spaces produced without task-specific subspace learning.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Embedding Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization through a task-independent random linear embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), latent dimension \(q<d\), and budget \(T\), draw a task-independent random matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{d\times q}\). Choose a latent domain \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) and a feasible map \(\phi_A:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\), such as projection of \(Az\) onto \(\mathcal X\). Initialize observations of \(g(z)=f(\phi_A(z))\). At iteration \(t\), fit a surrogate to latent observations, select \(z_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in\mathcal Z}a_t(z)\), evaluate \(f(\phi_A(z_{t+1}))\), and update. Return the best evaluated ambient point after \(T\) evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw a random low-dimensional linear embedding, run Bayesian optimization in its latent domain through a feasible ambient map, and return the best evaluated ambient point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(q<d\).
\(\phi_A(z)\in\mathcal X\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\).
Function evaluations are available at mapped ambient points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}=\phi_A(z_{t+1})\), where \(z_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in\mathcal Z}a_t(z)\).

notation.meaning: feasible map from latent to ambient space

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports random-embedding Bayesian optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches Random Embedding Methods and introduces its domains and maps consistently. Its embedding distribution, latent domain, and feasible-map construction are method-dependent, however, and no cited source establishes this formulation.

children.title: Learned Linear Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Task-adaptive estimation of influential linear directions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^D\) is compact and observations are \(y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\).
The chosen latent dimension satisfies \(1\le d<D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned projector \(U_nU_n^\top\) identifies the estimated influential linear subspace, and Bayesian optimization may be conducted over \(z=U_n^\top x\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis of a candidate influential subspace
surrogate predictor fitted in projected coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, task-adaptive linear dimension reduction for Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal D_n=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\), a learned linear subspace is represented by an orthonormal matrix \(U_n\) obtained from an objective of the form \[ (U_n,\theta_n)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{U^\top U=I_d,\,\theta}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n \ell\bigl(y_i,m_{U,\theta}(U^\top x_i)\bigr)+\lambda R(U,\theta)\right\}. \] The associated structured model is \(f(x)\approx g(U_n^\top x)\). Consequently, points having equal projected coordinates are indistinguishable to the reduced surrogate, while optimization is performed over the feasible projection \(U_n^\top\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An influential subspace is learned jointly with a reduced surrogate, after which Bayesian optimization searches projected coordinates rather than the full ambient space.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned Linear Subspaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The generic empirical objective does not define the loss, regularizer, regularization parameter, surrogate parameter space, or conditions under which a minimizer exists. Because learned-subspace objectives vary materially by method, authoritative method-specific support is required before this representation can be reviewed as mathematically reliable.

children.title: Nonlinear Latent Search Spaces
children.top_down_role: Encoder- or manifold-based representations of structured inputs.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is the structured input domain and \(\mathcal Z\subset\mathbb R^d\) is the latent search domain.
The decoder maps every searched latent point to a feasible input: \(D(\mathcal Z)\subseteq\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Latent Bayesian optimization replaces \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\) by \(\min_{z\in\mathcal Z}f(D(z))\), possibly with an encoder-based surrogate representation.

notation.meaning: encoder from inputs to latent coordinates
decoder from latent coordinates to feasible inputs
objective induced on the latent domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoder-decoder or manifold coordinates used as the Bayesian-optimization search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear latent search representation consists of maps \(E:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z\) and \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\), with attainable set \(\mathcal X_D=D(\mathcal Z)\). Bayesian optimization models and selects points for the induced objective \[ h(z)=f(D(z)),\qquad z\in\mathcal Z, \] and evaluates the structured input \(x=D(z)\). Exact preservation of the original optimization problem requires \[ \inf_{z\in\mathcal Z}f(D(z))=\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x). \] The common reconstruction identity \(D(E(x))=x\) need only hold on the subset whose objective values must be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoder turns low-dimensional latent candidates into feasible structured inputs, and optimization is exact only when the decoded set contains an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Latent Search Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Equality of infima does not, under the stated assumptions, imply the plain-text claim that the decoded set contains an original optimizer; attainment and suitable compactness or closedness assumptions are missing. The reconstruction statement is also method-dependent and does not precisely specify the subset on which it is required.

children.title: Latent Embedding Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Coverage, boundary, and distortion failures caused by inadequate latent representations.

children.title: Latent-Space Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relevant search regions omitted by the embedded domain.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is compact, \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, and \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\).
The decoded attainable set is \(\mathcal X_D=D(\mathcal Z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal X_D\cap\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)=\varnothing\), latent search has an irreducible optimality gap \(\Delta_D>0\).

notation.meaning: best-value loss caused by incomplete coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreducible optimization error caused by incomplete decoder coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the latent-space coverage gap by \[ \Delta_D:=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z}f(D(z))-\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\ge 0. \] If every global minimizer lies outside the attainable set, so that \(\mathcal X_D\cap\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)=\varnothing\), compactness and continuity imply \(\Delta_D>0\). No acquisition function, surrogate consistency property, or evaluation budget restricted to decoded points can reduce simple regret below \(\Delta_D\). Thus coverage of merely typical inputs is insufficient; the attainable set must contain points with arbitrarily near-optimal objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the decoder cannot reach any global optimizer, every latent-only method retains a positive objective gap regardless of its surrogate or evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Latent-Space Coverage Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited, and the claimed positive gap is not valid from the stated assumptions alone. The image D(Z) need not be compact or closed, the displayed minimum over Z need not be attained, and an attainable set can omit every minimizer while approaching one arbitrarily closely, yielding zero gap. A source-supported correction must add conditions such as compact Z and continuous D, or closedness of the attainable set, and distinguish minima from infima.

children.title: Underestimated Latent Dimension
children.top_down_role: Representations whose latent dimension cannot express influential variation.

assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{D\times r}\) has orthonormal columns and \(k<r\).
The searched affine embedding is \(x=x_0+Az\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{D\times k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(z_\star-B^\top x_0\notin\operatorname{range}(B^\top A)\), the embedded search has strictly positive minimum loss although the ambient minimum is zero.

notation.meaning: basis of the true influential subspace
basis of the underestimated search embedding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear counterexample for choosing fewer latent coordinates than influential directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\|B^\top x-z_\star\|_2^2\) on any compact domain containing an \(x_\star\) with \(B^\top x_\star=z_\star\). The ambient optimum is zero. Along the \(k\)-dimensional embedding \(x=x_0+Az\), however, \[ \inf_z f(x_0+Az)=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(z_\star-B^\top x_0,\operatorname{range}(B^\top A)\right)^2. \] Since \(\operatorname{rank}(B^\top A)\le k<r\), targets exist for which this distance is positive. Hence a latent dimension below the influential dimension can exclude the optimum even with an otherwise exact surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent space smaller than the true influential dimension cannot represent every optimal influential coordinate and can therefore impose positive irreducible regret.
knowledge_statements.title: Underestimated Latent Dimension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The objective is declared on a compact domain, but the displayed infimum ranges over every latent z without requiring x0+Az to remain in that domain. With feasible latent points restricted by the compact domain, the distance-to-range identity need not hold. The counterexample needs a consistently defined ambient domain or a feasibility-restricted formula supported by a specific source.

children.title: Boundary Projection Failures
children.top_down_role: Coverage defects arising near projected domain boundaries.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=[-1,1]^D\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{D\times d}\), and decoding uses coordinatewise projection.
The latent surrogate treats distinct latent points as distinct inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection can make the decoder noninjective and locally constant, invalidating latent geometry and producing acquisition plateaus unrelated to objective variation on \(\mathcal X\).

notation.meaning: coordinatewise Euclidean projection onto the box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by clipping an unbounded or oversized embedding to a bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the decoder \(D(z)=\Pi_{\mathcal X}(Az)\), coordinate \(j\) satisfies \[ D_j(z)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,(Az)_j\}\}. \] If \((Az)_j>1\) and a perturbation \(v\) preserves \((A(z+tv))_j>1\) for \(0\le t\le\epsilon\), then \(D_j(z+tv)=1\) throughout that interval. If all varying coordinates are similarly saturated, \(D(z+tv)=D(z)\) despite \(z+tv\ne z\). Thus large latent regions may decode to the same boundary point, creating duplicate evaluations and destroying the distance structure assumed by a latent kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping embedded candidates to a box can collapse many latent points onto one boundary point, causing duplicate evaluations and misleading latent distances.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Projection Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clipping calculation is internally plausible and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the projected-decoder convention or the asserted consequences for latent kernels and acquisition behavior. A method-specific reference with a section, theorem, or page locator is required.

children.title: Embedding Geometry Distortion
children.top_down_role: Latent representations that misstate proximity or feasible geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\) maps metric spaces \((\mathcal Z,d_{\mathcal Z})\) and \((\mathcal X,d_{\mathcal X})\).
The surrogate kernel is parameterized using latent distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stable geometric transfer requires positive lower and finite upper distortion bounds; violation of either bound permits latent proximity to misrepresent input proximity.

notation.meaning: decoder from latent to input space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bi-Lipschitz criterion delimiting geometry-preserving latent search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a searched set \(S\subseteq\mathcal Z\), bounded embedding distortion is the existence of constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \[ c\,d_{\mathcal Z}(z,z')\le d_{\mathcal X}(D(z),D(z'))\le C\,d_{\mathcal Z}(z,z') \quad\text{for all }z,z'\in S. \] If the lower bound fails, distant latent points may collapse to nearly identical inputs. If the upper bound fails, nearby latent points may decode far apart. Either failure breaks the interpretation of a stationary latent kernel as encoding comparable input-space smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoder preserves useful search geometry only when input distances are bounded above and below by constant multiples of latent distances.
knowledge_statements.title: Embedding Geometry Distortion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The bi-Lipschitz condition is a recognizable geometric condition, but the claim that failure of either global bound breaks the smoothness interpretation of a stationary latent kernel depends on the selected metrics, kernel, and regularity model. Because this leaf lies under a failure-boundary container, a source is also needed to determine whether the terminal record should remain a condition or be formulated as a failure_boundary.

children.title: Localized High-Dimensional Search
children.top_down_role: Search controlled through adaptive restrictions of the active domain.

children.title: Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Local Bayesian optimization organized around adaptive search regions.

children.title: Single-Region Search
children.top_down_role: Localized search centered on one active region.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^D\) is bounded and evaluations of \(f\) may be noisy.
A local probabilistic surrogate and acquisition rule are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the best observed feasible point after the evaluation budget is exhausted, while all acquisition maximizations occur inside the current single region.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic single trust-region Bayesian-optimization scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a center \(c_0\in\mathcal X\), lengths \(L_0>0\), counters \(s_0=q_0=0\), and \(R_0=\mathcal X\cap\{x:|x_j-c_{0j}|\le L_{0j}/2\}\). At iteration \(t\), fit the local surrogate to relevant observations, choose \[ x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in R_t}a_t(x), \] evaluate \(f(x_{t+1})\), and classify the evaluation as a success or failure relative to the incumbent. Update the counters and resize \(L_t\) after prescribed consecutive-success or consecutive-failure thresholds. Recenter at the best local observation; restart when the region becomes smaller than its minimum permitted size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-region Bayesian optimization repeatedly maximizes an acquisition function inside one adaptive trust region, resizing, recentering, and eventually restarting that region.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Region Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The success rule, observation assignment, recentering rule, resizing thresholds, restart behavior, and treatment of a noisy incumbent are left method-dependent. The conclusion additionally says the algorithm returns the best observed feasible point, but that output step is not stated in the algorithm and may be inappropriate without defining how noisy observations are compared.

children.title: Multiple-Region Search
children.top_down_role: Concurrent or competing local regions.

assumptions_latex: There are \(M\ge2\) active trust regions with local surrogates.
Each evaluation is assigned to one region, and a global budget of \(N\) evaluations is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the best observation across all regions, with region allocation determined by competing local acquisition values or an explicit scheduler.

notation.meaning: active trust region indexed by m
local acquisition function for region m

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic competing trust-region Bayesian-optimization scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize regions \(R_0^{(1)},\ldots,R_0^{(M)}\) with distinct centers and independent lifecycle states. At iteration \(t\), each active region proposes \[ x_t^{(m)}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in R_t^{(m)}}a_t^{(m)}(x). \] Select a region-candidate pair by \((m_t,x_{t+1})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{m}a_t^{(m)}(x_t^{(m)})\), or by a stated budget scheduler, and evaluate \(x_{t+1}\). Update only the assigned region's surrogate, counters, size, and center. Retire or restart regions meeting their termination criterion, maintaining at most \(M\) active regions until the global budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-region search maintains competing local surrogates and trust regions, allocates evaluations among their candidates, and independently resizes or restarts each region.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Region Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Acquisition values from independently fitted local models are not automatically comparable across regions, and the alternative of an unspecified scheduler does not define a complete algorithm. Region initialization, data sharing, allocation, retirement, and replenishment rules require method-specific authoritative support.

children.title: Adaptive Region Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Families for abandoning, resizing, splitting, or reinitializing regions.

children.title: Restart Triggers
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to abandon an unproductive local search.

assumptions_latex: A region has length statistic \(L_t>0\), minimum length \(L_{\min}>0\), and failure counter \(q_t\).
A prescribed failure tolerance \(\tau_f\in\mathbb N\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(L_t<L_{\min}\) or \(q_t\ge\tau_f\) is a verifiable restart trigger; optional stagnation criteria must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational predicate for terminating and restarting an unproductive trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_t\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether iteration \(t\) achieves the prescribed improvement. Update \(q_{t+1}=0\) when \(I_t=1\) and \(q_{t+1}=q_t+1\) otherwise. A size-or-failure restart trigger is \[ \mathsf{Restart}_{t+1}\iff \bigl(L_{t+1}<L_{\min}\bigr)\lor\bigl(q_{t+1}\ge\tau_f\bigr). \] A stagnation trigger may additionally require \(\max_{t-w<i\le t}f_i^{\mathrm{best}}-\min_{t-w<i\le t}f_i^{\mathrm{best}}\le\epsilon\) over a fixed window \(w\), with signs reversed for maximization. Once the predicate holds, the current region is terminated before another local proposal is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region restarts when it becomes too small, accumulates enough consecutive failures, or satisfies another explicitly quantified stagnation test.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Triggers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Treating q at the failure tolerance as an immediate restart conflicts with the sibling resizing policy, where reaching that tolerance triggers contraction. Likewise, a minimum-size test using L below L_min is unreachable if resizing clamps L at L_min. A specific lifecycle convention and source are required to resolve these trigger semantics.

children.title: Region Resizing Policies
children.top_down_role: Control of local-region extent across search conditions.

assumptions_latex: The scalar region size is constrained by \(0<L_{\min}\le L_t\le L_{\max}\).
Success and failure tolerances \(\tau_s,\tau_f\in\mathbb N\) and multipliers \(\gamma_+>1\), \(0<\gamma_-<1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy expands after \(\tau_s\) consecutive successes, contracts after \(\tau_f\) consecutive failures, and otherwise preserves region size.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counter-based multiplicative resizing of a local Bayesian-optimization region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After classifying the newest evaluation, increment the corresponding counter and reset the other. Update the region size by \[ L_{t+1}=\begin{cases} \min\{\gamma_+L_t,L_{\max}\},&s_{t+1}\ge\tau_s,\\ \max\{\gamma_-L_t,L_{\min}\},&q_{t+1}\ge\tau_f,\\ L_t,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \] Reset both counters whenever a resize occurs. For an anisotropic region, apply the scalar factor to a fixed or surrogate-derived aspect vector and intersect the resulting region with \(\mathcal X\). If contraction reaches the minimum admissible size without subsequent success, the lifecycle passes to its restart rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust region expands after enough consecutive successes, contracts after enough consecutive failures, and stays unchanged between those thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Region Resizing Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a resizing-policy leaf and the piecewise update is internally clear, but no source supports this particular counter convention, clamping rule, anisotropic extension, or transition from minimum size to restart. The last transition is not fully specified and must be reconciled with the restart-trigger record.

children.title: Region Splitting Strategies
children.top_down_role: Subdivision of promising or heterogeneous local regions.

assumptions_latex: A parent region \(R\subseteq\mathcal X\) contains observations on both sides of an admissible split.
A coordinate \(j\) and threshold \(u\) are selected by a stated score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children cover the parent, overlap only on the splitting boundary, and can thereafter maintain independent Bayesian-optimization states.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary partition rule for replacing one heterogeneous region by two local searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidate coordinate-threshold pairs, select \((j,u)\) maximizing a declared heterogeneity or expected-gain score, subject to minimum child-data and minimum-width constraints. Form \[ R^-=R\cap\{x:x_j\le u\},\qquad R^+=R\cap\{x:x_j\ge u\}. \] Initialize each child at its best contained observation, or at a feasible acquisition maximizer if it contains none, and inherit or refit its local surrogate. Replace \(R\) by \(R^-\) and \(R^+\), assign boundary observations by a fixed tie rule, and evolve the children independently under the region resizing and restart policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A splitting strategy selects a coordinate and threshold, partitions one region into two valid children, and initializes an independent local search in each.
knowledge_statements.title: Region Splitting Strategies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The declared score, admissible split set, child-data and width constraints, boundary tie rule, surrogate inheritance, and empty-child initialization are essential parts of the proposed algorithm but remain unspecified. There is no single standard Bayesian-optimization splitting strategy from which these choices can be inferred.

children.title: Region Reinitialization
children.top_down_role: Placement of replacement regions after local search termination.

assumptions_latex: A region has met a restart predicate and a set of feasible previously evaluated points is available.
A restart score \(b_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and initial size \(L_0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reinitialization creates a fresh region state centered at a feasible restart-score maximizer and prevents stale counters or size from carrying across the restart.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-reset rule following termination of a local trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the restart predicate holds, retire the current region and choose \[ c_{\mathrm{new}}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X\setminus E_t}b_t(x), \] where \(E_t\) is an optional exclusion set around active centers or exhausted regions. Define the new region as \(R_{\mathrm{new}}=\mathcal X\cap\{x:|x_j-c_{\mathrm{new},j}|\le L_{0j}/2\}\). Reset success and failure counters to zero, initialize a fresh local surrogate state from observations assigned to \(R_{\mathrm{new}}\), and generate subsequent candidates only after this initialization. If the maximization is randomized, its distribution and random seed convention form part of the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After termination, the method selects a new feasible center, restores the initial region size, clears lifecycle counters, and initializes a fresh local surrogate.
knowledge_statements.title: Region Reinitialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The feasible set outside the exclusion set may be empty, and no compactness or regularity assumptions ensure that the restart-score argmax exists. The assumptions introduce scalar L0 while the region formula uses components L0j. Observation assignment, exclusion construction, and fresh-surrogate initialization also require a method-specific algorithmic source.

children.title: Hierarchical Partition Search
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical subdivision into competing regions.

children.title: Space-Partitioning Search
children.top_down_role: Search organized through competing subdivisions of the domain.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact search space.
At iteration \(t\), the leaves \(\mathcal L_t\) form a finite partition of \(X\).
Each leaf \(R\) has a computable optimistic score \(U_t(R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in R_t\) is evaluated and \(\mathcal L_{t+1}\) remains a partition of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic optimistic partition search for localized Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite partition \(\mathcal L_0=\{X\}\). At iteration \(t\), compute \(U_t(R)\) for every \(R\in\mathcal L_t\), choose \(R_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{R\in\mathcal L_t}U_t(R)\), and select \(x_t\in R_t\) by maximizing a within-region acquisition function. After observing the response at \(x_t\), either retain \(R_t\) or replace it by finitely many pairwise disjoint children whose union is \(R_t\). Stop when the evaluation budget is exhausted and return the best observed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly select the most optimistic partition cell, evaluate within it, and optionally replace it by disjoint children until the evaluation budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.title: Space-Partitioning Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Space-Partitioning Search leaf, but the cited branch-and-bound section does not reliably support the stated Bayesian-optimization acquisition rule, posterior-dependent optimistic score, or retain-versus-split procedure. A direct hierarchical or partition-based Bayesian-optimization source is required.

children.title: Hierarchical Region Trees
children.top_down_role: Tree representations of nested candidate regions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set.
Every internal node has finitely many children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every internal node \(v\), the regions indexed by \(\operatorname{ch}(v)\) form a finite partition of \(R_v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted trees that recursively partition optimization regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hierarchical region tree on \(X\) is a rooted tree \(T=(V,E)\) with a nonempty region \(R_v\subseteq X\) assigned to each node \(v\in V\). Its root \(r\) satisfies \(R_r=X\). For every internal node \(v\), the family \(\{R_w:w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)\}\) is finite and pairwise disjoint, and \[R_v=\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}R_w.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical region tree assigns the whole domain to its root and recursively partitions every internal node's region among its finitely many children.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Region Trees

children.title: Partition Refinement Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria governing which regions receive finer resolution.

assumptions_latex: Each active leaf \(R\) has posterior summaries \(\mu_t(R)\) and \(s_t(R)\).
A nonnegative resolution measure \(\delta(R)\) is available.
\(\beta_t,L_t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only a leaf attaining the largest optimistic score is refined, with ties resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An optimistic criterion balancing predicted value, uncertainty, and spatial resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization, define the regional optimistic score \[U_t(R)=\mu_t(R)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_t(R)+L_t\delta(R).\] An active leaf \(R_t\) is eligible for refinement exactly when \(R_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{R\in\mathcal L_t}U_t(R)\) and \(\delta(R_t)>\delta_{\min}\). If the resolution condition fails, the algorithm evaluates or retains the leaf without splitting it. For minimization, apply the same criterion to \(-f\), or equivalently reverse the value bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine an unresolved leaf only when its posterior value, uncertainty, and geometric resolution give the largest optimistic regional score.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition Refinement Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the refinement-criteria leaf, but the particular additive score, the exact eligibility equivalence, and the threshold behavior are algorithm-specific and uncited. A direct source defining this refinement rule is required.

children.title: Localization Entrapment Failures
children.top_down_role: Failure of local restrictions to preserve global discovery.

children.title: Premature Region Contraction
children.top_down_role: Local restrictions imposed before sufficient global evidence is available.

assumptions_latex: The query sequence is \((x_t)_{t\geq1}\subseteq X\), and \(\tau\geq1\) is finite.
Every query with \(t\geq\tau\) lies in \(R_\tau=[0,0.5]\).
Every query with \(1\leq i<\tau\) satisfies \(f(x_i)\geq0.16\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simple regret satisfies \(r_t\geq0.16\) for every \(t\geq\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss from permanently excluding the global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^\star=0.9\) and define \(r_t=\min_{1\leq i\leq t}f(x_i)-f(x^\star)\). If every query from time \(\tau\) onward is restricted to \(R_\tau=[0,0.5]\), and no earlier query has objective value below \(0.16\), then \(r_t\geq0.16\) for every \(t\geq\tau\). This gives a smooth convex instance on which irreversible contraction away from \(x^\star\) prevents vanishing simple regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If localization excludes the minimizer and no earlier query found a better value, contraction to the wrong half of the interval leaves simple regret at least 0.16.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Region Contraction

children.title: Basin Entrapment
children.top_down_role: Persistent search within a locally attractive basin.

assumptions_latex: The query sequence is \((x_t)_{t\geq1}\subseteq X\), and \(\tau\geq1\) is finite.
Every query with \(t\geq\tau\) lies in \(B=[0.5,1.5]\).
Every query with \(1\leq i<\tau\) satisfies \(f(x_i)\geq0.2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simple regret satisfies \(r_t\geq0.2\) for every \(t\geq\tau\), whereas \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A localized optimizer remains in a strictly suboptimal basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The objective has global minimum \(f(-1)=0\), while \(x=1\) is a strict local minimizer with value \(0.2\), and \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=0.2\). Define \(r_t=\min_{1\leq i\leq t}f(x_i)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). If all queries from time \(\tau\) onward lie in \(B\), and no earlier query has value below \(0.2\), then \(r_t\geq0.2\) for every \(t\geq\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent localization in the suboptimal basin leaves simple regret at least 0.2 when no earlier query found a better value.
knowledge_statements.title: Basin Entrapment

children.title: Global-Discovery Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms preserving exploration beyond localized regions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact separable metric space.
A probability measure \(q\) satisfies \(q(O)>0\) for every nonempty open \(O\subseteq X\).
Independent exploration indicators have probabilities \(\varepsilon_t\) with \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_t=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The query sequence visits every nonempty open subset of \(X\) infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: Nonempty open subset of the domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent random exploration prevents permanent exclusion of any open region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), explore with probability \(\varepsilon_t\) by drawing \(x_t\sim q\), independently of previous exploration draws; otherwise use the localized acquisition rule. For every nonempty open set \(O\), the exploration-hit probabilities are \(\varepsilon_t q(O)\), whose sum diverges. Hence independent exploration hits \(O\) infinitely often almost surely. Applying this to a countable topological base shows that the complete query sequence is almost surely dense in \(X\), so no open basin can be excluded permanently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing localized search with persistent full-support random exploration makes the query sequence dense and prevents permanent exclusion of an open basin.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Discovery Safeguards

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The safeguard is mathematically plausible and locally relevant, but the almost-sure infinite-visitation and density guarantee is a theorem rather than a generic principle. It also lacks a citation for the independence and Borel-Cantelli conditions supporting the guarantee.

children.title: Heterogeneous Discrete Domain Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Non-Euclidean and heterogeneous input domains requiring structure-aware representations and inner optimizers.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Bayesian Optimisation over Multiple Continuous and Categorical Inputs
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Bayesian Optimisation over Multiple Continuous and Categorical Inputs

children.title: Finite-Value Domain Geometry
children.top_down_role: Finite-valued variables distinguished by the geometry retained among their values.

children.title: Ordered Discrete Variable Geometry
children.top_down_role: Discrete values retaining metric or ordinal relations.

children.title: Integer-Valued Variables
children.top_down_role: Discrete numeric domains retaining meaningful spacing.

assumptions_latex: \(l,u\in\mathbb Z\) with \(l\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(D\) is a finite ordered metric space under the usual order and \(d(i,j)=|i-j|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded integer coordinates in a finite structured search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bounded integer-valued decision coordinate has feasible set \(D=\{l,l+1,\ldots,u\}\subseteq\mathbb Z\). It inherits the usual integer order and the metric \(d(i,j)=|i-j|\). Two feasible values are adjacent when \(|i-j|=1\), so order, adjacency, and magnitude differences are part of the domain structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded integer-valued decision coordinate ranges over consecutive integers and inherits their order, adjacency, and distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Valued Variables

children.title: Ordinal Variables
children.top_down_role: Finite domains retaining rank order without requiring metric spacing.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\) is finite with \(m\geq2\).
A strict total order \(c_1\prec\cdots\prec c_m\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rank map preserves order but does not determine numerical spacing between categories.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite categories with order but without intrinsic interval scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordinal variable takes values in a finite set \(C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\) equipped with a strict total order \(c_1\prec\cdots\prec c_m\). Its rank encoding \(r:C\to\{1,ldots,m\}\), defined by \(r(c_i)=i\), satisfies \(c_i\prec c_j\) if and only if \(r(c_i)<r(c_j)\). Only order is intrinsic: differences such as \(r(c_j)-r(c_i)\) do not represent equal physical intervals unless additional spacing information is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordinal variable has ranked categories, but rank differences have no intrinsic interval meaning without additional spacing information.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinal Variables

children.title: Metric-Preserving Discretization
children.top_down_role: Representations that preserve relevant distance structure for ordered values.

assumptions_latex: \((D,d_D)\) is a finite ordered metric space.
\(z_1<\cdots<z_m\) are real grid locations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\) preserves all pairwise distances exactly and therefore preserves nearest-neighbor relations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact isometric encoding of an ordered finite domain on a numerical grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A grid encoding \(\phi:D\to\mathbb R\), with \(\phi(c_i)=z_i\), is metric-preserving when \[d_D(c_i,c_j)=|z_i-z_j|\qquad\text{for all }i,j.\] Under this equality, \(\phi\) is an isometry from \((D,d_D)\) onto \(\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}\) with the Euclidean metric. For uniformly spaced integer levels, choosing \(z_i=l+i-1\) preserves the canonical distance \(d_D(c_i,c_j)=|i-j|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discretization is metric-preserving when its numerical grid reproduces every pairwise distance of the original ordered finite domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Preserving Discretization

children.title: Categorical Kernel Models
children.top_down_role: Direct similarity models for unordered assignments.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\prod_{j=1}^p C_j\) with each \(C_j\) finite.
\(\sigma^2>0\) and \(\theta_j\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on the unordered assignment space \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponentiated weighted mismatch kernel for unordered categorical assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[k(c,c')=\sigma^2\exp\!\left(-\sum_{j=1}^p\theta_j\mathbf 1\{c_j\neq c'_j\}\right).\] For coordinate \(j\), the factor equals \(1\) for matching levels and \(e^{-\theta_j}\) otherwise; its Gram matrix is \((1-e^{-\theta_j})I+e^{-\theta_j}\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\), which is positive semidefinite. The product across coordinates is therefore positive semidefinite. The kernel depends only on category matches and requires no artificial ordering of levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponentiating a weighted categorical mismatch count yields a valid covariance kernel without imposing an order on category labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Kernel Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mismatch kernel is relevant and the property role is appropriate, but no source supports the exact kernel or its positive-semidefiniteness claim. The Gram-matrix and product argument is proof text and should be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Categorical Hybrid Selection Interface
children.top_down_role: Learned category representations and coupled discrete-continuous selection mechanisms.

children.title: Categorical Embedding Models
children.top_down_role: Learned latent representations for categorical values.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite categorical set.
\(\phi:C\to\mathbb R^q\) is an embedding.
\(\kappa\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pullback \(k_\phi\) is a positive-semidefinite categorical kernel on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latent Euclidean representations inducing similarities between categorical levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each category \(c\in C\) a latent vector \(\phi(c)\in\mathbb R^q\) and define \[k_\phi(c,c')=\kappa\bigl(\phi(c),\phi(c')\bigr).\] For any \(c_1,\ldots,c_n\in C\) and \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), positive semidefiniteness of \(\kappa\) gives \(\sum_{i,j=1}^n a_i a_j k_\phi(c_i,c_j)\geq0\). Hence latent distances or inner products can parameterize categorical similarity while retaining a valid Gaussian-process covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed categories as latent vectors and pull back a valid Euclidean kernel to obtain a valid categorical covariance model.
knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Embedding Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pullback construction fits categorical embedding models and representation is an acceptable role, but no source is supplied. The quadratic-form argument is proof text and should not appear in the eventual knowledge statement; a source should also clarify whether the embedding is fixed or learned and what identifiability conventions apply.

children.title: Bandit–BO Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Search architectures coupling categorical arm selection with Bayesian optimization.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite set of categorical arms and \(X_c\) is the continuous domain for arm \(c\).
Each arm has a posterior acquisition function \(a_{t,c}:X_c\to\mathbb R\).
Each arm has count \(n_{t,c}\) and \(t\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns the best observed pair after the prescribed evaluation budget.

notation.meaning: Number of evaluations assigned to arm c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bandit selection across categories with Bayesian optimization within each selected category.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize by evaluating at least one point in every arm. At iteration \(t\), compute \(A_{t,c}=\sup_{x\in X_c}a_{t,c}(x)\) and select \[c_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c\in C}\left\{A_{t,c}+\gamma_t\sqrt{\frac{\log t}{n_{t,c}}}\right\}.\] Then choose \(x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X_{c_t}}a_{t,c_t}(x)\), observe the response, and update the posterior and count for \(c_t\). Stop at the evaluation budget and return the observed pair with the best feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bandit rule selects a category using acquisition value and arm uncertainty; Bayesian optimization then chooses the continuous point within that category.
knowledge_statements.title: Bandit–BO Hybrids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage category-then-continuous search fits the Bandit–BO Hybrids leaf and algorithm is the correct content kind. However, the particular UCB-style bonus added to the supremal within-arm acquisition is one of many possible hybrids and has no supporting citation.

children.title: Discrete–Continuous Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination between categorical choices and continuous candidate variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete–Continuous Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate acquisition maximization over one finite categorical block and one compact continuous block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an acquisition function \(a:C\times X\to\mathbb R\), initialize \((c^0,x^0)\in C\times X\). For \(t=0,1,\ldots\), choose \(c^{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c\in C}a(c,x^t)\), then choose \(x^{t+1}\in X\) satisfying \(a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})\geq \sup_{x\in X}a(c^{t+1},x)-\eta_t\). Stop when \(a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})-a(c^t,x^t)\leq\varepsilon\), or when a prescribed evaluation budget is exhausted, and return the best visited feasible pair. With exact block updates, the acquisition values are nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate categorical maximization with continuous acquisition optimization, stopping at small improvement or budget exhaustion and returning the best feasible pair visited.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact.
\(a(c,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous for every \(c\in C\).
\(\eta_t\geq 0\) is the continuous-block optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})\geq a(c^t,x^t)-\eta_t\), with monotonicity when \(\eta_t=0\).

children.title: Product-Space Surrogates

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-process representation on a finite-by-continuous mixed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite categorical set and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). A product-space Gaussian-process surrogate is specified by \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\) on \(C\times X\), where \[k((c,x),(c',x'))=k_C(c,c')k_X(x,x')+k_A(c,c')+k_B(x,x').\] Here every component kernel is positive semidefinite on its stated domain. Consequently \(k\) is positive semidefinite and models both type-specific effects and categorical–continuous interaction without imposing arithmetic meaning on category labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-domain Gaussian process combines valid categorical and continuous kernels, with an optional product term representing interactions between variable types.
assumptions_latex: \(k_C\) and \(k_A\) are positive-semidefinite kernels on \(C\).
\(k_X\) and \(k_B\) are positive-semidefinite kernels on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(C\times X\).

children.title: Mixed-Variable Acquisition Search
children.top_down_role: Inner optimizers coordinating discrete and continuous candidate decisions.

children.title: Alternating Acquisition Search
children.top_down_role: Candidate search that alternates across variable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Acquisition Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate search for acquisition maximization on a mixed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a:C\times X\to\mathbb R\) and initialize \((c^0,x^0)\in C\times X\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(c^{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c\in C}a(c,x^t)\) and then choose \(x^{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}a(c^{t+1},x)\). Define \(\Delta_C^{t+1}=\max_{c\in C}a(c,x^{t+1})-a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})\) and \(\Delta_X^{t+1}=\max_{x\in X}a(c^{t+1},x)-a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})\). Terminate when \(\Delta_C^{t+1}\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\Delta_X^{t+1}\leq\varepsilon\), or at a fixed iteration limit, and return the visited pair with largest acquisition value. Exact updates are ascent-preserving, but the returned point need not be a global maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the categorical and continuous blocks in turn. Exact updates do not decrease acquisition; checking both block gaps at the same iterate certifies approximate coordinatewise optimality but not global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, and \(X\) is nonempty and compact.
\(a(c,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous for every \(c\in C\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact updates satisfy \(a(c^{t+1},x^{t+1})\geq a(c^t,x^t)\); if both displayed gaps are at most \(\varepsilon\), the iterate is an \(\varepsilon\)-coordinatewise maximizer.

children.title: Hybrid Acquisition Search
children.top_down_role: Candidate search combining multiple optimizer families.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Acquisition Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global discrete proposals combined with local continuous acquisition optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(a:C\times X\to\mathbb R\), a proposal rule \(P\), and budget \(B\), initialize a finite pool \(S_0\subset C\times X\). At round \(t\), use \(P\) to generate categorical proposals \(D_t\subseteq C\), solve \(x_c\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}a(c,x)\) for each \(c\in D_t\), and add \((c,x_c)\) and any feasible mixed mutations to \(S_{t+1}\). Stop after \(B\) acquisition evaluations and return \(z^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{z\in S_T}a(z)\). The output is the best candidate explicitly examined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate global categorical proposals, optimize their continuous coordinates locally, optionally mutate mixed candidates, and return the best acquisition value examined within budget.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and \(X\) is a nonempty compact subset of \(\mathbb R^d\).
The proposal rule returns feasible categorical values.
Continuous subproblems attain their maxima or use declared approximations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(z^\star)=\max_{z\in S_T}a(z)\).

children.title: Mixed-Block Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of discrete and continuous acquisition-search blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Block Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate coordinatewise optimality condition for acquisition search over heterogeneous blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a product domain \(Z=Z_1\times\cdots\times Z_p\) and acquisition \(a:Z\to\mathbb R\), a feasible point \(z\in Z\) is \(\varepsilon\)-mixed-block coordinated when, for every block \(j\), \[a(z)\geq\sup_{u\in Z_j}a(z_1,\ldots,z_{j-1},u,z_{j+1},\ldots,z_p)-\varepsilon_j.\] Each \(Z_j\) may be finite, integer-valued, categorical, or continuous. This predicate certifies resistance to every permitted one-block deviation, but it does not certify joint or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is mixed-block coordinated when changing any single heterogeneous block can improve acquisition by at most that block’s tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_j\neq\varnothing\) for every block \(j\).
\(\varepsilon_j\geq 0\) for every block \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible one-block replacement improves \(a\) by more than \(\varepsilon_j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the direct heterogeneous-block form of approximate coordinatewise optimality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Numerical Encoding Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Artificial geometry and duplicate evaluations introduced by numerical encodings.

children.title: Rounding Distortion
children.top_down_role: Candidate displacement caused by mapping continuous proposals to discrete values.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relax-and-round acquisition search can exhibit a nonvanishing loss relative to the relaxed optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible discrete set be \(D=\{0,1\}\), let its relaxation be \(R=[0,1]\), and define \(a(z)=-(z-1/2)^2\). The relaxed maximizer is \(z_R=1/2\) with \(a(z_R)=0\), whereas every decoding \(q:R\to D\) satisfies \(a(q(z_R))=-1/4\). Hence \[a(z_R)-a(q(z_R))=1/4.\] Thus exact optimization of this smooth relaxed acquisition leaves a fixed loss after decoding, even though the decoded endpoint happens to maximize \(a\) over \(D\) in this example.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth relaxed acquisition can peak between feasible discrete values, producing a fixed loss after rounding relative to the relaxed optimum; this example does not claim that the rounded endpoint is suboptimal within the discrete set.
assumptions_latex: \(q:[0,1]\to\{0,1\}\) is any decoding map.

notation.meaning: Discrete feasible set and continuous relaxation.
Decoder from the relaxation to the discrete set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit elementary calculation establishes the relaxation-to-decoding loss
external source desirable for taxonomy placement

children.title: Encoding-Induced Geometry
children.top_down_role: Artificial similarity or distance relationships introduced by numerical encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Induced Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numeric category codes create arbitrary distances under stationary Euclidean kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{a,b,c\}\), encode its labels by \(e(a)=0\), \(e(b)=1\), and \(e(c)=M\), and apply the squared-exponential kernel \(k_e(u,v)=\exp(-(e(u)-e(v))^2/(2\ell^2))\). For fixed \(\ell>0\), \(k_e(a,b)=\exp(-1/(2\ell^2))\), while \(k_e(a,c)=\exp(-M^2/(2\ell^2))\to0\) as \(M\to\infty\). Because relabeling or rescaling the same categories changes these similarities, the resulting surrogate geometry is an artifact of the encoding rather than an invariant property of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying a Euclidean kernel to arbitrary category codes makes similarity depend on label numbering; rescaling one code can drive an unchanged category pair’s covariance to zero.
assumptions_latex: The categories have no intrinsic numeric metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{M\to\infty}k_e(a,c)=0\), although the abstract categorical domain is unchanged.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit kernel calculation establishes non-invariance under arbitrary category coding
external source desirable for modeling guidance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel calculation correctly demonstrates non-invariance under arbitrary numerical category encodings and the counterexample fits the leaf. A source is still required for the specialized modeling claim and taxonomy placement.

children.title: Duplicate Candidate Collisions
children.top_down_role: Distinct encoded proposals mapping to the same evaluable configuration.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Candidate Collisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Many relaxed optimizer outputs can decode to the same discrete candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer coordinate with feasible set \(D_m=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}\), define nearest-integer decoding \(q(x)=\min\{m,\max\{0,\lfloor x+1/2\rfloor\}\}\) on \([0,m]\). Every interior integer \(j\) has the preimage \(q^{-1}(j)=[j-1/2,j+1/2)\). Hence distinct relaxed proposals \(x_1\neq x_2\) can satisfy \(q(x_1)=q(x_2)\). A batch constructed in relaxed space may therefore contain fewer than its nominal number of distinct feasible candidates unless uniqueness is enforced after decoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearest-integer decoding is many-to-one, so distinct relaxed batch proposals can collapse to the same feasible evaluation and waste evaluation capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq 2\) is an integer.
Candidates are deduplicated only after, or not at all after, decoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|q(\{x_1,\ldots,x_B\})|\leq B\), with strict inequality whenever a decoding collision occurs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the many-to-one decoder and collision mechanism are explicit and directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The many-to-one decoding calculation is correct, including the stated preimages for interior integers, but no source supports its presentation as a batch Bayesian-optimization failure boundary.

children.title: Conditional Domain Hierarchy

children.title: Tree-Structured Configuration Spaces
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical domains organized by conditional branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Structured Configuration Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional configurations represented by rooted decision trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tree-structured configuration space consists of a rooted tree \(T=(V,E,r)\), a choice set \(A_v\) at each decision node, and a parameter domain \(X_v\) attached to each node. A feasible configuration selects a root-to-leaf path \(P\) by choosing one outgoing branch at each visited decision node and assigns \(x_v\in X_v\) only for \(v\in P\). Its active coordinate set is \(P\); coordinates attached to \(V\setminus P\) are inactive and do not belong to the configuration’s effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree-structured configuration chooses a root-to-leaf branch and assigns values only to parameters activated along that branch.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is rooted and acyclic.
Every nonleaf decision node has a nonempty set of outgoing choices.
Every attached parameter domain \(X_v\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Z=\bigcup_{P\in\mathcal P(T)}\prod_{v\in P}X_v\), with branch labels included where required.

notation.meaning: Parameter domain activated at node v.

review_flags: source locator concerns tree search and may not support conditional configuration semantics directly

children.title: Inactive-Variable Representation System

children.title: Masked-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Encodings that mark coordinates unavailable under the current branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Masked-Variable Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-width representation of conditionally active configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in\mathbb N\), let \(X_1,\ldots,X_d\) be nonempty coordinate domains, and choose filler symbols \(\bot_i\notin X_i\). A masked representation is a pair \((m,\tilde x)\), where \(m\in\{0,1\}^d\) and \(\tilde x_i\in X_i\cup\{\bot_i\}\), satisfying \(m_i=0\Longleftrightarrow\tilde x_i=\bot_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\). The represented configuration consists exactly of the indexed values \((i,\tilde x_i)\) for which \(m_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary mask records which coordinates are active, active positions contain values from their coordinate domains, and inactive positions contain designated filler symbols.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a positive integer.
Each \(X_i\) is nonempty.
The mask is consistent with the governing conditional branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{decode}(m,\tilde x)=\{(i,\tilde x_i):m_i=1\}\).

notation.meaning: Designated inactive filler symbol for coordinate i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the corrected mask-plus-value representation is internally well-defined

children.title: Inactive-Coordinate Semantics
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between unavailable coordinates and observed coordinate values.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Coordinate Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance condition ensuring inactive fillers have no modeled meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For masked inputs \(z=(m,x)\) and \(z'=(m',x')\), define \(z\sim z'\) when \(m=m'\) and \(x_i=x'_i\) for every \(i\) with \(m_i=1\). A response, surrogate mean, acquisition, or other configuration functional \(g\) has valid inactive-coordinate semantics precisely when \[z\sim z'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g(z)=g(z').\] Thus changing an inactive filler cannot change the represented configuration or any well-defined functional on it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model respects inactivity when changing filler values in masked-off coordinates leaves every configuration-dependent output unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is defined on a fixed-width masked representation space.
The activity mask determines which coordinates are semantically present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) factors through the quotient of masked representations by \(\sim\).

notation.meaning: Equality of masks and all active coordinate values.
Any functional intended to depend only on the represented configuration.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quotient invariance is the complete mathematical predicate for filler-independent inactive-coordinate semantics
