children.title: Cross-Branch Mask Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Comparability of masked configurations drawn from different conditional branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Branch Mask Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel compatibility across configurations having different active branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let \(X_i\) be a nonempty active-value domain, let \(F_i\) be an inactive-filler set disjoint from \(X_i\), and choose an anchor \(x_i^0\in X_i\). A masked input is \(z=(m,x)\), where \(m\in\{0,1\}^d\), \(x_i\in X_i\) when \(m_i=1\), and \(x_i\in F_i\) when \(m_i=0\). Define \(z\sim\bar z\) when their masks and active values agree. A cross-branch covariance kernel \(k\) is mask-compatible when it is positive semidefinite and \(z\sim\bar z\), \(z'\sim\bar z'\) imply \(k(z,z')=k(\bar z,\bar z')\). Let \(\rho_i(z)=x_i\) when \(m_i=1\) and \(\rho_i(z)=x_i^0\) when \(m_i=0\). A sufficient construction is \[k(z,z')=k_M(m,m')+\sum_{i=1}^d m_i m'_i k_i(\rho_i(z),\rho_i(z')),\] where \(k_M\) is positive semidefinite on \(\{0,1\}^d\) and each \(k_i\) is positive semidefinite on \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-branch kernel must ignore inactive fillers. A valid construction combines a mask kernel with gated coordinate kernels, using fixed active-domain anchors solely to keep every kernel evaluation well-defined.
assumptions_latex: \(k_M\) is positive semidefinite on \(\{0,1\}^d\).
Each \(k_i\) is positive semidefinite on the nonempty domain \(X_i\).
Each anchor \(x_i^0\) belongs to \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(k\) is positive semidefinite and constant on inactive-filler equivalence classes.

notation.meaning: Kernel on active values of coordinate i.
Map replacing an inactive filler by a fixed active-domain anchor.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: gated positive-semidefinite kernels and their sums remain positive semidefinite

children.title: Cross-Branch Information Sharing
children.top_down_role: Transfer of evidence between related conditional subspaces.

assumptions_latex: The conditional search domain is a rooted tree with branch labels and branch-specific coordinates.
A positive-semidefinite covariance kernel is defined on the union of all branch domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k(x,x')\neq 0\) may transfer posterior information between distinct branches whenever their shared or related structure receives nonzero covariance.

notation.meaning: A configuration lying on a conditional branch.
Covariance kernel on the conditional domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-mediated evidence transfer across distinct branches of a conditional configuration tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B}\{b\}\times\mathcal X_b\) be a conditional domain and let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\). For observations \(y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\), the posterior mean at \(x\) depends on an observation at \(x_i\) through the cross-covariance \(k(x,x_i)\). Hence an observation on branch \(b(x_i)\) informs a different branch \(b(x)\neq b(x_i)\) exactly when the corresponding posterior update coefficient is nonzero. Branch independence is obtained when \(k(x,x')=0\) for every pair on distinct branches; shared-variable, ancestor, or learned branch components permit nonzero transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian-process observation transfers information across branches precisely through nonzero cross-branch posterior covariance; a block-diagonal branch kernel prevents such transfer.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Branch Information Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited information-acquisition section does not specifically support cross-branch Gaussian-process covariance. Moreover, with multiple observations the coefficient of an individual observation is determined by the conditioned covariance or by the full product k_x^T(K+Sigma)^{-1}, not by the prior pairwise value k(x,x_i) alone. A GP or conditional-kernel source and a precise sequential or batch formulation are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite feasible subsets represented by incidence vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and a feasible family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^V\), a subset-selection space is \(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{sub}}=\mathcal F\). Its canonical binary representation maps each \(S\in\mathcal F\) to \(z=\mathbf 1_S\in\{0,1\}^n\), where \(z_i=1\) if and only if \(i\in S\). Thus the represented domain is \(\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:\operatorname{supp}(z)\in\mathcal F\}\). Cardinality, budget, matroid, or logical restrictions are encoded by the choice of \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset-selection space is a feasible family of subsets of a finite ground set, equivalently represented by their binary incidence vectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d\) and define \(k_\phi(x,x')=\kappa(\phi(x),\phi(x'))\) for a positive-semidefinite kernel \(\kappa\). children.title: Relaxation-Based Acquisition Optimization
children.top_down_role: Candidate selection through continuous or convexified representations.

assumptions_latex: The discrete feasible set \(\mathcal X\) is embedded in a tractable relaxation \(\mathcal R\).
An extended acquisition \(\widetilde\alpha\) is defined on \(\mathcal R\).
A rounding map \(P:\mathcal R\to\mathcal X\) is available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an acquisition function \(\alpha:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) on a discrete feasible set, choose a tractable relaxation \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathcal R\), an extension \(\widetilde\alpha:\mathcal R\to\mathbb R\), and a rounding map \(P:\mathcal R\to\mathcal X\). Initialize \(z_0\in\mathcal R\), apply a continuous optimizer to obtain \(\widehat z\) satisfying the chosen stopping rule for \(\max_{z\in\mathcal R}\widetilde\alpha(z)\), and return \(\widehat x=P(\widehat z)\). The returned point is feasible, but acquisition optimality requires a separate relation between \(\widetilde\alpha\), \(P\), and \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extend the acquisition to a continuous relaxation, optimize there, round the relaxed solution to feasibility, and report the resulting discrete point.

At iteration \(t\), use the prescribed neighborhood, enumeration, or branching rule to generate feasible unevaluated candidates \(C_t\subseteq\mathcal X\setminus S_t\), evaluate selected members, set \(S_{t+1}=S_t\cup C_t\), and update \(x_{t+1}^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in S_{t+1}}\alpha(x)\). Stop at the stated budget, exhaustion, or certified bound condition and return the incumbent.

children.title: Relaxation Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where relaxed candidates poorly represent feasible combinatorial objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies when optimizing a continuous relaxation reliably approximates discrete acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset R\), let \(\alpha:X\to\mathbb R\), let \(\widetilde\alpha:R\to\mathbb R\), and let \(r:R\to X\) be a rounding map. If \(|\widetilde\alpha(x)-\alpha(x)|\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(\widetilde\alpha(z)-\alpha(r(z))\leq\delta\) for every \(z\in R\), then any \(z^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in R}\widetilde\alpha(z)\) satisfies \[\max_{x\in X}\alpha(x)-\alpha(r(z^\star))\leq\varepsilon+\delta.\] Without uniform extension fidelity and controlled rounding loss, the discrete suboptimality can be arbitrarily large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed acquisition optimization is reliable only when the extension matches discrete values and rounding has bounded loss; otherwise its returned discrete point can be arbitrarily poor.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and both displayed maxima exist.
\(\varepsilon,\delta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in X}\alpha(x)-\alpha(r(z^\star))\leq\varepsilon+\delta\).

notation.meaning: Rounding map into the discrete domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound is mathematically correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no inspectable source supports either the bound or the claim of arbitrarily large suboptimality without the stated controls.

children.title: Combinatorial Solver Integration
children.top_down_role: Use of structured discrete solvers within acquisition optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Solver Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or approximate combinatorial maximization of a Bayesian-optimization acquisition function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite feasible family \(F\), an acquisition function \(\alpha_t:F\to\mathbb R\), and tolerance \(\eta_t\geq0\), pass an objective oracle for \(\alpha_t\) and the constraints defining \(F\) to a combinatorial solver. Return \(x_{t+1}\in F\) satisfying \[\alpha_t(x_{t+1})\geq\max_{x\in F}\alpha_t(x)-\eta_t.\] Evaluate the expensive objective at \(x_{t+1}\), update the Bayesian surrogate, and repeat until the evaluation budget or another declared stopping rule is reached. Exact integration corresponds to \(\eta_t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, a combinatorial solver approximately maximizes the acquisition over feasible objects, after which the selected expensive evaluation updates the surrogate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
The solver can query or represent \(\alpha_t\) on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned candidate is feasible and has acquisition suboptimality at most \(\eta_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the container, but the cited branch-and-bound section does not establish Bayesian-optimization integration, the acquisition-tolerance interface, or the iterative surrogate-update procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Known Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-feasibility regime with exactly evaluable deterministic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the search domain and let \(g_j:X\to\mathbb R\), for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), be deterministic functions known before expensive objective evaluation. The directly feasible set is \[F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\leq0\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] A constraint is known in this regime when membership in \(F\) can be decided exactly, without learning a statistical surrogate and without consuming the expensive objective-evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known constraints define an exactly testable feasible subset of the search domain and require no learned feasibility model.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
Each \(g_j(x)\) is available whenever feasibility is tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\) if and only if \(g_j(x)\leq0\) for all \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise and locally appropriate, but it has no inspectable citation supporting this direct-feasibility terminology and regime distinction.

children.title: Cheap Feasibility Screening
children.top_down_role: Low-cost feasibility checks applied during candidate selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Cheap Feasibility Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filters candidates using inexpensive exact constraints before costly acquisition or objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidates \(C_t\subseteq X\), known constraints \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\), and acquisition \(\alpha_t\), compute \(C_t^F=\{x\in C_t:g_j(x)\leq0\text{ for all }j\}\). If \(C_t^F\neq\varnothing\), return any \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C_t^F}\alpha_t(x)\); otherwise declare the candidate batch infeasible and regenerate or stop according to a declared rule. No expensive objective evaluation is performed for any point in \(C_t\setminus C_t^F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact cheap constraints remove infeasible candidates before acquisition maximization and prevent spending objective evaluations on rejected points.
assumptions_latex: Every \(g_j\) is cheaper to evaluate than the expensive objective.
Feasibility tests are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned \(x_{t+1}\) satisfies \(g_j(x_{t+1})\leq0\) for all \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The screening algorithm and feasibility conclusion are coherent, but no source supports the prescribed integration into acquisition maximization.

children.title: Candidate-Generation Integration
children.top_down_role: Incorporation of directly available restrictions into the candidate domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Generation Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enforces known constraints inside candidate construction rather than by post hoc rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a proposal mechanism \(Q_t\) on \(X\) and a known feasible set \(F\), construct a feasible proposal \(Q_t^F\) supported on \(F\), either by parameterizing candidates in \(F\) or by conditioning \(Q_t\) on feasibility. Generate \(C_t\) from \(Q_t^F\), maximize \(\alpha_t\) over \(C_t\), and return the maximizer. In the conditioning case, \[Q_t^F(A)=\frac{Q_t(A\cap F)}{Q_t(F)}\] for measurable \(A\subseteq X\), provided \(Q_t(F)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate generation is restricted to the known feasible set, so every proposed point satisfies the direct constraints by construction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is exactly testable.
For conditional generation, \(Q_t(F)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_t^F(F)=1\), hence every generated candidate is feasible almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-distribution formula is correct, but the algorithm lacks a source and does not state conditions ensuring that the generated candidate set is nonempty and has an acquisition maximizer.

children.title: Unknown Constraint Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Probabilistic models for constraints unavailable before evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Constraint Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior representation of feasibility when constraint functions must be learned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let feasibility mean \(c_j(x)\leq0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), where the functions are unknown and observed through data \(D_t^c\). A probabilistic surrogate induces \[p_t^F(x)=\mathbb P\!\left(c_1(x)\leq0,\ldots,c_m(x)\leq0\mid D_t^c\right).\] If the constraint posteriors are conditionally independent given \(D_t^c\), then \[p_t^F(x)=\prod_{j=1}^m\mathbb P\!\left(c_j(x)\leq0\mid D_t^c\right).\] Otherwise the joint posterior probability, rather than the product of marginals, is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint surrogates convert uncertain constraint values into posterior feasibility probabilities; multiplying marginal probabilities is valid only under conditional independence.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint observation has a specified likelihood.
The posterior distribution conditional on \(D_t^c\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is represented by the posterior joint probability \(p_t^F(x)\).

notation.meaning: Constraint data available at iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The posterior joint-feasibility representation and conditional-independence factorization are correct and fit the container, but no inspectable constrained-BO source is supplied.

children.title: Expensive Feasibility Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Constraint channels whose observation consumes substantial resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Expensive Feasibility Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint regime in which learning feasibility consumes a material evaluation resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each constraint channel \(j\), let \(K_j(x)>0\) denote the resource cost of obtaining an observation \(Y_j(x)\) whose likelihood depends on the unknown value \(c_j(x)\). Feasibility evaluation is expensive when these observations consume the finite optimization budget and cannot be treated as free screening. A query therefore consists of a permitted pair \((x,j)\), incurs cost \(K_j(x)\), produces \(Y_j(x)\), and updates the posterior distribution of \(c_j\) and consequently the feasibility probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expensive feasibility test consumes optimization budget, returns a noisy or exact constraint observation, and updates the learned feasibility model.
assumptions_latex: The total available evaluation budget is finite.
Each observation channel has a specified likelihood and positive cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint observations must be selected and budgeted as optimization actions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches an expensive learned-feasibility regime, but the resource-action characterization has no supporting citation.

children.title: Feasibility–Value Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Allocation between learning feasibility and improving objective value.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Value Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balances posterior objective improvement against the probability that a candidate is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(f(x)\) denote the posterior-random objective value at \(x\), let \(f_t^{\mathrm{best}}\) be a feasible incumbent, define \(I_t(x)=(f_t^{\mathrm{best}}-f(x))_+\), and let \(F(x)\) be the feasibility event. The constrained expected improvement is \[\operatorname{CEI}_t(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[I_t(x)\mathbf 1_{F(x)}\mid D_t\right].\] If \(I_t(x)\) and \(F(x)\) are conditionally independent given \(D_t\), then \[\operatorname{CEI}_t(x)=\operatorname{EI}_t(x)p_t^F(x),\] where \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=\mathbb E[I_t(x)\mid D_t]\) and \(p_t^F(x)=\mathbb P(F(x)\mid D_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained expected improvement is the posterior expectation of improvement obtained on feasible outcomes. Under conditional independence, it equals expected improvement multiplied by posterior feasibility probability.
assumptions_latex: A feasible incumbent \(f_t^{\mathrm{best}}\) exists.
The posterior expectation \(\mathbb E[I_t(x)\mid D_t]\) is finite.
The factorization requires conditional independence of \(I_t(x)\) and \(F(x)\) given \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under conditional independence, \(\operatorname{CEI}_t(x)=\operatorname{EI}_t(x)p_t^F(x)\).

children.title: Constraint Observation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Objective and constraint channels observed jointly or separately.

children.title: Coupled Constraint Observation
children.top_down_role: Objective and constraint outcomes obtained from the same evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Constraint Observation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observation protocol where objective and constraint channels are returned together.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the response channels be the objective \(f\) and constraints \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\). Observation is coupled when every admissible query is a location \(x\in X\) and returns the complete response vector \[Y(x)=(Y_f(x),Y_{c_1}(x),\ldots,Y_{c_m}(x)).\] The decision maker may choose \(x\) but cannot request an individual channel separately. Consequently, after \(n\) queries all objective and constraint datasets contain observations at the same queried locations, although their noise models may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled query evaluates the objective and every constraint at one location; individual response channels cannot be scheduled separately.
assumptions_latex: All response channels are available at every admissible \(x\).
A query returns the complete channel vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective and constraint observations share the same queried design locations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and fits the coupled-observation leaf, but no inspectable source supports the complete-vector convention used here.

children.title: Decoupled Constraint Observation
children.top_down_role: Constraint channels evaluable separately from the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Decoupled Constraint Observation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observation protocol permitting separate scheduling of objective and constraint channels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the search domain, let channel \(0\) represent the objective, and let channels \(1,\ldots,m\) represent the constraints. Observation is decoupled when an admissible action is a pair \((x,k)\in X\times\{0,\ldots,m\}\) that returns only \(Y_k(x)\) and incurs channel-specific cost \(K_k(x)>0\). The admissible action set may restrict which channels are observable at each location. Because channels can be selected separately, their datasets may contain different numbers of observations and different design locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoupled action selects a location and one response channel, allowing objective and constraint channels to have distinct costs, sample counts, and design locations.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
At least one channel can be queried without querying every other channel.
Each permitted channel action has a specified positive cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Response-channel datasets need not share design locations or sample sizes.

notation.meaning: Observation from channel k at x.

children.title: Channel-Scheduling Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Allocation across separately observable objective and constraint channels.

knowledge_statements.title: Channel-Scheduling Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware scheduling of decoupled objective and constraint observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every permitted action \((x,k)\), compute a nonnegative posterior utility \(U_t(x,k)\) measuring expected decision improvement from observing channel \(k\), and let \(K_k(x)>0\) be its cost. Select \[(x_{t+1},k_{t+1})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(x,k)}\frac{U_t(x,k)}{K_k(x)},\] observe \(Y_{k_{t+1}}(x_{t+1})\), update that channel's posterior and any dependent joint model, and repeat while the remaining budget covers the selected action. The utility must account for both objective-value learning and feasible-set learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decoupled channels are scheduled by cost-adjusted expected utility, balancing objective learning, feasibility learning, and unequal observation costs.
assumptions_latex: The admissible action set is nonempty.
Utilities and positive channel costs are available for all admissible actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each step selects an admissible channel-location pair maximizing declared utility per unit cost.

notation.meaning: Posterior utility of a channel action.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Utility-per-cost maximization is a particular scheduling heuristic, not a generic consequence of decoupling. A source is needed for this exact rule, and maximization should be restricted to actions affordable under the remaining budget.

children.title: Feasibility-Safety Search Calculus
children.top_down_role: Search prioritizing feasible discovery or evaluation safety.

children.title: Feasibility-First Search
children.top_down_role: Search prioritizing discovery of admissible candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-First Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-phase constrained search that first discovers feasibility and then optimizes value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_t^F(x)\) be posterior feasibility probability and let \(S_t\) be the set of observed feasible points. While \(S_t=\varnothing\), select \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}p_t^F(x),\] evaluate the required constraint channels, and update their surrogates. Once \(S_t\neq\varnothing\), define a feasible incumbent and select subsequent points by a declared constrained acquisition, such as \(\mathbb E[I_t(x)\mathbf 1_{F(x)}\mid D_t]\). Stop when the evaluation budget is exhausted or another declared criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before any feasible point is known, search maximizes feasibility probability; after feasibility is observed, it switches to a value-sensitive constrained acquisition.
assumptions_latex: Posterior feasibility probabilities are defined on \(X\).
The constraint channels needed to determine observed feasibility can be queried.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search prioritizes feasibility until \(S_t\neq\varnothing\), then incorporates objective improvement.

notation.meaning: Improvement relative to the feasible incumbent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-phase algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports this precise feasibility-first policy, and existence or approximate attainment of the feasibility-probability maximizer is not specified.

children.title: Safe Search
children.top_down_role: Search restricted to evaluations satisfying safety requirements.

assumptions_latex: A compact design space \(\mathcal X\) and unknown objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are given.
Unknown safety constraints \(g_j(x)\le 0\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\), have posterior means \(\mu_{j,t}\) and standard deviations \(\sigma_{j,t}\).
A nonempty certified-safe seed set \(S_0\subseteq\mathcal X\) and confidence multipliers \(\beta_t>0\) are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every queried point belongs to the current conservative safe set.

notation.meaning: Conservatively certified safe set after stage t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical posterior-confidence formulation of safe Bayesian search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior-confidence safe search with pointwise inequality constraints and an initially certified seed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(S_0\). After observations through stage \(t\), form the conservative safe set \[S_t=\left\{x\in\mathcal X:\mu_{j,t}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{j,t}(x)\le 0\ \text{for every }j\right\}.\] Choose \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in S_t}a_t(x)\), observe the objective and constraints at \(x_{t+1}\), update their posteriors, and repeat until a prescribed evaluation budget or stopping rule is met. Output the best observed feasible point. On any event where all simultaneous upper confidence bounds dominate the true constraints, every evaluation selected by this rule is safe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict every Bayesian-optimization query to points whose constraint upper confidence bounds certify safety, starting from a known safe seed.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Safe Search, but no inspectable citation supports the confidence-bound safety guarantee. The displayed definition of S_t also does not explain how the certified seed S_0 is retained when posterior bounds would exclude it.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe Gaussian-process optimization over a finite design space, initialized by evaluating a designated safe point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite design space X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}, an initially empty Gaussian process, an initially safe index i, an objective f, a safety threshold y_{\max}, a confidence scalar \beta, and an iteration limit k_{\max}, first observe f(x_i). At each iteration, update the Gaussian-process confidence bounds (l_j,u_j), construct the SafeOpt safe, potential-minimizer, and expander sets, select a new query from the eligible points, and observe its objective value. Stop after k_{\max} iterations or when no query is available. Finally set S=\{j:u_j\le y_{\max}\}; if S\ne\varnothing, return \left(\min_{j\in S}u_j,\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in S}u_j\right), and otherwise return (\mathrm{NaN},0).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SafeOpt begins by evaluating a designated safe point in a finite design space. It repeatedly updates Gaussian-process confidence intervals, constructs safe, potential-minimizer, and expander sets, and evaluates a selected eligible point. It stops at the iteration limit or when no query is available, then returns the smallest certified-safe upper bound and its design index, or (NaN, 0) if no point is certified safe.
assumptions_latex: X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\text{ is finite}
\mathrm{GP}\text{ is initially empty}
i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ indexes a designated initially safe point}
\beta\ge 0
k_{\max}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}
\text{The Gaussian process supports observation, prediction, and confidence-bound updates}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=\{j:u_j\le y_{\max}\},\qquad S\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow (u_{\mathrm{best}},i_{\mathrm{best}})=\left(\min_{j\in S}u_j,\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in S}u_j\right),\qquad S=\varnothing\Rightarrow (\mathrm{NaN},0).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain SafeOpt Algorithm

children.title: Feasible-Set Expansion
children.top_down_role: Progressive enlargement of regions considered admissible for evaluation.

assumptions_latex: The assumptions and confidence event defining a conservative safe set \(S_t\) hold.
A reachability relation \(R_t(x,z)\) certifies that evaluating safe point \(x\) can establish safety of candidate \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified region expands monotonically: \(S_t\subseteq S_{t+1}\).

notation.meaning: Certified safe set at stage t
Potentially certifiable points reachable through x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract expander-set formulation used by safe Bayesian optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract safe-set expansion; the reachability certificate may arise from Lipschitz or posterior confidence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(x\in S_t\), define its expansion set by \[E_t(x)=\{z\in\mathcal X\setminus S_t:R_t(x,z)\}.\] Let \(G_t=\{x\in S_t:E_t(x)\ne\varnothing\}\). If \(G_t\ne\varnothing\), select an expander \(x_{t+1}\in G_t\) maximizing a prescribed uncertainty or expansion score, evaluate it, and update the constraint posterior. Define \(S_{t+1}\) as \(S_t\) together with every newly certified point; hence \(S_t\subseteq S_{t+1}\). If \(G_t=\varnothing\), stop expansion or switch to safe objective optimization. Output the final certified set and the best feasible observation in it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate uncertain safe boundary points that can certify additional locations, retaining all previously certified points so the safe set grows monotonically.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set Expansion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Feasible-Set Expansion, but the abstract relation R_t is not defined strongly enough to establish that newly added points are safe. An authoritative source for the intended Lipschitz or posterior-confidence expansion variant is required.

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Constrained search organized through surrogate-assisted Lagrangian merit families.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X} f(x)\) subject to \(g_j(x)\le0\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
Surrogate posteriors are available for the objective and constraints.
Penalty parameters \(\rho_k>0\) and multipliers \(\lambda_{j,k}\ge0\) are initialized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained problem is searched through sequential surrogate optimization of augmented-Lagrangian merit functions.

notation.meaning: Augmented-Lagrangian merit function at outer iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard inequality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian surrogate-search template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-constrained surrogate search using a squared-hinge augmented Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), define \[L_k(x)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_{j,k}g_j(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\sum_{j=1}^m[g_j(x)]_+^2.\] Construct the posterior distribution of \(L_k(x)\) induced by the objective and constraint surrogates, choose one or more evaluations by maximizing a scalar Bayesian-optimization acquisition for minimizing \(L_k\), and update all observed surrogates. For a selected incumbent \(x_k\), update \(\lambda_{j,k+1}=[\lambda_{j,k}+\rho_k g_j(x_k)]_+\); increase \(\rho_k\) when constraint violation fails to decrease adequately. Stop at the evaluation budget and return the best observed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine objective and violations into an augmented-Lagrangian merit function, optimize its surrogate acquisition, and update multipliers and penalties from observed violations.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Bayesian Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the container, but the stated squared-hinge merit combined with the linear multiplier term is not identified as a standard augmented-Lagrangian variant and may reward strictly feasible negative constraints. A source must establish the exact merit and multiplier/penalty updates.

children.title: Multiobjective Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian search over vector-valued outcomes and Pareto structure.

children.title: Scalarization-Based Search
children.top_down_role: Reduction to families of scalar search problems.

assumptions_latex: An unknown vector objective \(F=(f_1,\ldots,f_q):\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^q\) is minimized.
A family of scalarizations \(s_\theta:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) is monotone in every objective component.
A distribution \(\pi\) over scalarization parameters is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated scalar Bayesian searches generate candidates targeted to different supported or preference-weighted Pareto tradeoffs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical random-scalarization reduction for multiobjective Bayesian optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random monotone scalarizations for minimization of finitely many objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), draw or select \(\theta_t\) from \(\pi\), define \(h_{\theta_t}(x)=s_{\theta_t}(F(x))\), and derive its posterior from the joint surrogate for \(F\). Choose \[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x;h_{\theta_t}),\] where \(a_t\) is any valid scalar Bayesian-optimization acquisition for minimizing \(h_{\theta_t}\). Evaluate all components of \(F(x_{t+1})\), update the surrogate, and repeat to the evaluation budget. Return the nondominated subset of observed outcomes. Monotonicity ensures that every global minimizer of a strictly increasing scalarization is weakly Pareto optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a monotone scalarization, run a scalar Bayesian-optimization step, and return the nondominated outcomes collected across tradeoff parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalarization-Based Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Scalarization-Based Search, and the strict-monotonicity Pareto statement is plausible, but no citation supports the random-scalarization procedure or the claimed range of targeted tradeoffs.

children.title: Hypervolume-Based Search
children.top_down_role: Policies driven by changes in dominated outcome-space volume.

assumptions_latex: A finite nondominated outcome set \(P_t\subset\mathbb R^q\) is maintained for a minimization problem.
A reference point \(r\in\mathbb R^q\) is dominated by every relevant Pareto outcome.
The posterior predictive random outcome at design \(x\) is \(Y(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next query maximizes expected enlargement of the dominated hypervolume.

notation.meaning: Dominated hypervolume relative to reference point r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard expected hypervolume improvement acquisition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected hypervolume improvement for finite nondominated observations in a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the hypervolume improvement of a candidate outcome \(y\) by \[I_{\mathrm{HV}}(y;P_t)=\operatorname{HV}_r(P_t\cup\{y\})-\operatorname{HV}_r(P_t)\ge0.\] Its Bayesian acquisition is \[\alpha_t(x)=\mathbb E_t[I_{\mathrm{HV}}(Y(x);P_t)].\] Select \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_t(x)\), evaluate the vector objective, update the surrogate and nondominated set, and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted. The output is the final observed nondominated set. The reference point and objective orientation must remain fixed when comparing hypervolume gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the design with greatest posterior expected increase in dominated objective-space volume relative to a fixed reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: Hypervolume-Based Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and formulas match expected-hypervolume-improvement search for minimization, but the record supplies no inspectable authoritative citation for EHVI or its reference-point convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominated hypervolume and expected hypervolume improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypervolume utility for posterior multiobjective optimization relative to an inferior reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given available objective outcomes and a reference point \(r\), the hypervolume or \(\mathcal S\)-metric is the volume of the outcome-space region dominated by those outcomes and bounded below by \(r\). Exact observations determine this region directly; with noisy observations, statistical lower bounds on objective values can define a conservative estimated region. The expected one-step marginal increase in hypervolume is expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI). The reference point prevents the measured dominated region from extending without bound. Hypervolume is positive only when the bounded dominated region has positive measure. EHVI computation becomes substantially more costly as the number of objectives grows because the region must be decomposed and integrated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypervolume measures the outcome-space volume dominated by available outcomes relative to an inferior reference point. Noisy outcomes may be replaced by statistical lower bounds. EHVI is the expected one-step gain in hypervolume, and computing it becomes harder as the number of objectives increases.
assumptions_latex: \text{Objectives use the maximization convention.}
r\text{ is bounded below the outcomes used to form the dominated region.}
\text{Strict positivity additionally requires the dominated region to have positive measure.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{EHVI}(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[HV(\mathcal D\cup\{(x,Y(x))\};r)-HV(\mathcal D;r)\mid\mathcal D\right],\qquad HV(\mathcal D;r)\ge0.

source_evidence.locator: Extensions and Related Settings / 11.7. Multiobjective Optimization / Definition 11.7-extra-4

source_refs.locator: Extensions and Related Settings / 11.7. Multiobjective Optimization / Definition 11.7-extra-4

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated hypervolume and expected hypervolume improvement

source_witnesses.locator: Extensions and Related Settings / 11.7. Multiobjective Optimization / Definition 11.7-extra-4

children.title: Pareto Information Target Pair
children.top_down_role: Information-directed search for Pareto structure.

children.title: Pareto-Set Information Search
children.top_down_role: Information-directed search targeting Pareto-optimal decisions.

assumptions_latex: A posterior is maintained over an unknown vector objective \(F:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^q\).
The random Pareto set \(X^\star\subseteq\mathcal X\) is measurable under that posterior.
A prospective observation is the random variable \(Y_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each query maximizes posterior mutual information about the design-space Pareto set.

notation.meaning: Posterior-random Pareto set in design space
Prospective noisy vector observation at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: entropy-search criterion with the Pareto set as information target
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-based search targeting Pareto-optimal input locations rather than their objective images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), assign each candidate \(x\in\mathcal X\) the acquisition \[\alpha_t(x)=I_t(Y_x;X^\star)=H_t(X^\star)-\mathbb E_t[H_t(X^\star\mid Y_x)].\] Choose \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_t(x)\), observe the objective vector, and update the posterior. For continuous \(\mathcal X\), the entropy and mutual information are computed using a declared finite, point-process, or other measurable representation of \(X^\star\). Stop at the evaluation budget and output an estimator of the Pareto set, such as its posterior mode, inclusion-probability level set, or nondominated observed designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Query where the prospective observation is expected to reduce uncertainty most about which design points are Pareto optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Set Information Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Pareto-Set Information Search, but entropy of a continuous random set is not defined merely by measurability. A source must support the selected representation, entropy measure, acquisition, and output estimator.

children.title: Pareto-Frontier Information Search
children.top_down_role: Information-directed search targeting attainable nondominated outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A posterior is maintained over an unknown vector objective \(F:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^q\).
The random Pareto frontier \(Z^\star=F(X^\star)\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) has a specified measurable representation.
A prospective observation is the random variable \(Y_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each query maximizes posterior mutual information about the objective-space Pareto frontier.

notation.meaning: Posterior-random Pareto frontier in objective space
Prospective noisy vector observation at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: entropy-search criterion with the Pareto frontier as information target
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-based search targeting nondominated objective values rather than their generating designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), define \[\alpha_t(x)=I_t(Y_x;Z^\star)=H_t(Z^\star)-\mathbb E_t[H_t(Z^\star\mid Y_x)].\] Select \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_t(x)\), observe its objective vector, and update the posterior. Entropy is evaluated only after fixing a representation of the random frontier, such as an ordered finite approximation, attainment function, or discretized nondominated set. Continue to the evaluation budget and output a posterior frontier estimator together with the observed nondominated outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose observations expected to reduce uncertainty most about the nondominated objective values forming the Pareto frontier.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Frontier Information Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Pareto-Frontier Information Search, but the entropy expression depends on a precisely defined frontier representation and base measure. No source supports the listed alternatives or the resulting acquisition.

children.title: Representation-Sensitive Information Targets
children.top_down_role: Differences induced by targeting decision-space or objective-space Pareto structure.

assumptions_latex: A random Pareto object \(T\) is encoded by a measurable representation \(R(T)\).
Information acquisition uses entropy or mutual information involving \(R(T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Information values are invariant under bijective measurable recodings, but may change under lossy or discretization-dependent representations.

notation.meaning: Chosen measurable encoding of the target

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mutual-information invariance under measurable bijections and loss under noninvertible encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of Pareto information acquisitions on target encoding, discretization, and loss of identity information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a prospective observation. If \(R_1(T)=\phi(R_2(T))\) almost surely for a measurable bijection \(\phi\) with measurable inverse, then \[I(Y;R_1(T))=I(Y;R_2(T)).\] If instead \(R_1(T)=\psi(R_2(T))\) for a noninvertible measurable map \(\psi\), then the data-processing inequality gives \[I(Y;R_1(T))\le I(Y;R_2(T)).\] Consequently, a Pareto-set encoding that discards design identities, or a frontier discretization that merges distinct outcomes, can change acquisition rankings. Any information-search specification must therefore declare the target representation and approximation resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information search is unchanged by invertible target recodings, but lossy encodings or discretizations can reduce information and alter query rankings.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Sensitive Information Targets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, and mutual-information invariance and data processing are standard. However, no citation is supplied, and the further claim about altered acquisition rankings is not implied by the displayed pointwise inequality alone without an example or additional conditions.

children.title: Preference-Guided Multiobjective Search
children.top_down_role: Pareto search focused by known or interactively learned decision-maker preferences.

assumptions_latex: An unknown vector objective \(F:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^q\) is minimized.
Preference data \(D_t^{\mathrm{pref}}\) determine a posterior \(p_t(\theta)\) over utility parameters.
For every \(\theta\), utility \(u_\theta\) is monotone with respect to Pareto improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search concentrates evaluations on outcomes having high posterior decision value under the modeled preferences.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Bayesian utility-integrated acquisition for preference-guided multiobjective search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian multiobjective search with known or interactively inferred monotone preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), update \(p_t(\theta)=p(\theta\mid D_t^{\mathrm{pref}})\). Define a preference-integrated acquisition \[\alpha_t(x)=\mathbb E_{\theta\sim p_t}\!\left[a_t\bigl(x;u_\theta\circ F\bigr)\right],\] where \(a_t\) is a scalar Bayesian-optimization acquisition under the objective posterior. Select \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_t(x)\), observe \(F(x_{t+1})\), and optionally request a comparison or choice that updates \(D_t^{\mathrm{pref}}\). Continue until the evaluation or interaction budget is exhausted. Return observed nondominated alternatives ranked by posterior expected utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrate a scalar acquisition over known or learned preferences, alternating objective evaluations with optional preference queries.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Guided Multiobjective Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Preference-Guided Multiobjective Search, but utility versus loss orientation is not fixed for minimization, and averaging an arbitrary scalar acquisition over preference parameters requires methodological support. No inspectable citation is given.

children.title: Cross-Task Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization across related tasks, environments, or historical studies.

children.title: Finite Task Collections
children.top_down_role: Joint search across an indexed set of related tasks.

assumptions_latex: The task index set is finite: \(\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,K\}\).
Each task has an unknown objective \(f_k:\mathcal X_k\to\mathbb R\).
A joint prior specifies cross-task dependence among the objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite task collection is represented as one joint Bayesian optimization problem on an augmented input domain.

notation.meaning: Joint objective on the augmented domain

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard augmented-domain representation of finite multitask Gaussian-process optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite indexed tasks represented by a joint surrogate on a disjoint augmented domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the augmented domain and objective by \[\widetilde{\mathcal X}=\bigcup_{k=1}^K(\mathcal X_k\times\{k\}),\qquad \widetilde f(x,k)=f_k(x).\] A multitask surrogate is a joint prior on \(\widetilde f\); for example, when domains agree, a separable covariance has the form \[\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde f(x,k),\widetilde f(x',\ell))=k_X(x,x')B_{k\ell},\] where \(B\) is positive semidefinite. A query is a pair \((x,k)\), possibly carrying a task-dependent cost, and its observation updates every correlated task. Thus task and design selection can be performed jointly by an acquisition on \(\widetilde{\mathcal X}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent finitely many related objectives as one function on design-task pairs, using cross-task covariance so each observation can inform correlated tasks.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Task Collections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind correctly fits Finite Task Collections, and the augmented-domain and separable-covariance formulas are standard, but no specific multitask Bayesian-optimization source is cited.

children.title: Continuous Context Spaces
children.top_down_role: Search conditioned on continuously varying environments.

assumptions_latex: The context space \(\mathcal C\) and design space \(\mathcal X\) are measurable, with \(\mathcal C\) continuous.
The response is an unknown function \(f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\).
A joint surrogate models dependence across both design and context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contextual optimization is Bayesian optimization on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal C\), with decisions conditioned on the realized context.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard contextual Bayesian-optimization formulation on a product domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous observed contexts with a design decision optimized conditionally for each context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each context \(c\in\mathcal C\), the target decision is \[x^\star(c)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x,c).\] Place a joint surrogate on \(f\) over \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal C\), such as a Gaussian process with covariance \(k((x,c),(x',c'))\). When context \(c_t\) is externally revealed, choose \[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x,c_t),\] observe the noisy response at \((x_t,c_t)\), and update the joint posterior. Correlation across nearby contexts transfers information while preserving a context-specific optimizer. Performance must be assessed under a declared context sequence or distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model response jointly over designs and continuous contexts, then optimize the design conditionally whenever a context is observed.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Context Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Continuous Context Spaces, but the externally revealed-context protocol and conditional acquisition require a contextual Bayesian-optimization citation. The local inventory contains no supporting source.

children.title: Historical Transfer Initialization
children.top_down_role: Reuse of observations, models, or incumbents from previous searches.

children.title: Warm-Start Initialization
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior observations, incumbents, or model state at search initialization.

assumptions_latex: Historical data \(D_H\) and a target task with objective \(f_T:\mathcal X_T\to\mathbb R\) are given.
A transfer model specifies how historical observations inform the target surrogate.
An initial target-evaluation budget \(n_0\ge0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target search begins from a posterior conditioned on selected historical data and any initial target evaluations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic historical-posterior warm-start procedure for transfer Bayesian optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Historical-data warm start with explicit source selection and optional initial target evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a historical subset \(D_H^{\mathrm{sel}}\subseteq D_H\) using a declared relevance rule. Fit the transfer model and, if \(n_0>0\), choose an initial target design \(X_T^0\subseteq\mathcal X_T\) with \(|X_T^0|=n_0\) and collect \(D_T^0\). Initialize \[p_0(f_T)=p(f_T\mid D_H^{\mathrm{sel}},D_T^0).\] For \(t\ge0\), maximize a target-task acquisition under the current posterior, evaluate the chosen target point, and update the posterior. Stop at the target budget and return the best observed target point. The selected historical subset, transfer hyperparameters, and initial target design are part of the algorithm specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condition the target surrogate on selected historical studies and optional initial target evaluations before beginning ordinary target-task Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Warm-Start Initialization, but the transfer model and relevance rule are left abstract, so the historical-conditioning procedure and safeguards against negative transfer cannot be evaluated without a specific source.

children.title: Historical-Study Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of evidence from completed related studies.

knowledge_statements.title: Historical-Study Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-surrogate transfer from completed source studies to a new target study.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let task index \(0\) denote the target and let \(S\) index completed historical studies, with data \(D_s=\{(x_{si},y_{si})\}_{i=1}^{n_s}\). Historical-study transfer is Bayesian optimization in which a joint prior \(p(f_0,(f_s)_{s\in S})\) couples the latent objectives and the target posterior is \[p(f_0\mid D_0,(D_s)_{s\in S}).\] At target iteration \(t\), the next point satisfies \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\), where \(a_t\) is computed from this transferred posterior rather than from \(D_0\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Historical-study transfer conditions a target-task surrogate on both target observations and completed related studies, then selects target evaluations using the resulting posterior acquisition function.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a common measurable design space.
The joint prior supplies well-defined cross-task dependence.
Historical and target likelihoods are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(f_0\mid D_0,(D_s)_{s\in S})\) determines the transferred target acquisition.

notation.meaning: target acquisition function at iteration t

review_flags: Specialized cross-task Bayesian-optimization source and exact locator are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the historical-transfer leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation supports the joint-prior and transferred-posterior formulation.

children.title: Source-Study Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of historical studies considered relevant to the current search.

knowledge_statements.title: Source-Study Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation-based selection of historical studies before target optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidate sources \(S\), initial target data \(D_0\), validation folds \(V_1,\ldots,V_K\), and penalty \(\lambda\geq0\), initialize \(U=\varnothing\). For each admissible subset \(A\subseteq S\), fit the transfer model using sources in \(A\) and score \[J(A)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\log p_A(V_k\mid D_0\setminus V_k)-\lambda c(A).\] After all admissible subsets are scored, stop and output \(U\in\arg\max_A J(A)\). Only data from sources in \(U\) are used to initialize the target posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select historical studies by maximizing held-out target predictive fit minus a source-use penalty, and transfer only the maximizing subset.
assumptions_latex: \(D_0\) contains data that can be partitioned into validation folds.
\(p_A\) is a proper predictive distribution for every admissible \(A\).
\(c(A)\geq0\) is a specified complexity or access cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\in\arg\max_{A\subseteq S}J(A)\).
review_flags: The node admits multiple source-selection criteria; a canonical supporting reference is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits source-study selection, but penalized target-fold validation is one particular selection procedure and requires a direct source with an exact locator.

children.title: Target-Task Transfer
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary tasks used to accelerate a designated target search.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Task Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-task information is transferred solely to improve a designated target search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the designated target objective and let \((f_s)_{s\in S}\) be auxiliary objectives. Target-task transfer is a sequential policy \(\pi\) whose target decision at time \(t\) may depend on \(D_0^t\) and auxiliary data \((D_s)_{s\in S}\), but whose output is a target recommendation \(\widehat x_T\in\mathcal X\). Its performance is assessed only through a target loss, such as simple regret \(r_T=f_0(x_0^*)-f_0(\widehat x_T)\), where \(x_0^*\in\arg\max_x f_0(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target-task transfer policy uses auxiliary-task data to choose evaluations, but returns and evaluates a recommendation only for the designated target objective.
assumptions_latex: All tasks have observations mapped to a common target design space \(\mathcal X\).
A joint or conditional model relates auxiliary tasks to the target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T\) is judged by target loss \(r_T\), not by auxiliary-task performance.
review_flags: A direct source for this formal target-centric definition is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The target-centric definition matches the container, but no source establishes this formal policy-and-target-loss characterization.

children.title: Transfer Mismatch Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by misleading cross-task relations.

children.title: Negative Transfer
children.top_down_role: Performance degradation caused by reuse of misleading source information.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer fails when auxiliary information worsens target performance relative to target-only optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For target loss \(L_0\), a transfer policy \(\pi_{\mathrm{tr}}\) exhibits negative transfer relative to a target-only policy \(\pi_0\) when \[\mathbb E[L_0(\pi_{\mathrm{tr}})]>\mathbb E[L_0(\pi_0)]\] under the same target budget. A sharp two-point mechanism is \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), \(f_0(a)=1\), \(f_0(b)=0\), and source objective \(f_1(a)=0\), \(f_1(b)=1\): a policy that copies the source maximizer returns \(b\) with simple regret \(1\). The failed assumption is positive source-target alignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative transfer occurs when a transfer policy has greater expected target loss than a target-only policy under the same budget; anti-aligned tasks provide a two-point example.
assumptions_latex: Both policies receive the same target-evaluation budget.
Expectations use the same target problem distribution and observation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[L_0(\pi_{\mathrm{tr}})]>\mathbb E[L_0(\pi_0)]\).
review_flags: The performance comparison is standard, but a transfer-learning source with an exact locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and equal-budget loss comparison are appropriate, but the definition and embedded anti-alignment example lack a cited transfer-learning source.

children.title: Task Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Differences between source and target tasks that invalidate assumed relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Task Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform discrepancy condition for identifying a source objective incompatible with the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_s:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be target and source objectives on a common domain, and fix an admissible discrepancy \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Source task \(s\) is \(\varepsilon\)-mismatched to the target precisely when \[d_\infty(f_s,f_0):=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|f_s(x)-f_0(x)|>\varepsilon.\] If objectives are identifiable only up to an additive constant, replace this distance by \(\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|f_s(x)+c-f_0(x)|\). The chosen invariance convention must be fixed before testing mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source is mismatched when its uniform discrepancy from the target exceeds a declared tolerance, optionally after removing an irrelevant additive offset.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0\) and \(f_s\) are bounded on \(\mathcal X\).
The tolerance \(\varepsilon\) and any invariance convention are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\) is mismatched if and only if \(d_\infty(f_s,f_0)>\varepsilon\).
review_flags: Task mismatch has several inequivalent metrics; this uniform version needs path-specific source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally precise, but task mismatch is not canonically equivalent to uniform objective discrepancy; this path-specific metric and its additive-shift variant require direct support.

children.title: Transfer-Robustness Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to identify unreliable cross-task information sharing.

knowledge_statements.title: Transfer-Robustness Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Held-out target prediction detects whether transfer is beneficial before continued source use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given target folds \(V_1,ldots,V_K\), fit a transferred predictor \(p_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and a target-only predictor \(p_0\) on each complementary fold. Compute differences \(\delta_k=\log p_{\mathrm{tr}}(V_k)-\log p_0(V_k)\), their mean \(\bar\delta\), and a valid lower confidence bound \(B_\alpha\) for their expected value. Stop after all folds are evaluated. Retain transfer if \(B_\alpha\geq0\); otherwise disable or downweight the implicated sources and continue with the target-only model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare transferred and target-only held-out predictive scores; retain transfer only when a valid lower confidence bound on improvement is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The target data admit a prespecified validation scheme.
Both models assign finite predictive log scores to every validation fold.
\(B_\alpha\) has the declared coverage under the fold dependence model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_\alpha<0\) triggers rejection or downweighting of transfer.

notation.meaning: lower confidence bound for expected improvement

review_flags: The diagnostic and dependence-valid confidence construction require a specialized source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the diagnostics leaf, but the confidence-bound decision rule and fold-dependence validity need specialized support. The statement also contains the typo `V_1,ldots,V_K`, which should be `V_1,\ldots,V_K`.

children.title: Structured Observation Channels
children.top_down_role: Observation forms beyond a single scalar function value.

children.title: Gradient Observation Channels
children.top_down_role: Gradient-like information incorporated into surrogate search.

children.title: Derivative Observations
children.top_down_role: Gradient or partial-derivative information attached to evaluated candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-process conditioning with noisy linear derivative measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\) on an open set \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\), with \(m\) differentiable and \(k\) twice continuously differentiable. For linear differential functionals \(L_i\), observations have the form \(y_i=L_i f+\epsilon_i\), where \(\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\). Their joint Gaussian representation is \[\mathbb E[y_i]=L_i m,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(y_i,y_j)=L_iL_j'k+\Sigma_{ij},\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(f(x),y_i)=L_i'k(x,\cdot).\] Thus ordinary GP conditioning incorporates derivatives by applying the observation operators to the kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy derivatives are linear observations of a Gaussian process; their means and covariance blocks result from differentiating the mean and kernel.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is open.
The kernel derivatives required by every \(L_iL_j'\) exist and are continuous.
Observation noise is Gaussian and independent of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f(x),y_1,\ldots,y_n)\) is jointly Gaussian with covariance obtained by applying the derivative operators to \(k\).

notation.meaning: operator acting on the kernel's second argument

review_flags: The supplied derivative locator concerns hyperparameter optimization, not derivative observations; a direct GP source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear-operator GP representation is appropriate and coherent, but the inventory locator concerns derivative-based hyperparameter optimization rather than derivative observations, and no applicable source is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional derivative is a linear projection of the gradient, with GP covariance obtained by projecting the kernel's mixed Hessian along the observed directions.
assumptions_latex: Every \(x_i\) lies in the interior of \(\mathcal X\).
The mixed kernel derivatives exist at all observation pairs.

children.title: Partial-Derivative Channels
children.top_down_role: Settings where only selected coordinate derivatives are observed.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Derivative Channels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-indexed channels reveal selected gradient components with noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be the coordinates observed at \(x_i\). The partial-derivative channel returns \(y_{i,r}=\partial_r f(x_i)+\epsilon_{i,r}\) for each \(r\in I_i\). If \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), then all channel outputs are jointly Gaussian and \[\operatorname{Cov}(y_{i,r},y_{j,q})=\partial_{x_r}\partial_{x'_q}k(x_i,x_j)+\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon_{i,r},\epsilon_{j,q}).\] Function-value cross-covariances satisfy \(\operatorname{Cov}(f(x),y_{i,r})=\partial_{x'_{i,r}}k(x,x_i)\), allowing arbitrary coordinate subsets across observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-derivative channel observes selected gradient coordinates; GP covariance blocks are the corresponding mixed partial derivatives of the kernel plus noise covariance.
assumptions_latex: The required coordinatewise mixed derivatives of \(k\) exist.
The coordinate sets \(I_i\) are observed.
The noise vector is Gaussian and independent of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y_{i,r})_{r\in I_i}\) is a jointly Gaussian linear observation channel.

notation.meaning: noisy r-th partial derivative at point i

review_flags: A direct source for coordinatewise derivative channels is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-channel representation fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the joint Gaussian and mixed-partial covariance formulas.

children.title: Ordinal Feedback Query Family
children.top_down_role: Optimization based on ordinal, pairwise, or projective feedback.

children.title: Pairwise Preferential Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Latent-objective search using comparisons between candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Preferential Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential latent-objective optimization using noisy comparisons instead of cardinal responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), comparison data \(D_0\), and budget \(T\), initialize the posterior over \(f\). At iteration \(t\), choose \((x_t,x_t')\in\arg\max_{(x,x')\in\mathcal X^2}a_t(x,x')\), observe \(y_t\in\{0,1\}\) with \[\Pr(y_t=1\mid f)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{f(x_t)-f(x_t')}{\sigma}\right),\] append the comparison to \(D_t\), and update the non-Gaussian posterior. Stop after \(T\) queries and output \(\widehat x_T\in\arg\max_x\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_T]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preferential Bayesian optimization repeatedly selects candidate pairs, observes noisy preferences governed by a latent objective, updates its posterior, and returns the largest posterior-mean candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a nonempty feasible set.
\(\sigma>0\) is the comparison-noise scale.
The posterior and acquisition maximizers are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_T]\).
review_flags: The probit preferential-BO formulation requires a direct specialized citation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits preferential Bayesian optimization, but the probit likelihood, pair acquisition, posterior update, and posterior-mean recommendation constitute a specific formulation requiring a direct citation.

children.title: Rich Preference Query Family
children.top_down_role: Feedback richer than ordinary binary comparisons.

children.title: Projective Queries
children.top_down_role: Preference feedback elicited over restricted projections of the decision space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projective Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preference queries returning the best point on a parameterized feasible slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be latent, let \(z\in\mathcal X\), and let \(V\in\mathbb R^{d\times q}\). Define the feasible parameter set \(A(z,V)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb R^q:z+V\alpha\in\mathcal X\}\). A projective query \((z,V)\) returns a possibly noisy \(\widehat\alpha\) representing preference for \(z+V\widehat\alpha\) over other points on the slice, with the noiseless response satisfying \[\widehat\alpha\in\arg\max_{\alpha\in A(z,V)}f(z+V\alpha).\] For \(q=1\), the query optimizes preference along a feasible line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projective query asks for the preferred point on an affine feasible slice; without noise, its response maximizes the latent objective over that slice.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
\(A(z,V)\) is nonempty and the displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z+V\widehat\alpha\in\arg\max_{x\in(z+\operatorname{range}(V))\cap\mathcal X}f(x)\).
review_flags: The intended meaning of projective query is terminology-sensitive and needs a path-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, but “projective query” is terminology-sensitive and no path-specific source confirms that it means affine-slice preference maximization.

children.title: Ranking Queries
children.top_down_role: Feedback ordering multiple candidate alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinal queries returning a total or partial order over a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a query tuple \(Q=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathcal X^m\), a ranking query returns an ordered partition \((B_1,\ldots,B_r)\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). In the noiseless latent-utility model, \(i\in B_p\) and \(j\in B_q\) with \(p<q\) imply \(f(x_i)\geq f(x_j)\); indices in one block represent unresolved ties. A strict ranking is the special case \(|B_p|=1\) for every \(p\). A noisy ranking channel instead specifies a probability distribution over such ordered partitions conditional on \((f(x_i))_{i=1}^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranking query orders a finite candidate set by latent utility, possibly allowing ties or a probabilistic noisy ordering.
assumptions_latex: Each queried point belongs to \(\mathcal X\).
Any noisy channel is a normalized distribution over ordered partitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p<q\) implies \(f(x_i)\geq f(x_j)\) for \(i\in B_p\) and \(j\in B_q\) in the noiseless model.
review_flags: The supplied ranking-and-selection locator does not directly establish ordinal ranking-query semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-partition definition fits ranking queries, but the available ranking-and-selection locator does not establish these ordinal-query semantics, and no supporting citation is attached.

children.title: Query-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Information and burden differences across richer preference queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Query-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-per-cost principle for choosing among ordinal queries of differing granularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) denote the unknown utility or optimizer, \(D\) the current data, and \(q\in\mathcal Q\) an ordinal query whose response \(Y_q\) has likelihood \(p(y\mid\Theta,q)\) and positive cost \(c(q)\). A cost-normalized query policy selects
\[q^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{q\in\mathcal Q}\frac{I(\Theta;Y_q\mid D)}{c(q)}.\]
Increasing query granularity is beneficial only when its additional conditional information compensates for its greater elicitation cost; hence a richer ranking query need not dominate a pairwise or projective query under a fixed resource budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose ordinal-query granularity by posterior information gained per unit elicitation cost; richer responses are preferable only when their extra information justifies their extra cost.
assumptions_latex: \(0<c(q)<\infty\) for every admissible query \(q\).
\(I(\Theta;Y_q\mid D)\) exists and is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{q\in\mathcal Q} I(\Theta;Y_q\mid D)/c(q)\).

notation.meaning: latent utility, preference parameter, or optimizer
resource cost of issuing and answering q

review_flags: Exact preference-query information-per-cost source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-per-cost policy is mathematically coherent and fits the tradeoff container, but no source supports this particular preference-query criterion or the comparison among ranking, pairwise, and projective queries.

children.title: Interactive Utility Learning
children.top_down_role: Joint learning of outcome preferences and experimental decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interactive Utility Learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bayesian learning of an outcome model and a decision maker's latent utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given designs \(\mathcal X\), outcomes \(\mathcal Y\), priors \(p(f)\) and \(p(u)\), and preference likelihood \(p(r\mid u,f,q)\), initialize \(D_0=\varnothing\). At round \(t\), form \(p(f,u\mid D_t)\), choose an experiment or preference query
\[q_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{q\in\mathcal Q_t} A_t(q;p(f,u\mid D_t)),\]
observe response \(r_t\), and set \(D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{(q_t,r_t)\}\). Stop at the prescribed budget \(T\), and output a Bayes decision \(x_T\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[u(f(x))\mid D_T]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly update a joint posterior over outcomes and utility, select the most useful experiment or preference query, and finally recommend the design with greatest posterior expected utility.
assumptions_latex: The posterior \(p(f,u\mid D_t)\) is proper at every round.
Each acquisition maximization has an admissible maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_T\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[u(f(x))\mid D_T]\).
review_flags: A source for this specific joint Bayesian decision-and-utility-learning formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits interactive utility learning, but the specific joint posterior, mixed experiment/query acquisition, and terminal Bayes decision require a source.

children.title: Structured Output Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Structured response objects modeled or summarized for optimization.

children.title: Functional Outputs
children.top_down_role: Curve-, field-, or trajectory-valued responses used during optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Functional Outputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-integrable response curves represented by finitely many basis coefficients and a residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each design \(x\in\mathcal X\) produce a random function \(Y(x)\in L^2(\mathcal T)\). For orthonormal functions \(\{\phi_k\}_{k\ge1}\), its rank-\(K\) representation is
\[Y(x,t)=\mu(t)+\sum_{k=1}^{K}a_k(x)\phi_k(t)+r_K(x,t),\qquad a_k(x)=\langle Y(x,\cdot)-\mu,\phi_k\rangle_{L^2}.\]
A surrogate may model the coefficient vector \((a_1(x),\ldots,a_K(x))\); the approximation error is measured by \(\lVert r_K(x,\cdot)\rVert_{L^2}\), which vanishes as \(K\to\infty\) when the basis is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each response curve by basis coefficients plus a functional residual, then model the finite coefficient vector while tracking truncation error.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x,\cdot)-\mu\in L^2(\mathcal T)\).
\(\{\phi_k\}_{k\ge1}\) is a complete orthonormal basis of \(L^2(\mathcal T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(x,\cdot)=\mu+\sum_{k=1}^{K}a_k(x)\phi_k+r_K(x,\cdot)\) in \(L^2(\mathcal T)\).

notation.meaning: basis coefficient of the functional output
index domain of the output function
