children.title: Multivariate Outputs
children.top_down_role: Vector-valued responses with exploitable cross-output structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Outputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-valued surrogate representation with valid cross-output covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\ge2\), a multivariate output is a map \(Y:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\) with \(Y(x)=(Y_1(x),\ldots,Y_m(x))^\top\). A vector-valued Gaussian-process surrogate is specified by mean \(\mu:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\) and matrix-valued kernel \(K\), where
\[K_{ij}(x,x')=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_i(x),Y_j(x')).\]
Validity requires \(K(x,x')=K(x',x)^\top\) and
\[\sum_{a,b=1}^{n}v_a^\top K(x_a,x_b)v_b\ge0\]
for all finite \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathcal X\) and \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model vector responses jointly with a matrix-valued covariance kernel that captures both spatial dependence and cross-output correlation.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite.
All component means and covariances are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\sim\operatorname{GP}(\mu,K)\) defines a valid vector-valued Gaussian process when the stated symmetry and positive-semidefiniteness conditions hold.

notation.meaning: component i of the output at design x
cross-covariance between output components i and j

children.title: Output Summarization
children.top_down_role: Optimization-relevant reductions of structured response objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Output Summarization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar or low-dimensional summaries induced from structured simulator outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y(x)\) take values in a measurable output space \(\mathcal Y\), and let \(S:\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R^d\) be a measurable summary map. The summarized response is
\[Z(x)=S(Y(x)).\]
If a posterior distribution \(P_x\) describes \(Y(x)\), then the posterior law of the summary is the pushforward
\[P_x^S(B)=P_x(S^{-1}(B)),\qquad B\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d).\]
Optimization based only on \(Z\) is lossless for an objective \(J:\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R\) precisely when some \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(J=h\circ S\) on the attainable outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a measurable summary to structured outputs and propagate posterior uncertainty through it; optimization is lossless only when the objective factors through that summary.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\) is a measurable \(\mathcal Y\)-valued random element.
\(S\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_x^S=P_x\circ S^{-1}\), and objective values are preserved when \(J=h\circ S\).

notation.meaning: pushforward posterior distribution of the summary

children.title: Partial Outcome Observation Family
children.top_down_role: Non-Gaussian or partially observed outcomes carrying optimization information.

children.title: Censored Observations
children.top_down_role: Outcomes observed only through thresholds, bounds, or truncation.

knowledge_statements.title: Censored Observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood representation for outcomes observed only relative to censoring thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z(x)\in\mathbb R\) be a latent outcome. Under right censoring at a known threshold \(c\), the observation is \((Y,\delta)\), where
\[Y=\min\{Z(x),c\},\qquad \delta=\mathbf 1\{Z(x)\le c\}.\]
If \(Z(x)\) has conditional density \(p_x\) and distribution function \(F_x\), its likelihood contribution is
\[L_x(Y,\delta)=p_x(Y)^\delta\bigl(1-F_x(c)\bigr)^{1-\delta}.\]
Thus an uncensored outcome contributes its density, whereas a censored outcome contributes the probability of exceeding the threshold rather than a fictitious point value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A censored observation reports either the realized outcome or only that it exceeded a threshold, and its likelihood uses density or tail probability accordingly.
assumptions_latex: The censoring threshold \(c\) is known.
Censoring is conditionally noninformative given the modeled outcome.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_x(Y,\delta)=p_x(Y)^\delta(1-F_x(c))^{1-\delta}\).

notation.meaning: indicator that the outcome is observed exactly

review_flags: A precise survival-analysis or censored-regression source locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The right-censoring definition and likelihood are standard and precise, but no survival-analysis or censored-regression source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Binary Observations
children.top_down_role: Two-valued outcome channels carrying optimization-relevant information.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bernoulli observation channel obtained by thresholding or classifying a latent response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A binary observation at design \(x\in\mathcal X\) is a random variable \(B(x)\in\{0,1\}\) satisfying
\[B(x)\mid f(x)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi(x)),\qquad \pi(x)=\ell(f(x)),\]
where \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is latent and \(\ell:\mathbb R\to(0,1)\) is a specified link, such as the logistic or probit link. For observed \(b\in\{0,1\}\), the likelihood is
\[p(b\mid f(x))=\ell(f(x))^b\bigl(1-\ell(f(x))\bigr)^{1-b}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary channel observes success or failure with probability determined by a linked latent response, yielding the standard Bernoulli likelihood.
assumptions_latex: The link \(\ell\) is measurable and takes values strictly between zero and one.

children.title: Failure Observations
children.top_down_role: Evaluation failures treated as informative outcomes rather than missing records.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed observation channel distinguishing experimental validity from the outcome produced on success.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether an experiment at \(x\) fails, with \(\Pr(F(x)=1\mid x)=\rho(x)\). An outcome \(Y(x)\) is observed only when \(F(x)=0\), with conditional density \(p(y\mid x,F=0)\). The mixed likelihood is
\[p(F=1\mid x)=\rho(x),\qquad p(F=0,Y=y\mid x)=(1-\rho(x))p(y\mid x,F=0).\]
A failure flag therefore supplies information about \(\rho\) but, without an explicit failure-penalty model, is not a numerical observation of the latent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model experimental failure separately from successful outcomes; a failure updates failure risk but is not automatically an extreme objective value.
assumptions_latex: Failure status is always observed.
The successful-outcome density is defined conditional on \(F=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(F,Y\mid x)\) factors into a Bernoulli failure model and a conditional outcome model on successful trials.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Observations and data in stochastic optimization p. 62

review_flags: A source explicitly treating failed experiments as a mixed observation channel is desirable.

children.title: Shape-Symmetry Structural Priors
children.top_down_role: Known qualitative relations used to constrain or quotient the surrogate search space.

children.title: Shape-Constrained Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Surrogate models incorporating known qualitative response shape.

knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Constrained Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian surrogate restricted to functions satisfying prescribed global shape inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\) be a function space on \(\mathcal X\), let \(P\) be a prior on \(f\in\mathcal F\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F\) encode a shape restriction, such as
\[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{mono}}=\{f:\partial f(x)/\partial x_j\ge0\text{ for all }x\in\mathcal X\}\]
or
\[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{conv}}=\{f:\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\text{ for all }x\in\mathcal X\}.\]
A shape-constrained surrogate uses the conditional posterior \(P(df\mid D,f\in\mathcal C)\), provided \(P(f\in\mathcal C)>0\), so every posterior-supported function satisfies the selected restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condition a surrogate model on a function class enforcing monotonicity, convexity, or another specified shape restriction throughout the domain.
assumptions_latex: The required derivatives exist on \(\mathcal X\).
\(P(f\in\mathcal C)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(f\in\mathcal C\mid D,f\in\mathcal C)=1\).
review_flags: A source for posterior conditioning under global shape constraints is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits shape-constrained surrogates under its positive-prior-mass assumption, but the global-event conditioning formulation requires a specific source.

children.title: Invariant Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations insensitive to known transformations of inputs or outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feature maps constant on orbits of a specified group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a group \(G\) act on a set \(\mathcal X\). A representation \(\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z\) is \(G\)-invariant when
\[\phi(g\cdot x)=\phi(x)\qquad\text{for every }g\in G\text{ and }x\in\mathcal X.\]
It is orbit-separating when the converse also holds: \(\phi(x)=\phi(x')\) implies \(x'=g\cdot x\) for some \(g\in G\). Every invariant \(\phi\) factors uniquely through the quotient projection \(\pi:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X/G\), so there exists a unique \(\bar\phi:\mathcal X/G\to\mathcal Z\) satisfying \(\phi=\bar\phi\circ\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant representation assigns identical features to symmetry-equivalent designs and factors through the set of group orbits.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi=\bar\phi\circ\pi\) for a unique map \(\bar\phi:\mathcal X/G\to\mathcal Z\).

notation.meaning: symmetry group acting on the design space
projection from a design to its orbit

review_flags: A group-actions or invariant-representation source locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariance, orbit separation, and quotient-factorization statements are correct as set-theoretic claims, but no group-action or invariant-representation source is supplied.

children.title: Symmetry-Aware Search
children.top_down_role: Search exploiting equivalence among symmetry-related candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Aware Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian search using invariant posteriors and one representative per symmetry orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a group \(G\) act on \(\mathcal X\), and suppose the objective satisfies \(f(g\cdot x)=f(x)\). Choose a transversal \(R\subseteq\mathcal X\) containing one representative of each orbit and an invariant surrogate kernel satisfying
\[k(g\cdot x,g'\cdot x')=k(x,x')\]
for all \(g,g'\in G\). After conditioning on data \(D_t\), compute an orbit-invariant acquisition \(a_t\), select
\[x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in R}a_t(x),\]
observe the response, and update \(D_{t+1}\). Stop at the evaluation budget and return the orbit of the best recommended representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploit objective symmetry by using invariant surrogate quantities and optimizing acquisitions over one representative from each orbit.
assumptions_latex: The objective and observation law are constant on \(G\)-orbits.
A representative exists for every orbit.
Each acquisition maximization over \(R\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search evaluates at most one chosen representative per acquisition decision while preserving acquisition values over every orbit.
review_flags: A source for symmetry-reduced Bayesian optimization is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits symmetry-aware search, but its independently invariant kernel condition, transversal reduction, and acquisition-preservation claims require a symmetry-reduced Bayesian-optimization source.

children.title: Quotient Search Spaces
children.top_down_role: Reduced domains formed by grouping structurally equivalent candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Search Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search domain formed by identifying designs related through a symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a group \(G\) act on a search space \(\mathcal X\). Define \(x\sim_Gx'\) when \(x'=g\cdot x\) for some \(g\in G\). The quotient search space is
\[\mathcal X/G=\{[x]_G:x\in\mathcal X\},\qquad [x]_G=\{g\cdot x:g\in G\}.\]
If \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is invariant, then \(\bar f([x]_G)=f(x)\) is well-defined and
\[\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)=\inf_{[x]_G\in\mathcal X/G}\bar f([x]_G).\]
Thus optimization may be performed over equivalence classes without changing its optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identify symmetry-equivalent designs as one orbit; an invariant objective then descends to the quotient and retains the same optimum value.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on \(\mathcal X\).
\(f(g\cdot x)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar f([x]_G)=f(x)\) is well-defined and \(\inf_{\mathcal X}f=\inf_{\mathcal X/G}\bar f\).

notation.meaning: orbit of x under the group action

review_flags: A quotient-space optimization source locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient construction and preservation of the invariant objective's infimum are mathematically coherent and fit the container, but no specific source locator is supplied.

children.title: Uncertainty-Responsive Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization when outcomes include intrinsic randomness or the decision criterion values performance under uncertainty.

children.title: Observation Noise Regime Pair
children.top_down_role: Noise models distinguished by whether variability changes across the domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Gaussian observation noise and its exact limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian scalar observations with either constant or location-dependent positive noise scale; exact evaluation is obtained separately as the zero-noise limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi=f(x)\). For \(\sigma_n(x)>0\), additive Gaussian observation noise is defined by \(y=\phi+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\mid x\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_n(x)^2)\), so \(p(y\mid x,\phi,\sigma_n)=\mathcal N(y;\phi,\sigma_n(x)^2)\). Constant \(\sigma_n\) is homoskedastic, whereas location-dependent \(\sigma_n(x)\) is heteroskedastic. In the limit \(\sigma_n\equiv0\), \(y=\phi\) exactly and \(p(y\mid\phi)=\delta(y-\phi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive Gaussian observation is the objective value plus zero-mean Gaussian error. Constant variance gives homoskedastic noise, location-dependent variance gives heteroskedastic noise, and zero noise gives exact evaluation represented by a Dirac distribution.
assumptions_latex: \phi=f(x)
\varepsilon\mid x\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_n(x)^2)\text{ when }\sigma_n(x)>0
\sigma_n(x)\ge 0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\mid x,\phi\sim\mathcal N(\phi,\sigma_n(x)^2)\text{ for positive noise scale},\qquad \sigma_n\equiv0\Rightarrow p(y\mid\phi)=\delta(y-\phi).
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Gaussian observation noise and its exact limit

children.title: Homoskedastic Observation Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation variability treated as constant across the domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Homoskedastic Observation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant conditional observation variance in noisy Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be a design space and let observations satisfy \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\). The observation noise is homoskedastic when there exists one constant \(\sigma^2\in(0,\infty)\) such that \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i\mid x_i]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i\mid x_i)=\sigma^2\) for every \(x_i\in\mathcal X\). If the errors are conditionally independent, the noise covariance for \(n\) observations is \(\sigma^2 I_n\), including when multiple observations share a design location.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation errors are homoskedastic when their conditional variance is the same positive constant at every design location.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) for \(x_i\in\mathcal X\).
The errors are conditionally independent and have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is homoskedastic exactly when \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i\mid x_i)=\sigma^2\) for one location-independent \(\sigma^2>0\).

children.title: Heteroskedastic Observation Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation variability changing across candidate locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Heteroskedastic Observation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Location-dependent conditional observation variance in Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations obey \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) on a design space \(\mathcal X\). The observation noise is heteroskedastic when \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i\mid x_i]=0\) and its conditional variance is a nonconstant function \(s^2:\mathcal X\to(0,\infty)\), so that \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i\mid x_i)=s^2(x_i)\). Under conditional independence, the noise covariance at design points \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(s^2(x_1),\ldots,s^2(x_n))\). Replicates at one location share the same conditional variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation noise is heteroskedastic when its conditional variance varies with the evaluated design location.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) for \(x_i\in\mathcal X\).
The errors are conditionally independent and have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is heteroskedastic when \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i\mid x_i)=s^2(x_i)\) for a nonconstant positive function \(s^2\).

notation.meaning: diagonal matrix formed from its arguments

children.title: Noise-Model Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty about the appropriate spatial structure of observation variability.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Model Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epistemic uncertainty about the observation-noise law or its parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) and the conditional error law belongs to \(\{p_\theta(\cdot\mid x):\theta\in\Theta\}\). Noise-model uncertainty is present when \(\theta\), or even the family containing the true error law, is unknown and is represented by a posterior \(\Pi(d\theta\mid\mathcal D_n)\) or an admissible set \(\Theta_n\). Predictive uncertainty must then marginalize or range over the noise model rather than condition on one fixed variance function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise-model uncertainty concerns uncertainty about the error distribution or variance model itself, not merely randomness generated by a known noise law.
assumptions_latex: The conditional error law is modeled by \(p_\theta(\cdot\mid x)\) with \(\theta\in\Theta\).
Observed data are \(\mathcal D_n=\{(x_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noise-model uncertainty is represented by nondegenerate uncertainty over \(\theta\) or over the family \(\{p_\theta\}\).

children.title: Replication-Aware Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Sequential choice between new locations and repeated evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication-Aware Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential allocation between unexplored designs and replicates at observed designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal D_0\), a budget \(N\), and a posterior utility \(U\), let \(S_t\) be the distinct locations observed by time \(t\). For \(t=0,\ldots,N-1\), form candidates from \(\mathcal X\), including both \(S_t\) and unobserved locations, and choose \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[U(\mathcal D_t\cup\{(x,Y)\})-U(\mathcal D_t)\mid\mathcal D_t,x]\). Observe \(Y_{t+1}\), update \(\mathcal D_{t+1}\), and stop after \(N\) evaluations. Output a posterior-optimal recommendation; choosing \(x_{t+1}\in S_t\) constitutes replication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each step, compare the expected posterior value of repeating an observed location with that of evaluating a new location.
assumptions_latex: The observation model supplies \(p(Y\mid x,\mathcal D_t)\).
The utility increments are integrable and the evaluation budget satisfies \(N\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a recommendation measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_N\), after adaptively allocating evaluations to new locations or replicates.

notation.meaning: set of distinct locations evaluated by time t

children.title: Risk-Aware Objective Families
children.top_down_role: Search criteria targeting distributional performance rather than only mean response.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Aware Objective Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objectives obtained by applying risk functionals to random performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,W)\) be an integrable random loss for decision \(x\in\mathcal X\). A risk-aware objective has the representation \(J_\rho(x)=\rho(L(x,W))\), where \(\rho\) is a specified law-invariant risk functional. Important families include the mean \(\rho(Z)=\mathbb E[Z]\), the upper quantile \(\rho(Z)=\inf\{z:\mathbb P(Z\le z)\ge\alpha\}\), and conditional value at risk \(\rho(Z)=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+(1-\alpha)^{-1}\mathbb E[(Z-\eta)_+]\}\), with \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Optimization minimizes \(J_\rho\) over \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk-aware optimization applies a chosen risk functional—such as a mean, quantile, or conditional value at risk—to each decision's random loss.
assumptions_latex: \(L(x,W)\) is integrable for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The risk level satisfies \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective family is \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}J_\rho(x)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\rho(L(x,W))\).

notation.meaning: random loss at decision x under uncertainty W

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and the displayed mean, quantile, and CVaR formulas are standard and fit the objective-family container, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Exogenous Uncertainty Interface
children.top_down_role: Optimization over controllable decisions under uncertain operating conditions.

children.title: Environmental Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertain exogenous conditions affecting evaluated or deployed performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Environmental Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random exogenous conditions affecting performance but not selected by the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathcal X\) be a decision and let \(W\sim P_W\) denote an exogenous environmental variable whose distribution is not controlled by choosing \(x\). Environmental uncertainty is the randomness in the response \(G(x,W)\) induced by unrevealed or varying \(W\). A stochastic optimization criterion therefore evaluates the distribution of \(G(x,W)\), for example through \(\mathbb E_{P_W}[G(x,W)]\) or another specified risk functional, rather than treating the response at \(x\) as deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Environmental uncertainty arises from uncontrollable external conditions whose random realizations affect the performance of a chosen decision.
assumptions_latex: The decision belongs to \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The environmental variable has law \(W\sim P_W\), unaffected by the choice of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Performance is the random variable \(G(x,W)\), and its evaluation depends on its law under \(P_W\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Environmental Variables and Random Control Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Models performance depending on a controllable configuration and an exogenous environmental variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partially controllable objective has the form \(g(x,\omega)\), where \(x\) is the configuration to be optimized and \(\omega\) is an environmental variable outside the decision maker's control. Random perturbation of the implemented control is the special case \(g(x,\omega)=h(x+\omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Performance may depend on both a chosen configuration and an uncontrolled environmental variable. Random implementation error is the special case obtained by evaluating an underlying objective at the perturbed input x plus omega.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is a controllable configuration}
\omega\text{ is an uncontrolled environmental variable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x,\omega)=h(x+\omega)\quad\text{in the random-input-perturbation special case}
