children.title: Certainty-Based Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping governed by posterior or frequentist decision certainty.

children.title: Precision-Threshold Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping based on a required level of estimation precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Threshold Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping when posterior uncertainty in every recommendation-relevant objective gap is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite alternatives, let \(\widehat i_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_i\mu_t(i)\) be the current posterior-mean recommendation and define the objective gap \(G_{i,t}=f_i-f_{\widehat i_t}\). Given a precision tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define
\[\tau_{\mathrm{prec}}=\inf\left\{t\geq0:\max_{i\neq\widehat i_t}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(G_{i,t}\mid D_t)}\leq\varepsilon\right\}.\]
At this time, terminate sampling and return \(\widehat i_t\). This criterion controls posterior standard deviation of pairwise gaps; it does not by itself guarantee that the recommended alternative is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when every posterior standard deviation of a gap between the current recommendation and a competitor is at most the prescribed precision tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The alternative set is finite.
Every posterior gap variance is finite.
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\max_{i\neq\widehat i_t}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(f_i-f_{\widehat i_t}\mid D_t)}\leq\varepsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{stop and return }\widehat i_t.\]

notation.meaning: Objective gap between competitor i and the recommendation.

review_flags: A source for this recommendation-gap precision criterion is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition precisely controls posterior standard deviations of recommendation-relative gaps and correctly disclaims an optimality guarantee. It fits the leaf, but no source supports this exact gap-precision stopping criterion.

children.title: Confidence-Threshold Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping based on a required level of decision confidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Threshold Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Framework-neutral stopping rule based on a declared confidence measure for an acceptable recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat x_t\) be the current recommendation and let \(E_t(\widehat x_t)\) denote the declared acceptability event, such as \(f(\widehat x_t)-\inf_x f(x)\leq\varepsilon\). Let \(C_t(\widehat x_t)\in[0,1]\) be a specified, data-measurable confidence assessment for that event, interpreted according to its declared posterior or frequentist construction. For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), define
\[\tau_C=\inf\left\{t\geq0:C_t(\widehat x_t)\geq1-\alpha\right\}.\]
Terminate at \(\tau_C\) and return \(\widehat x_{	au_C}\). The confidence interpretation is valid only under the calibration or coverage assumptions of the chosen construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when the declared confidence that the current recommendation meets a specified acceptability criterion reaches at least one minus the chosen error tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t(\widehat x_t)\) is data-measurable and takes values in \([0,1]\).
The acceptability event and confidence construction are fixed before applying the threshold.
The chosen construction's calibration or coverage assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C_t(\widehat x_t)\geq1-\alpha\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{stop and return }\widehat x_t.\]

notation.meaning: Declared event that the current recommendation is acceptable.
Confidence assessment for the acceptability event.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Variational inequalities and confidence bounds p. 21

review_flags: The cited confidence-bound section must be checked for an explicit stopping-threshold formulation.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Variational inequalities and confidence bounds p. 21

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic threshold condition fits the leaf, but its confidence object deliberately spans posterior and frequentist constructions whose sequential interpretations require different calibration or coverage conditions. The cited confidence-bounds section does not establish the exact stopping rule from the supplied evidence, so a direct source or separate construction-specific support is required.

children.title: Posterior-Certainty Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping governed by posterior uncertainty about the terminal decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Certainty Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian stopping based on posterior probability of an epsilon-optimal terminal recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be finite, let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be maximized, and let \(\Pi_n\) denote the posterior after \(n\) observations. For a data-measurable recommendation \(r_n\in\mathcal X\), define its posterior certainty by \[q_n(r_n)=\Pi_n\!\left(f(r_n)\ge \max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-\varepsilon\right).\] Given \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), posterior-certainty termination uses the stopping time \[\tau_{\varepsilon,\alpha}=\inf\{n\ge0:q_n(r_n)\ge1-\alpha\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\), and returns \(r_{\tau_{\varepsilon,\alpha}}\) whenever the stopping time is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when the posterior probability that the current recommendation is epsilon-optimal reaches at least one minus alpha, then return that recommendation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and the posterior \(\Pi_n\) is well defined.
\(r_n\) is measurable with respect to the observations available at time \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\tau_{\varepsilon,\alpha}}(r_{\tau_{\varepsilon,\alpha}})\ge1-\alpha\) on \(\{\tau_{\varepsilon,\alpha}<\infty\}\).

notation.meaning: terminal recommendation considered at time n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits posterior-certainty termination, but no inspectable citation supports this stopping-rule formulation.

children.title: Frequentist-Certainty Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping governed by repeated-sampling measures of decision certainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Frequentist-Certainty Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-confidence stopping certified by simultaneous confidence bounds over a finite decision set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be maximized on a finite set, and suppose data-measurable bounds \(L_n(x)\le U_n(x)\) satisfy \[\mathbb P_f\!\left(\forall n\ge0,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X:\ L_n(x)\le f(x)\le U_n(x)\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] For a recommendation \(r_n\), stop at \[\tau=\inf\left\{n\ge0:L_n(r_n)\ge\max_{x\in\mathcal X}U_n(x)-\varepsilon\right\}.\] On the simultaneous-coverage event and \(\{\tau<\infty\}\), the returned point satisfies \[f(r_\tau)\ge\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when the recommendation's lower confidence bound is within epsilon of every candidate's upper bound; simultaneous coverage then certifies epsilon-optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The confidence sequence has simultaneous coverage probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P_f(\tau<\infty\Rightarrow f(r_\tau)\ge\max_x f(x)-\varepsilon)\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: simultaneous lower and upper confidence bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and simultaneous-coverage conclusion are coherent and fit the leaf, but the confidence-sequence stopping rule has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Terminal Recommendation Rules
children.top_down_role: Alternative terminal choices after data collection ends.

children.title: Observed-Incumbent Recommendation
children.top_down_role: Terminal selection restricted to previously evaluated candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Observed-Incumbent Recommendation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recommendation restricted to evaluated decisions and ranked by their observed estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(n\) evaluations, let \(E_n\subseteq\mathcal X\) be the nonempty set of decisions observed at the designated target fidelity, and let \(\widehat f_n(x)\) be the prescribed observation-based estimator for each \(x\in E_n\). For maximization, an observed-incumbent recommendation is any measurable selection \[r_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in E_n}\widehat f_n(x).\] Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule. Thus the recommendation must be previously evaluated and depends on observed estimates rather than unrestricted posterior predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommend the previously evaluated target-fidelity decision having the largest prescribed observed estimate, with deterministic tie-breaking.
assumptions_latex: \(E_n\ne\varnothing\).
\(\widehat f_n(x)\) is defined for every \(x\in E_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\in E_n\) and \(\widehat f_n(r_n^{\mathrm{obs}})=\max_{x\in E_n}\widehat f_n(x)\).

notation.meaning: decisions evaluated at target fidelity by time n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the recommendation leaf, but the target-fidelity restriction and prescribed estimator convention require a direct source, especially under noisy observations.

children.title: Posterior-Mean Recommendation
children.top_down_role: Terminal selection based on posterior expected objective quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Mean Recommendation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayes recommendation maximizing the posterior mean of the target-fidelity objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the target-fidelity objective and let \(\mathcal D_n\) be the data collected by time \(n\). Assume the posterior mean \[\mu_n(x)=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\] exists for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and attains its maximum. A posterior-mean recommendation is any measurable selection \[r_n^{\mu}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(x),\] with ties resolved by a specified rule. Under posterior expected simple regret, this rule is Bayes optimal because the conditional term \(\mathbb E[\max_x f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\) does not depend on the selected point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommend a decision maximizing the posterior mean of the target-fidelity objective; this minimizes posterior expected simple regret.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[|f(x)|\mid\mathcal D_n]<\infty\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_n^{\mu}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{r\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-f(r)\mid\mathcal D_n]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The posterior-mean rule and its expected-simple-regret characterization are correct under the stated assumptions, but neither claim has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Posterior-Optimality Recommendation
children.top_down_role: Terminal selection based on posterior evidence of optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Optimality Recommendation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain recommendation maximizing posterior probability of being a true optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be finite and let \(\Pi_n\) be the posterior distribution of the target objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\). Define the posterior optimality probability of \(x\) by \[p_n(x)=\Pi_n\!\left(x\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\right).\] A posterior-optimality recommendation is a measurable selection \[r_n^{\mathrm{PO}}
\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}p_n(x),\] with a fixed tie-breaking convention. Equivalently, it is a Bayes action for zero-one loss \(\ell(r,f)=\mathbf 1\{r\notin\operatorname*{arg\,max}_u f(u)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommend the decision having the greatest posterior probability of belonging to the true optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and nonempty.
The posterior probabilities \(p_n(x)\) are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_n^{\mathrm{PO}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{r\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[\ell(r,f)\mid\mathcal D_n]\).

notation.meaning: posterior probability that x is optimal

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain definition and zero-one-loss characterization fit the leaf, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Recommendation Disagreement
children.top_down_role: Regimes where incumbent-based and posterior-based choices diverge.

knowledge_statements.title: Recommendation Disagreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects when terminal rules select different decisions from the same information state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the same data \(\mathcal D_n\) and fixed tie-breaking conventions, let \(r_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(r_n^{\mu}\), and \(r_n^{\mathrm{PO}}\) denote the observed-incumbent, posterior-mean, and posterior-optimality recommendations whenever all three exist. Recommendation disagreement occurs precisely when \[\left|\{r_n^{\mathrm{obs}},r_n^{\mu},r_n^{\mathrm{PO}}\}\right|>1.\] Pairwise disagreement may be quantified by \[D_n(a,b)=\mathbf 1\{r_n^a\ne r_n^b\},\qquad a,b\in\{\mathrm{obs},\mu,\mathrm{PO}\}.\] Agreement is the complementary condition in which all three selected decisions coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommendation disagreement occurs when the observed-incumbent, posterior-mean, and posterior-optimality rules do not all select the same decision.
assumptions_latex: All three recommendation rules are defined from the same \(\mathcal D_n\).
Each rule uses a fixed tie-breaking convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|\{r_n^{\mathrm{obs}},r_n^{\mu},r_n^{\mathrm{PO}}\}\right|>1\) if and only if at least one pairwise indicator \(D_n(a,b)\) equals \(1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition precisely expresses disagreement among the three recommendation rules and the content kind fits, but the record lacks cited support.

children.top_down_role: Optimization using observations that differ in cost, accuracy, resolution, or provenance.

children.title: Information-Source Geometry
children.top_down_role: Structural forms of fidelity controls and source choices.

children.title: Discrete Ordered Fidelity Levels
children.top_down_role: Ordered collections of simulators, resolutions, or approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Ordered Fidelity Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite fidelity hierarchy ordered by increasing accuracy and evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A discrete ordered fidelity system consists of a design space \(\mathcal X\), levels \(\mathcal Z=\{1,\ldots,L\}\), responses \(f_\ell:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), and costs \(c_\ell:\mathcal X\to(0,\infty)\). Level \(L\) is the target fidelity. Relative to a discrepancy functional \(d_x(f_\ell,f_L)\), the ordering requires, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \[c_1(x)\le\cdots\le c_L(x),\qquad d_x(f_1,f_L)\ge\cdots\ge d_x(f_L,f_L)=0.\] Equalities are permitted; strict inequalities may be imposed when distinct resource and accuracy levels are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete fidelities form finitely many levels whose cost does not decrease and whose discrepancy from the target does not increase.
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) is finite.
The discrepancy \(d_x\) is nonnegative and vanishes at the target response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\le i\le j\le L\) implies \(c_i(x)\le c_j(x)\) and \(d_x(f_i,f_L)\ge d_x(f_j,f_L)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits an ordered fidelity hierarchy, but simultaneous pointwise monotonicity of both cost and target discrepancy is a substantive convention requiring a multifidelity source.

children.title: Continuous Fidelity Controls
children.top_down_role: Continuously tunable accuracy, resolution, or effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Fidelity Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuously tunable resource control approaching a designated target fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous fidelity model consists of a design domain \(\mathcal X\), a compact fidelity domain \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), a target \(z^\star\in\mathcal Z\), a response \(g:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R\), and a positive cost \(c:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to(0,\infty)\). The target objective is \(f(x)=g(x,z^\star)\). For a one-dimensional ordered control \(\mathcal Z=[0,1]\) with \(z^\star=1\), the fidelity convention is \[z_1\le z_2\Longrightarrow c(x,z_1)\le c(x,z_2),\qquad d_x(g(\cdot,z_1),f)\ge d_x(g(\cdot,z_2),f).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous fidelity is a tunable control whose target value defines the objective, with higher settings conventionally costing more and reducing target discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Z\) is compact and contains \(z^\star\).
The response and cost are defined on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,z^\star)=f(x)\) and \(d_x(g(\cdot,z^\star),f)=0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

notation.meaning: response at design x and fidelity z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general representation fits continuous fidelity controls, but compactness and the one-dimensional monotonicity convention need support, and the discrepancy functional used in the statement is not formally introduced.

children.title: Multiple Unordered Information Sources
children.top_down_role: Sources related by usefulness rather than a global fidelity order.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Unordered Information Sources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sources lacking a single design-independent ranking by cost-adjusted information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index information sources with observations \(Y_s(x)\) and costs \(c_s(x)>0\). Given current data \(\mathcal D\) and a target quantity \(T\), define the cost-adjusted information value \[V_s(x)=\frac{I(T;Y_s(x)\mid\mathcal D)}{c_s(x)}.\] The sources are unordered when no permutation \(\pi\) ranks them uniformly over the design domain, namely when there is no \(\pi\) satisfying \[V_{\pi(1)}(x)\le\cdots\le V_{\pi(m)}(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.\] Thus relative usefulness can vary with location and information state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information sources are unordered when no single source ranking by cost-adjusted information value holds throughout the design domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is finite and \(c_s(x)>0\).
The conditional mutual information \(I(T;Y_s(x)\mid\mathcal D)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every permutation \(\pi\), some \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(i<j\) satisfy \(V_{\pi(i)}(x)>V_{\pi(j)}(x)\).

notation.meaning: observation supplied by source s at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mutual-information ranking is one possible usefulness criterion, not an intrinsic definition of unordered information sources. A source is needed to justify this exact model-dependent terminal formulation.

children.title: Multidimensional Fidelity Spaces
children.top_down_role: Several interacting controls over evaluation accuracy and cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Multidimensional Fidelity Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fidelity represented by several jointly chosen resource or approximation controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A multidimensional fidelity space is a product \[\mathcal Z=\mathcal Z_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal Z_q,
\qquad q\ge2,\] with response \(g:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R\), cost \(c:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to(0,\infty)\), and target vector \(z^\star=(z_1^\star,\ldots,z_q^\star)\). The target objective is \(f(x)=g(x,z^\star)\). Under the componentwise order \(z\preceq z'\), a monotone model satisfies \[c(x,z)\le c(x,z'),\qquad d_x(g(\cdot,z),f)\ge d_x(g(\cdot,z'),f).\] Incomparable vectors may trade different accuracy and cost mechanisms and need not admit a scalar fidelity ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several fidelity controls form a product space with a target vector; componentwise improvements may be ordered, while cross-coordinate tradeoffs can remain incomparable.
assumptions_latex: \(q\ge2\) and each \(\mathcal Z_i\) contains its target value \(z_i^\star\).
The discrepancy is nonnegative and vanishes at \(z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,z^\star)=f(x)\), while \(z\npreceq z'\) and \(z'\npreceq z\) need not determine any fidelity ordering.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-space representation fits the leaf, but componentwise monotonicity of cost and discrepancy is an additional modeling assumption needing direct multifidelity support.

children.title: Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Relations
children.top_down_role: Model families connecting auxiliary sources to the target objective.

children.title: Autoregressive Co-Kriging Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical dependence among fidelity levels.

children.title: Autoregressive Fidelity Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Directed dependence across ordered fidelity levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Autoregressive Fidelity Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kennedy–O'Hagan-style recursive Gaussian-process relation across ordered fidelities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ordered levels \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\), an autoregressive fidelity hierarchy represents latent responses recursively as \[f_1(x)=\delta_1(x),\qquad f_\ell(x)=\rho_{\ell-1}(x)f_{\ell-1}(x)+\delta_\ell(x),\quad \ell=2,\ldots,L.\] The discrepancy processes \(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_L\) are mutually independent Gaussian processes, and the deterministic scale functions \(\rho_{\ell-1}\) are fixed or parametrically estimated. Consequently, \[f_\ell(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\left(\prod_{k=j}^{\ell-1}\rho_k(x)\right)\delta_j(x),\] where an empty product equals \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each fidelity equals a scaled version of the preceding fidelity plus an independent Gaussian-process discrepancy, yielding an explicit sum over discrepancies.
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) and all processes share the domain \(\mathcal X\).
The Gaussian processes \(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_L\) are mutually independent.
Each \(\rho_\ell:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is deterministic conditional on model parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\ell\) is a Gaussian process whose dependence on lower fidelities is induced by the recursive scaling relation.

notation.meaning: latent response at fidelity level ell

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive representation and expanded sum are internally consistent and fit an autoregressive fidelity hierarchy, but a canonical co-kriging citation with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Co-Kriging Covariance Structures
children.top_down_role: Joint spatial covariance representations across fidelity outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Co-Kriging Covariance Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-fidelity covariance induced by an autoregressive Gaussian-process hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the autoregressive hierarchy with constant scales \(f_1=\delta_1\) and \(f_\ell=\rho_{\ell-1}f_{\ell-1}+\delta_\ell\), where independent discrepancy processes satisfy \(\operatorname{Cov}(\delta_j(x),\delta_j(x'))=k_j(x,x')\). Define \(a_{j,\ell}=\prod_{r=j}^{\ell-1}\rho_r\) for \(j\le\ell\). Then the co-kriging cross-covariance between levels \(\ell\) and \(m\) is \[K_{\ell m}(x,x')=\operatorname{Cov}(f_\ell(x),f_m(x'))=
\sum_{j=1}^{\min(\ell,m)}a_{j,\ell}a_{j,m}k_j(x,x').\] The resulting block kernel is positive semidefinite whenever every \(k_j\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The covariance between two fidelities sums the kernels of their shared discrepancy ancestors, weighted by products of autoregressive scales.
assumptions_latex: The autoregressive scales \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{L-1}\) are deterministic constants.
The discrepancy processes are mutually independent and have positive-semidefinite kernels \(k_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\ell m}(x,x')=\sum_{j=1}^{\min(\ell,m)}a_{j,\ell}a_{j,m}k_j(x,x')\), and \(K\) is a positive-semidefinite matrix-valued kernel.

notation.meaning: covariance kernel of discrepancy process j
cumulative autoregressive scale from level j to level ell
cross-covariance between fidelity levels ell and m

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cross-covariance formula and positive-semidefinite block-kernel conclusion follow from the stated constant-scale hierarchy and fit the representation leaf, but no canonical source or locator is provided.

children.title: Nested Fidelity Designs
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical models supported by nested observation locations.

assumptions_latex: There are fidelity levels indexed by \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\).
Each level has a design set \(D_\ell\subseteq\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_L\subseteq D_{L-1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq D_1\).

notation.meaning: design points evaluated at fidelity level \(\ell\)

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports nested multifidelity experimental designs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact nesting for ordered, finite fidelity levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multifidelity design \((D_1,\ldots,D_L)\) on an input domain \(\mathcal X\) is nested, with fidelity increasing in \(\ell\), when \[D_L\subseteq D_{L-1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq D_1\subseteq\mathcal X.\] Thus every input evaluated at level \(\ell+1\) is also evaluated at level \(\ell\). In particular, observations of adjacent fidelities are colocated at all points in \(D_{\ell+1}\), so discrepancies between those fidelities can be observed directly there. The definition imposes no requirement that the inclusions be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fidelity design is nested when every point evaluated at a higher fidelity is also evaluated at every lower fidelity.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Fidelity Designs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the nesting convention or the colocated-discrepancy interpretation.

children.title: Hierarchy Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Model failure when assumed fidelity ordering or dependence is inaccurate.

assumptions_latex: The fitted hierarchy is \(f_\ell(x)=\rho_{\ell-1}f_{\ell-1}(x)+\delta_\ell(x)\).
The true conditional relation need not have constant linear scaling or independent discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of \(\operatorname{Cov}(\delta_\ell,f_{\ell-1})=0\) or constant scaling invalidates the stated autoregressive hierarchy.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports autoregressive co-kriging misspecification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the model boundary of a constant-scale autoregressive co-kriging hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The autoregressive hierarchy is misspecified whenever the true relation cannot satisfy, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \[f_\ell(x)=\rho_{\ell-1}f_{\ell-1}(x)+\delta_\ell(x),\qquad \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\delta_\ell(x),f_{\ell-1}(x')\right)=0\quad\text{for all }x'\in\mathcal X,\] with a constant \(\rho_{\ell-1}\). A concrete failure family is \(f_\ell(x)=r(x)f_{\ell-1}(x)+\varepsilon_\ell(x)\), where \(r\) is nonconstant and \(\varepsilon_\ell\) is independent of \(f_{\ell-1}\). No constant choice of \(\rho_{\ell-1}\) then yields an independent residual unless \((r(x)-\rho_{\ell-1})f_{\ell-1}(x)\) vanishes identically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-scale autoregressive hierarchy fails when fidelity scaling varies with input or its residual remains correlated with the lower-fidelity process.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Misspecification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the assertion about when nonconstant scaling cannot yield an independent residual requires authoritative support and careful qualification for exceptional stochastic constructions.

children.title: Coregionalized Multitask Covariance Models
children.top_down_role: Joint covariance models treating sources as related outputs or tasks.

children.title: Coregionalization Covariances
children.top_down_role: Cross-output covariance structures for related information sources.

assumptions_latex: \(k_q\) is a positive-semidefinite scalar kernel on \(\mathcal X\) for each \(q\).
\(B_q\) is a positive-semidefinite \(T\times T\) matrix for each \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K((x,t),(x',t'))=\sum_{q=1}^Q (B_q)_{tt'}k_q(x,x')\) is a valid multitask covariance.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports linear coregionalization covariances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-task linear model of coregionalization covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tasks \(t,t'\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and inputs \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\), a linear coregionalization covariance has the representation \[K\bigl((x,t),(x',t')\bigr)=\sum_{q=1}^{Q}(B_q)_{tt'}k_q(x,x').\] Each \(B_q\succeq0\) controls cross-task dependence for component \(q\), while \(k_q\) controls its dependence over inputs. The resulting \(K\) is positive semidefinite because, on any finite collection of input-task pairs, each summand induces a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix and their sum remains positive semidefinite. The intrinsic coregionalization model is the special case \(Q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coregionalization expresses multitask covariance as a sum of input kernels weighted by positive-semidefinite task covariance matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Coregionalization Covariances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but it has no citation and includes proof-style justification that should not appear in a knowledge statement.

children.title: Multitask Gaussian Processes
children.top_down_role: Joint surrogate representations treating sources as related tasks.

assumptions_latex: The task set \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) is finite.
The mean \(m\) and kernel \(K\) are defined on \(\mathcal X\times\{1,\ldots,T\}\), with \(K\) positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite vector \((f_{t_i}(x_i))_{i=1}^n\) is multivariate Gaussian with covariance induced by \(K\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports multitask Gaussian processes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a finite-task Gaussian process through its joint input-task index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multitask Gaussian process is a collection \(\{f_t(x):x\in\mathcal X,\ t=1,\ldots,T\}\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and every selection \((x_i,t_i)_{i=1}^n\), \[\bigl(f_{t_1}(x_1),\ldots,f_{t_n}(x_n)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma),\] where \(\mu_i=m(x_i,t_i)\) and \(\Sigma_{ij}=K((x_i,t_i),(x_j,t_j))\). Equivalently, it is an ordinary Gaussian process indexed by the product set \(\mathcal X\times\{1,\ldots,T\}\). Cross-task information transfer is determined by the off-diagonal task blocks of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multitask Gaussian process is a Gaussian process indexed jointly by an input and a finite task label.
knowledge_statements.title: Multitask Gaussian Processes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-task definition is precise and appropriate, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Task-Specific Noise
children.top_down_role: Unequal observation uncertainty across modeled tasks.

assumptions_latex: Conditional on the latent processes, observation errors are independent across evaluations.
Each task variance satisfies \(\sigma_t^2\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The observation covariance equals the latent multitask covariance plus \(\sigma_t^2\) on matching observations of task \(t\).

notation.meaning: observed response for task \(t\) at input \(x\)

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports task-specific noise in multitask Gaussian processes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent homoscedastic noise within each task, with variance varying across tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Task-specific observation noise is modeled by \[y_t(x)=f_t(x)+\epsilon_t(x),\qquad \epsilon_t(x)\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_t^2),\] with errors conditionally independent over distinct evaluations and independent of all latent processes. Hence, for indexed observations \((x_i,t_i)\) and \((x_j,t_j)\), \[\operatorname{Cov}(y_{t_i}(x_i),y_{t_j}(x_j))=K((x_i,t_i),(x_j,t_j))+\sigma_{t_i}^2\mathbf 1\{i=j\}.\] Thus the observation Gram matrix is the latent multitask Gram matrix plus a diagonal matrix whose entries are selected by task. The model permits noiseless tasks by allowing \(\sigma_t^2=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each task has its own observation-noise variance, added to the corresponding diagonal entries of the joint covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Task-Specific Noise

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes independent task-specific homoscedastic noise, but it lacks a supporting citation and locator.

children.title: Negative Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where cross-task coupling degrades target prediction.

assumptions_latex: The target task and an auxiliary task are truly independent.
A fitted model enforces nonzero cross-task dependence rather than estimating independence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forced cross-task coupling can increase target prediction error relative to fitting the target task independently.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports a formal negative-transfer boundary.
Exact risk comparison depends on the fitted covariance and observation design.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete misspecification boundary for transfer from an unrelated auxiliary task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two tasks with true cross-covariance \(K_{12}^{\star}(x,x')=0\) for all \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\). Suppose instead that the fitted coregionalization model fixes \(K_{12}\neq0\). Its target posterior mean then generally contains a nonzero linear term in the auxiliary observations. Conditional on the target data, that term has zero true predictive signal but positive variance whenever the auxiliary noise or process variance is positive. Consequently, under squared-error risk averaged over the true independent tasks, the coupled predictor has risk equal to the target-only predictor's risk plus the variance of this spurious term, except where its coefficient vanishes. This is a negative-transfer boundary: independence must remain representable by the fitted model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When tasks are truly independent, forced cross-task covariance injects signal-free auxiliary variation and can make target prediction worse than independent modeling.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the claimed exact risk increase is not established by independence alone: forced coupling can also alter target-data coefficients and introduce covariance terms. A formal source and sufficient conditions are required.

children.title: Discrepancy Model Family
children.top_down_role: Explicit representations of source-to-target disagreement.

children.title: Additive Discrepancy Models
children.top_down_role: Source disagreement represented through additive correction structure.

assumptions_latex: The low-fidelity response \(f_L\) and discrepancy \(\delta\) are functions on \(\mathcal X\).
When probabilistic, \(f_L\) and \(\delta\) are independent Gaussian processes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_H(x)=\rho f_L(x)+\delta(x)\), with covariance \(\rho^2k_L+k_\delta\) under independence.

notation.meaning: additive discrepancy from scaled low fidelity

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports additive multifidelity discrepancy models.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-scale additive discrepancy model for two fidelity levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An additive discrepancy model relates low- and high-fidelity responses by \[f_H(x)=\rho f_L(x)+\delta(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\] where \(\rho\in\mathbb R\) is a scale parameter and \(\delta:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is the discrepancy. If \(f_L\sim\mathcal{GP}(m_L,k_L)\), \(\delta\sim\mathcal{GP}(m_\delta,k_\delta)\), and the two processes are independent, then \(f_H\) is Gaussian with mean \(\rho m_L+m_\delta\) and covariance \[k_H(x,x')=\rho^2k_L(x,x')+k_\delta(x,x').\] The special case \(\rho=1\) models the high-fidelity response as the low-fidelity response plus a correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The high-fidelity response equals a scaled low-fidelity response plus an additive discrepancy, often modeled as an independent Gaussian process.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Discrepancy Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and Gaussian covariance formula fit the leaf, but no source supports the stated multifidelity discrepancy model.

children.title: Nonlinear Discrepancy Models
children.top_down_role: Source disagreement represented through nonlinear cross-source relations.

assumptions_latex: The lower-fidelity output is scalar-valued.
The linking map \(g:\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is assigned a deterministic or stochastic function model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_H(x)=g(x,f_L(x))\) permits nonlinear dependence on the low-fidelity response.
review_flags: Several nonlinear multifidelity model families exist; this record uses a nonlinear linking-function formulation.
No supplied source locator selects or supports this formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear linking-function formulation for two fidelity levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear discrepancy model represents the high-fidelity response as \[f_H(x)=g\bigl(x,f_L(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\] or, with a separate residual, as \[f_H(x)=g\bigl(x,f_L(x)\bigr)+\delta(x).\] Here \(g:\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is not restricted to be affine in its second argument. Accordingly, this family contains the additive model when \(g(x,z)=\rho z\) and the residual is \(\delta(x)\), but it also represents saturation, thresholds, and input-dependent transformations. If \(g\) is random, its prior and any residual prior must jointly determine a valid distribution over \(f_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear discrepancy model maps the input and low-fidelity output through a nonlinear linking function, optionally adding a residual correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Discrepancy Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition describes one valid nonlinear linking family, but the title does not uniquely select this formulation; a source is needed to establish the intended local meaning.

children.title: Input-Varying Discrepancy
children.top_down_role: Source disagreement whose magnitude or form varies across the domain.

assumptions_latex: Both fidelities are defined on a common domain \(\mathcal X\).
The scale function \(\rho\) and residual discrepancy \(\delta\) are estimable from multifidelity observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_H(x)=\rho(x)f_L(x)+\delta(x)\) allows the fidelity relation to vary over \(\mathcal X\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports input-varying multifidelity discrepancy models.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-varying scale and correction in a two-fidelity discrepancy relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An input-varying discrepancy relation has the form \[f_H(x)=\rho(x)f_L(x)+\delta(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\] where \(\rho:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and \(\delta:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are functions rather than constant parameters. The local discrepancy relative to the unscaled low-fidelity response is therefore \[d(x)=f_H(x)-f_L(x)=\bigl(\rho(x)-1\bigr)f_L(x)+\delta(x).\] This model permits the sign and magnitude of fidelity association to change across the design domain. Constant-scale additive discrepancy is recovered when \(\rho(x)\equiv\rho_0\). Priors or constraints on \(\rho\) and \(\delta\) are required to regularize their otherwise confounded contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Input-varying discrepancy models let both fidelity scaling and residual correction change across the design domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Input-Varying Discrepancy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The input-varying relation and identifiability warning fit the leaf, but neither is supported by a cited source.

children.title: Discrepancy Extrapolation Risk
children.top_down_role: Target-prediction sensitivity outside regions supported by paired source data.

assumptions_latex: High-fidelity observations occur only on a proper subset \(S\subsetneq\mathcal X\).
The discrepancy model is learned from paired fidelity data on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement of discrepancy functions on \(S\) does not identify their values on \(\mathcal X\setminus S\) without structural restrictions.

notation.meaning: region containing paired high- and low-fidelity observations

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports discrepancy extrapolation risk.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonidentifiability of discrepancy outside the paired-observation region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subsetneq\mathcal X\) contain every input with a paired high- and low-fidelity observation. Choose a nonzero function \(h:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(h(x)=0\) for all \(x\in S\), and define \(\delta_2=\delta_1+h\). Under the additive relations \(f_H=\rho f_L+\delta_j\), the two discrepancy models make identical noiseless predictions at every paired input in \(S\), yet differ wherever \(h\neq0\). Therefore the data on \(S\) alone cannot identify discrepancy values on \(\mathcal X\setminus S\). Reliable extrapolation requires additional restrictions, such as a justified kernel, smoothness class, parametric form, or high-fidelity coverage of the target region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired data identify discrepancy only where collected; outside that region, distinct corrections can fit all observations yet imply different high-fidelity responses.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrepancy Extrapolation Risk

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonidentifiability construction appropriately captures extrapolation risk, but it has no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Continuous-Fidelity Models
children.top_down_role: Joint models over design variables and continuous fidelity controls.

assumptions_latex: The fidelity variable lies in a continuous set \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^p\).
The kernel \(K\) is positive semidefinite on \((\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z)^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Gaussian process on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\) jointly interpolates or predicts across inputs and continuous fidelities.

notation.meaning: design input and continuous fidelity control

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports continuous-fidelity Gaussian-process models.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint Gaussian-process representation over design and continuous fidelity variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous-fidelity surrogate represents evaluations as a single random function \[f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R,\qquad f\sim\mathcal{GP}(m,K),\] where \(z\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) controls fidelity or computational resource. For any finite \(((x_i,z_i))_{i=1}^n\), the response vector is Gaussian with mean \(m(x_i,z_i)\) and covariance \(K((x_i,z_i),(x_j,z_j))\). A separable instance is \[K((x,z),(x',z'))=k_x(x,x')k_z(z,z'),\] with positive-semidefinite kernels \(k_x\) and \(k_z\). The highest-fidelity objective is a designated slice \(x\mapsto f(x,z_H)\), while observations at other \(z\) inform that slice through \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous-fidelity model places one surrogate over the product of design inputs and continuously valued fidelity controls.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Fidelity Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the topic role and clearly defines a product-domain Gaussian process, but no source supports this continuous-fidelity formulation.

children.title: Input-Dependent Fidelity Models
children.top_down_role: Source quality allowed to vary across the design domain.

assumptions_latex: Source \(s\) and the target response are defined on a common domain \(\mathcal X\).
The source-target relation is permitted to vary with \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Input-dependent cross-covariance or scaling represents source quality that changes across \(\mathcal X\).
review_flags: Several input-dependent fidelity model families exist; this record uses varying source scaling and discrepancy.
No supplied source locator selects or supports this formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Source quality modeled by spatially varying scaling and residual uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source \(s\), an input-dependent fidelity model may represent the target as \[f_0(x)=\rho_s(x)f_s(x)+\delta_s(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X.\] The function \(\rho_s:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) describes local association with the target, while \(\delta_s\) describes remaining local bias or uncertainty. If \(f_s\) and \(\delta_s\) are independent zero-mean processes, then \[\operatorname{Cov}(f_0(x),f_s(x'))=\rho_s(x)\operatorname{Cov}(f_s(x),f_s(x')).\] Hence source informativeness can be strong in one region and weak or sign-reversed in another. A globally constant fidelity relation is recovered when \(\rho_s(x)\) is constant and the discrepancy law is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Source quality can vary by location through input-dependent scaling, cross-covariance, or discrepancy rather than a single global fidelity ranking.
knowledge_statements.title: Input-Dependent Fidelity Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the stated topic role, but it selects one of several input-dependent fidelity families without a source establishing that choice or its concluding global-relation characterization.

children.title: Multi-Fidelity Acquisition Families
children.top_down_role: Policies selecting both a design point and an information source.

children.title: Improvement-Based Fidelity Selection
children.top_down_role: Improvement utilities adapted to source cost and target relevance.

knowledge_statements.title: Improvement-Based Fidelity Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost- and relevance-weighted expected improvement for minimization with multiple fidelities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the target fidelity be \(L\), let \(\tau_n\) be the best target value observed by stage \(n\), and let \(F_\ell(x)\) have the current marginal posterior at source \(\ell\). For positive cost \(c_\ell(x)\) and target-relevance weight \(r_\ell(x)\in[0,1]\), define
\[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{IEI}}(x,\ell)=\frac{r_\ell(x)}{c_\ell(x)}\,\mathbb E_n[(\tau_n-F_\ell(x))_+].\]
Select \((x_{n+1},\ell_{n+1})\in\arg\max_{(x,\ell)\in\mathcal X\times\{1,\ldots,L\}}\alpha_n^{\mathrm{IEI}}(x,\ell)\), observe that source, update the joint posterior, and stop when the remaining budget is below every feasible query cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the feasible source-location pair maximizing expected improvement weighted by target relevance and divided by evaluation cost.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\) and the displayed argmax is attained.
\(c_\ell(x)>0\) for every feasible query.
The source outputs are placed on a common minimization scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{n+1},\ell_{n+1})\) maximizes relevance-adjusted expected improvement per unit cost.

notation.meaning: best observed target-fidelity value at stage n
posterior relevance of source l to the target at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the relevance-weighted, cost-normalized improvement rule is model-dependent and has no cited source defining or supporting it.

children.title: Knowledge-Gradient Fidelity Selection
children.top_down_role: Source selection through expected terminal decision value.

knowledge_statements.title: Knowledge-Gradient Fidelity Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step, cost-sensitive knowledge gradient based on terminal target-fidelity decision value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_n^L(x)=\mathbb E_n[F_L(x)]\) be the target-fidelity posterior mean and define the current terminal value for minimization by \(V_n=-\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu_n^L(x)\). For a prospective observation \(Y_\ell(x)\), let \(V_{n+1}(x,\ell)=-\min_{z\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E_n[F_L(z)\mid Y_\ell(x)]\). Define
\[\operatorname{KG}_n(x,\ell)=\mathbb E_n[V_{n+1}(x,\ell)]-V_n.\]
With query cost \(c_\ell(x)>0\), select a feasible maximizer of \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x,\ell)/c_\ell(x)\), observe \(Y_\ell(x)\), and update the joint posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Query the source-location pair with the largest expected increase in terminal target decision value per unit cost.
assumptions_latex: The posterior expectations and minima defining \(V_n\) and \(V_{n+1}\) are finite.
The posterior jointly models every source with the target fidelity.
A maximizer exists over the feasible query set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected query maximizes one-step expected terminal decision-value gain per unit cost.

notation.meaning: prospective observation from source l at x

source_refs.locator: 7.4 The Knowledge Gradient Algorithm for Discrete Alternatives p. 262

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 The Knowledge Gradient Algorithm for Discrete Alternatives p. 262

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited discrete-alternative knowledge-gradient section does not directly support the stated continuous, cost-sensitive multifidelity extension. A direct source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Information-Directed Fidelity Selection
children.top_down_role: Source selection through information about target optima or optimal values.

children.title: Entropy-Reduction Fidelity Selection
children.top_down_role: Fidelity choice based on expected reduction in target uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-Reduction Fidelity Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-normalized expected posterior entropy reduction for a chosen target decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) be a target decision variable with posterior law \(p_n\), such as the target optimizer or optimal value, and suppose its entropy \(H_n(Z)\) is finite. For a prospective source observation \(Y_\ell(x)\), define
\[\alpha_n^{H}(x,\ell)=\frac{H_n(Z)-\mathbb E_n[H_n(Z\mid Y_\ell(x))]}{c_\ell(x)}.\]
At stage \(n\), select any feasible \((x_{n+1},\ell_{n+1})\) maximizing \(\alpha_n^{H}\), acquire the observation, and update the posterior. The numerator is the expected reduction in uncertainty about \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the affordable query producing the greatest expected entropy reduction about the target decision variable per unit cost.
assumptions_latex: The prior and conditional entropies of \(Z\) exist and are finite.
\(c_\ell(x)>0\) for every feasible query.
The displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected query maximizes expected posterior entropy reduction per unit cost.

notation.meaning: target optimizer, target optimal value, or another terminal decision variable

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and container are compatible, but no source supports this cost-normalized multifidelity entropy-reduction acquisition rule.

children.title: Mutual-Information Fidelity Selection
children.top_down_role: Fidelity choice based on dependence between observations and target quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Mutual-Information Fidelity Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information form of information-directed source selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a target variable \(Z\) and a prospective observation \(Y_\ell(x)\), conditional on stage-\(n\) data \(\mathcal D_n\), the query information is
\[I_n(Z;Y_\ell(x))=H_n(Z)-\mathbb E_n[H_n(Z\mid Y_\ell(x))]=D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(p_n^{Z,Y_\ell(x)}\,\middle\|\,p_n^Zp_n^{Y_\ell(x)}\right).\]
Thus a cost-sensitive information-directed rule selects a feasible maximizer of \(I_n(Z;Y_\ell(x))/c_\ell(x)\). The value is nonnegative and equals zero exactly when \(Z\) and \(Y_\ell(x)\) are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal D_n\), subject to existence of the displayed quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected entropy reduction equals conditional mutual information, so fidelity selection can maximize information about the target per unit cost.
assumptions_latex: The relevant conditional distributions admit the displayed entropies or Kullback--Leibler divergence.
\(c_\ell(x)>0\) for every feasible query.
Conditioning is on the current data \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The entropy-reduction numerator equals \(I_n(Z;Y_\ell(x))\), and it vanishes precisely under conditional independence.

notation.meaning: mutual information conditional on current data
current posterior marginal law of Z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mutual-information representation is standard and appropriately classified, but no inspectable citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Target-Optimizer Information
children.top_down_role: Selection criteria focused on uncertainty about the target optimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Optimizer Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information gained about the optimizer of the highest-fidelity latent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_L:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the random target-fidelity objective and fix a measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the target optimizer by
\[X_\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}F_L(x).\]
For a prospective observation \(Y_\ell(x)\), its target-optimizer information at stage \(n\) is
\[\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(x,\ell)=I(X_\star;Y_\ell(x)\mid\mathcal D_n).\]
When the conditional entropies exist, this equals \(H(X_\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_n[H(X_\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_\ell(x))]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-optimizer information is the conditional mutual information between a prospective source observation and the target objective's minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The target objective has a measurable minimizer after tie-breaking.
The conditional mutual information is well defined.
\(Y_\ell(x)\) is jointly modeled with \(F_L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(x,\ell)\) quantifies the query's expected information about \(X_\star\).

notation.meaning: tie-broken minimizer of the target-fidelity objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A direct source is required. The displayed argmin is ordinarily set-valued despite the stated tie-breaking rule; a sourced version should explicitly define the measurable selected minimizer.

children.title: Target-Value Information
children.top_down_role: Selection criteria focused on uncertainty about the optimal target value.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Value Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information gained about the optimum value of the highest-fidelity latent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_L:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the random target-fidelity objective and assume its minimum is measurable and finite. Define the target optimum value by
\[F_\star=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}F_L(x).\]
For a prospective observation \(Y_\ell(x)\), its target-value information at stage \(n\) is
\[\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{val}}(x,\ell)=I(F_\star;Y_\ell(x)\mid\mathcal D_n).\]
Whenever the conditional entropies exist, this equals \(H(F_\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_n[H(F_\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_\ell(x))]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-value information is the conditional mutual information between a prospective source observation and the target objective's minimum value.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\star\) is measurable and finite almost surely.
The conditional mutual information is well defined.
\(Y_\ell(x)\) is jointly modeled with \(F_L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{val}}(x,\ell)\) quantifies the query's expected information about \(F_\star\).

notation.meaning: minimum value of the target-fidelity objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but it lacks an inspectable source for target-optimum-value information.

children.title: Bound-Based Source Screening
children.top_down_role: Fidelity allocation through uncertainty bounds and source screening.

children.title: Confidence-Bound Fidelity Allocation
children.top_down_role: Fidelity allocation governed by uncertainty bounds on target quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Bound Fidelity Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allocation by optimistic target bounds corrected for fidelity discrepancy and query cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimization, suppose source \(\ell\) has posterior mean \(\mu_{n,\ell}(x)\), standard deviation \(s_{n,\ell}(x)\), and a deterministic target-discrepancy bound \(\zeta_\ell(x)\) satisfying \(|F_L(x)-F_\ell(x)|\leq\zeta_\ell(x)\). Define the target lower confidence bound
\[B_{n,\ell}^{-}(x)=\mu_{n,\ell}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_n}s_{n,\ell}(x)-\zeta_\ell(x).\]
Among queries surviving the source-screening rule, allocate the next evaluation to a feasible minimizer of \(B_{n,\ell}^{-}(x)\), with ties resolved by smaller cost. Update all posterior bounds after observing the selected source.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the surviving source-location pair with the most optimistic discrepancy-corrected lower confidence bound, breaking ties by cost.
assumptions_latex: The simultaneous confidence event \(|F_\ell(x)-\mu_{n,\ell}(x)|\leq\sqrt{\beta_n}s_{n,\ell}(x)\) holds on the screened domain.
\(|F_L(x)-F_\ell(x)|\leq\zeta_\ell(x)\).
A feasible minimizing query exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On the confidence event, \(B_{n,\ell}^{-}(x)\leq F_L(x)\) for every screened pair.

notation.meaning: target lower confidence bound induced by source l

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The discrepancy-corrected lower bound is coherent on the stated confidence event, but the resulting multifidelity allocation algorithm has no direct source.

children.title: Source-Screening Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies that restrict source use according to informativeness or reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Source-Screening Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe elimination of source-location queries whose optimistic target bounds cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_{n,\ell}(x)\) be a valid lower confidence bound on the target value inferred from source \(\ell\) at \(x\), and let \(U_n^{\mathrm{inc}}\) be a valid upper confidence bound on the value of an incumbent target design. For minimization, retain
\[\mathcal S_n=\{(x,\ell):L_{n,\ell}(x)\leq U_n^{\mathrm{inc}}-\varepsilon_n\},\]
where \(\varepsilon_n\geq0\) is a screening margin. Discard pairs outside \(\mathcal S_n\), apply the chosen acquisition rule within \(\mathcal S_n\), and restore all feasible pairs if \(\mathcal S_n\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Screen out queries whose optimistic target bound is already worse than the incumbent bound by the prescribed margin.
assumptions_latex: The lower and upper bounds hold simultaneously on an event \(E_n\).
\(\varepsilon_n\geq0\).
The optimization problem is posed as minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(E_n\), every discarded pair satisfies \(F_L(x)>F_L(x_n^{\mathrm{inc}})-\varepsilon_n\).

notation.meaning: set of queries retained after screening
upper confidence bound for the incumbent target value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The screening implication follows from the stated simultaneous bounds, but the proposed screening and empty-set restoration policy is uncited and appears constructed from the node role.

children.title: Fidelity-Escalation Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing movement toward more expensive fidelity levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Fidelity-Escalation Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold condition for replacing a cheap source by a more accurate, more expensive fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Order fidelities so that \(c_1(x)\leq\cdots\leq c_L(x)\), and let \(w_{n,\ell}(x)\) denote the half-width of a target confidence interval inferred from source \(\ell\). Given thresholds \(\gamma_{n,\ell}(x)\geq0\), escalation from \(\ell<L\) to \(\ell+1\) at \(x\) is triggered exactly when
\[w_{n,\ell}(x)\leq\gamma_{n,\ell}(x)\quad\text{and}\quad (x,\ell)\text{ remains competitive under target bounds}.\]
Otherwise the policy continues sampling fidelity \(\ell\), screens \(x\), or terminates it according to the surrounding allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalate only after the current fidelity is sufficiently resolved and the design remains competitive for the target objective.
assumptions_latex: Fidelities are ordered by nondecreasing cost.
\(w_{n,\ell}(x)\geq0\) is a valid target-interval half-width.
Competitiveness is decided by a specified simultaneous-bound rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conjunction is the fidelity-escalation predicate at \((x,\ell)\).

notation.meaning: target confidence-interval half-width induced by the current fidelity
cost of fidelity l at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the threshold family is policy-dependent, the competitiveness predicate is not defined mathematically, and no canonical source is cited.

children.title: Screening-Error Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where useful sources or candidates are removed prematurely.

knowledge_statements.title: Screening-Error Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating confidence-safe screening from possible elimination of the target optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_\star\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal X}F_L(x)\). A lower-bound screening rule discards \(x\) when \(L_n(x)>U_n^{\mathrm{inc}}-\varepsilon_n\). On the simultaneous validity event
\[E_n=\{L_n(x)\leq F_L(x)\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\quad F_L(x_n^{\mathrm{inc}})\leq U_n^{\mathrm{inc}}\},\]
the optimizer can be discarded only if \(F_L(x_n^{\mathrm{inc}})-F_L(x_\star)<\varepsilon_n\). Consequently, exact safe screening requires \(\varepsilon_n=0\); with positive margin, protection extends only to designs whose target improvement over the incumbent is at least \(\varepsilon_n\). Outside \(E_n\), no such guarantee follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid zero-margin bounds cannot screen the optimizer; a positive margin may remove any design improving the incumbent by less than that margin.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimization and \(x_\star\) is a target optimizer.
Screening uses \(L_n(x)>U_n^{\mathrm{inc}}-\varepsilon_n\).
The simultaneous validity event \(E_n\) occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding \(x_\star\) implies \(F_L(x_n^{\mathrm{inc}})-F_L(x_\star)<\varepsilon_n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification and stated implication are coherent, but the result has no source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Progressive Evaluation Optimization
children.top_down_role: Evaluations revealing intermediate performance as resources accumulate.

children.title: Trace Observations
children.top_down_role: Intermediate outcomes exposed by progressive evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Trace Observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtration-compatible intermediate outputs from an evaluation indexed by consumed resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a design \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(R\subseteq[0,R_{\max}]\) be ordered resource levels. A trace observation from one progressive evaluation is a finite collection
\[\mathcal T(x)=\{(r_j,Y(x,r_j)):0<r_1<\cdots<r_k\leq R_{\max}\},\]
where \(Y(x,r_j)\) is measurable with respect to the evaluation history through resource \(r_j\). The same run may subsequently produce observations at larger resource levels. A terminal observation is the special case \(r_j=R_{\max}\); earlier elements are intermediate outcomes rather than independent reevaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trace is the ordered sequence of measurable intermediate outcomes exposed by one evaluation as its consumed resource increases.
assumptions_latex: Resource levels are totally ordered and bounded by \(R_{\max}\).
Each intermediate outcome is observable when its resource level is reached.
Observations sharing a trace belong to the same evaluation run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T(x)\) is an ordered, filtration-compatible record of progressive evaluation outcomes.

notation.meaning: resource consumed at the j-th observation
intermediate outcome at design x and resource level r_j
trace generated by one progressive evaluation

source_refs.locator: 3.1.1 Observations and data in stochastic optimization p. 62

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.1 Observations and data in stochastic optimization p. 62

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the cited general observations section does not directly establish progressive, same-run trace observations or their filtration-compatible formulation.

children.title: Learning-Curve Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Forecasting terminal performance from partial trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Learning-Curve Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior prediction of terminal performance from a partially observed resource trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a learning curve satisfy \(Y(x,r)=g(r;\theta_x)+\epsilon(x,r)\) for resource \(r\in[0,R_{\max}]\), with prior \(p(\theta_x)\) and specified noise law. Given a partial trace \(\mathcal T_k(x)=\{(r_j,y_j)\}_{j=1}^k\), the posterior terminal predictive distribution is
\[p(Y(x,R_{\max})\mid\mathcal T_k(x))=\int p(Y(x,R_{\max})\mid\theta_x)\,p(\theta_x\mid\mathcal T_k(x))\,d\theta_x.\]
A point extrapolation may be the posterior mean, while posterior quantiles provide uncertainty bounds; both must condition on the same observed partial trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infer curve parameters from the partial trace, then integrate their posterior uncertainty to predict terminal performance and credible bounds.
assumptions_latex: The curve family \(g(r;\theta_x)\), parameter prior, and observation-noise law are specified.
The terminal predictive integral exists.
The partial trace is observed at increasing resource levels below or equal to \(R_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed posterior predictive law represents terminal performance conditional on the observed learning curve.

notation.meaning: parametric learning curve for design x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A direct learning-curve extrapolation source is required. The displayed predictive factorization additionally assumes that terminal performance is conditionally independent of the partial trace given the curve parameter, which is not stated and need not follow from an arbitrary noise law.

children.title: Resumable Evaluation Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Resource allocation with reusable partial computation.

children.title: Pausable Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Evaluations whose resource consumption can be interrupted.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathcal X\) is a configuration and \(r\in[0,R]\) is consumed resource.
An evaluation has observable state \(S_x(r)\) and trace \(Y_x(r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pausing at \(r\) returns \((S_x(r),Y_x|_{[0,r]})\) without requiring completion to \(R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pausing as interruption with a recoverable state, independently of whether later continuation is supported.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a configuration \(x\in\mathcal X\), let an evaluation evolve over resource levels \(r\in[0,R]\), with state \(S_x(r)\) and observation trace \(Y_x(r)\). The evaluation is pausable if, at every admissible pause level \(r<R\), an interrupt operation terminates current resource consumption in finite time and returns a checkpoint \(S_x(r)\) together with the available trace \(Y_x|_{[0,r]}\), without first advancing the evaluation to \(R\). No continuation guarantee is included in this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pausable evaluation can be interrupted before maximum resource and yields its current checkpoint and observation trace without being forced to finish.
knowledge_statements.title: Pausable Evaluations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Pausable Evaluations leaf, distinguishes pausing from continuation, introduces its notation, and contains properly delimited TeX. However, no citation is supplied for the domain-specific checkpoint and finite-interruption semantics, so the candidate requires an inspectable source with a specific locator.

children.title: Resumable Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Interrupted evaluations that can continue from preserved state.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathcal X\) has been paused at resource \(r<R\).
The saved checkpoint is \(S_x(r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuation from \(S_x(r)\) reproduces the conditional law of uninterrupted future outputs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses distributional equivalence, allowing stochastic evaluations as well as deterministic ones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A paused evaluation of \(x\in\mathcal X\) at resource \(r<R\) is resumable if, for every target level \(r'\in(r,R]\), a continuation initialized from \(S_x(r)\) produces the future trace \(Y_x|_{(r,r']}\) with the same conditional distribution, given \(S_x(r)\), as an uninterrupted evaluation continued from \(r\) to \(r'\). In the deterministic case, equality in conditional distribution reduces to equality of the continued state and trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resumable evaluation continues from its saved state and has the same future behavior as an uninterrupted run, conditionally on that state.
knowledge_statements.title: Resumable Evaluations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Resumable Evaluations leaf and consistently handles deterministic and stochastic evaluations through conditional-law equivalence. An authoritative source is required to support this particular state-conditional resumption criterion and its deterministic specialization.

children.title: Checkpoint Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of intermediate evaluation state across allocation decisions.

assumptions_latex: A checkpoint \(S_x(r)\) from configuration \(x\) is available.
The resumed target resource satisfies \(r'>r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reusable checkpoints reduce incremental cost from \(C_x(r')\) to \(C_x(r')-C_x(r)+H_x(r,r')\).

notation.meaning: cost of an uninterrupted run to resource r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exact reuse by state sufficiency and gives its incremental resource accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checkpoint \(S_x(r)\) is reusable for continuation to \(r'>r\) when it contains every state component required by the transition law beyond \(r\), so that resumption has the same conditional future-output law as uninterrupted execution. If \(C_x(r)\) is cumulative uninterrupted cost and \(H_x(r,r')\geq0\) is loading and synchronization overhead, then reusable continuation incurs incremental cost \(C_x(r')-C_x(r)+H_x(r,r')\), rather than \(C_x(r')\) for a fresh run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable checkpoint is sufficient for correct continuation and replaces full rerun cost by the remaining resource cost plus restart overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Checkpoint Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is locally relevant, but the exact incremental-cost formula presumes that cumulative uninterrupted cost is additively separable between resource levels and that checkpoint overhead is the only additional cost. Those modeling assumptions and the state-sufficiency characterization need a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Restart Overhead
children.top_down_role: Time and resource penalties associated with interrupted computation.

assumptions_latex: A saved evaluation at resource \(r\) is resumed toward \(r'>r\).
All costs are measured in one nonnegative resource unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Checkpoint reuse is resource-beneficial exactly when \(H_x(r,r')<C_x(r)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates fixed restart overhead from the remaining computation required after a checkpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuation from resource \(r\) to \(r'>r\), define restart overhead \(H_x(r,r')\geq0\) by \(C_x^{\mathrm{resume}}(r,r')=C_x(r')-C_x(r)+H_x(r,r')\). Relative to restarting from resource zero at cost \(C_x(r')\), checkpoint reuse yields a strict resource saving if and only if \(H_x(r,r')<C_x(r)\); equality gives no saving, and \(H_x(r,r')>C_x(r)\) makes a fresh restart cheaper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart overhead is checkpoint loading and synchronization cost; reuse is worthwhile exactly when this overhead is smaller than the work already saved.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given the stated cost identity, the saving condition follows algebraically and the condition content kind fits Restart Overhead. The underlying additive restart-cost model is nevertheless domain-specific and uncited, so an inspectable source is required before this candidate can pass review.

children.title: Early-Termination Policies
children.top_down_role: Stopping individual evaluations before maximum fidelity.

assumptions_latex: There are active evaluations \(i\in\mathcal I_t\) with traces \(D_{i,t}\).
Each continuation has cost \(c_{i,t}>0\) and utility score \(U_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy terminates evaluation \(i\) when \(U_{i,t}/c_{i,t}\leq\tau_t\).

notation.meaning: active evaluation set at decision time t
posterior utility of continuing evaluation i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a generic posterior utility-per-cost stopping rule rather than a named early-stopping method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At decision time \(t\), for each active evaluation \(i\in\mathcal I_t\), update its posterior from trace data \(D_{i,t}\). Compute the posterior expected utility \(U_{i,t}\geq0\) of continuing to the next fidelity and its incremental cost \(c_{i,t}>0\). Given threshold \(\tau_t\geq0\), terminate \(i\) permanently when \(U_{i,t}/c_{i,t}\leq\tau_t\); otherwise allocate the next resource increment. Stop when the budget is exhausted or \(\mathcal I_t\) is empty, and return all completed or retained observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each resource checkpoint, terminate an evaluation when its posterior benefit from another increment, divided by that increment's cost, falls below a threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Early-Termination Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the Early-Termination Policies topic, but the proposed utility-per-cost threshold rule is one particular policy rather than a canonical definition of the topic. The meaning and horizon of the posterior utility are not mathematically specified, and no source supports the rule, threshold, or terminal return behavior.

children.title: Adaptive Source Validation
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics and decision families governing whether auxiliary sources should continue to influence target search.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Unreliable Information Sources
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Unreliable Information Sources

children.title: Source Discrepancy Assessment
children.top_down_role: Assessment of source-to-target agreement across the search domain.

assumptions_latex: The target response is \(f_0:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\).
Source \(s\) has response \(f_s:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\).
Assessment uses a probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_s(\mu)=\left(\int_{\mathcal X}(f_s(x)-f_0(x))^2\,d\mu(x)\right)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects root-mean-square source error; other discrepancy functionals may be preferable for ranking-only transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_s\in L^2(\mathcal X,\mu)\), where \(f_0\) is the target response, \(f_s\) is auxiliary source \(s\), and \(\mu\) weights regions of the search domain. The global source-to-target discrepancy is \[D_s(\mu)=\left(\int_{\mathcal X}\lvert f_s(x)-f_0(x)\rvert^2\,d\mu(x)\right)^{1/2}.\] For paired noisy observations, the corresponding posterior assessment is the posterior distribution or posterior expectation of this functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Source discrepancy is the root-mean-square difference between an auxiliary response and the target response over a specified distribution on the search domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Source Discrepancy Assessment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The L2 discrepancy is mathematically well formed and appropriate as one possible source-discrepancy assessment, with consistent plain text and TeX. It is not uniquely determined by the leaf title, and the extension to posterior assessment is uncited; a source must justify this specific functional and interpretation.

children.title: Adaptive Source Suppression
children.top_down_role: Adaptive rejection or reduced use of misleading sources.

children.title: Hard Source Elimination
children.top_down_role: Permanent or conditional removal of an auxiliary source.

assumptions_latex: At time \(t\), source \(s\) has posterior discrepancy risk \(R_{s,t}\).
A rejection threshold \(\eta_t\) is fixed.
