knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_{s,t}>\eta_t\), then \(s\) is excluded from all subsequent source selections.

notation.meaning: posterior risk that source s is unacceptable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes irreversible elimination; reversible suppression belongs under source reentry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the active set as \(\mathcal S_0=\mathcal S\). At validation time \(t\), compute for each \(s\in\mathcal S_t\) a posterior discrepancy risk \(R_{s,t}\in[0,1]\). Given \(\eta_t\in[0,1]\), update \(\mathcal S_{t+1}=\{s\in\mathcal S_t:R_{s,t}\leq\eta_t\}\). Acquisition and posterior updates after time \(t\) may use only sources in \(\mathcal S_{t+1}\). The rule is hard elimination because every removed source remains unavailable at all later times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard elimination irreversibly removes any source whose posterior discrepancy risk exceeds a specified validation threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard Source Elimination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The irreversible active-set update fits Hard Source Elimination and is correctly classified as an algorithm. However, the event represented by the posterior discrepancy risk is not defined, and no citation supports the threshold policy or its use in Bayesian multi-source optimization.

children.title: Soft Source Downweighting
children.top_down_role: Reduced influence for sources judged less reliable or informative.

assumptions_latex: Source \(s\) has posterior discrepancy risk \(R_{s,t}\in[0,1]\).
Its unsuppressed acquisition value is \(a_{s,t}(x)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Source selection uses \(\widetilde a_{s,t}(x)=w_{s,t}a_{s,t}(x)\) with \(w_{s,t}=g(R_{s,t})\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers continuous attenuation of acquisition value while retaining every source as selectable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a nonincreasing mapping \(g:[0,1]\to[0,1]\). At each validation time \(t\), compute \(R_{s,t}\) and set \(w_{s,t}=g(R_{s,t})\). Replace the source acquisition value \(a_{s,t}(x)\) by \(\widetilde a_{s,t}(x)=w_{s,t}a_{s,t}(x)\), then select a source-location pair maximizing the adjusted acquisition per cost. Because \(w_{s,t}\) may subsequently increase and need not equal zero, the source is downweighted rather than irreversibly eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft downweighting multiplies each source's acquisition value by a reliability weight that decreases with posterior discrepancy risk and can later recover.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft Source Downweighting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches Soft Source Downweighting, but an arbitrary nonincreasing mapping g is not source-supported. Moreover, allowing g to attain zero does not ensure that every source remains effectively selectable, so the scope note overstates the stated rule. A source is needed to determine the intended weighting assumptions and acquisition policy.

children.title: Source Reentry Criteria
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which a previously restricted source regains influence.

assumptions_latex: Source \(s\) is currently suppressed.
New paired validation data produce posterior risk \(R_{s,t}\).
Reentry threshold \(\eta_{\mathrm{in}}\) is below rejection threshold \(\eta_{\mathrm{out}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Source \(s\) reenters when \(R_{s,t}\leq\eta_{\mathrm{in}}\) and validation support is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses hysteresis and minimum validation support to prevent rapid switching of source availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let suppressed source \(s\) receive new paired validation evidence, yielding posterior discrepancy risk \(R_{s,t}\) and effective validation size \(n_{s,t}^{\mathrm{eff}}\). For thresholds \(0\leq\eta_{\mathrm{in}}<\eta_{\mathrm{out}}\leq1\) and \(n_{\min}\geq1\), reenter \(s\) into the active set exactly when \(R_{s,t}\leq\eta_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(n_{s,t}^{\mathrm{eff}}\geq n_{\min}\). The strict threshold separation supplies hysteresis relative to suppression at risk above \(\eta_{\mathrm{out}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suppressed source reenters only after enough new validation evidence lowers its discrepancy risk below a stricter recovery threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Source Reentry Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind and hysteresis structure fit Source Reentry Criteria. The effective validation sample size is not defined, and the exact conjunction of risk and sample-size thresholds is a proposed calibration rule with no supporting citation.

children.title: Premature Source Rejection
children.top_down_role: Loss of useful information caused by early elimination or excessive downweighting.

assumptions_latex: A source is eliminated when an estimated discrepancy exceeds a threshold.
Validation observations are noisy and finite.
Elimination is irreversible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For any finite validation size, a useful source can be rejected with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies finite-sample false rejection as the principal failure of irreversible source suppression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a useful source satisfies \(D_s<\delta\), but hard elimination rejects it when \(\widehat D_{s,n}>\delta\). If the finite-sample estimator has nondegenerate noise with \(\mathbb P(\widehat D_{s,n}>\delta\mid D_s)>0\), then the source is permanently rejected with positive probability despite being acceptable. Thus irreversible thresholding without calibrated uncertainty control or reentry cannot guarantee retention of every useful source at any fixed finite validation size \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With noisy finite validation, irreversible thresholding can discard a genuinely useful source because its estimated discrepancy crosses the rejection threshold by chance.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Source Rejection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification fits Premature Source Rejection, and the positive-probability conclusion is valid under the explicitly assumed tail probability. A source is still required for treating this construction as a recognized failure phenomenon of irreversible source suppression in the target domain.

children.title: Unreliable Low-Fidelity Sources
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary information whose bias outweighs its cost advantage.

assumptions_latex: Source \(s\) costs \(c_s>0\) per query.
Target queries cost \(c_0>0\).
Transfer utility is measured by \(V_s\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Source \(s\) is unreliable for allocation when \(V_s/c_s\leq V_0/c_0\), or when its transfer bias violates the prescribed tolerance.

notation.meaning: expected decision value of querying source s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines unreliability decision-theoretically, combining source discrepancy with information value per unit cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_s\) be the posterior expected improvement in the target decision produced by one query to low-fidelity source \(s\), and let \(c_s\) be its cost. Relative to a target query with value \(V_0\) and cost \(c_0\), source \(s\) is allocation-unreliable when \(V_s/c_s\leq V_0/c_0\). It is also transfer-unreliable under tolerance \(\delta\) when its assessed discrepancy satisfies \(D_s>\delta\), regardless of its smaller raw query cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-fidelity source is unreliable when its target-relevant value per cost is no better than a target query or its discrepancy exceeds tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Unreliable Low-Fidelity Sources

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record proposes two distinct sufficient labels for unreliability: inferior decision value per cost and excessive discrepancy. Neither the decision-value functional nor the relationship between these criteria is specified or cited, so the exact condition cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Fidelity Ordering Failures
children.top_down_role: Source orderings that change across the domain or fail to track accuracy.

children.title: Nonmonotone Fidelity Response
children.top_down_role: Accuracy or response quality that does not improve consistently with fidelity.

assumptions_latex: Fidelity is indexed by \(r\in[0,1]\), with target response \(f(x)=y(x,1)\).
The domain contains configurations \(x_1\) and \(x_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family \(y(x_1,r)=r\), \(y(x_2,r)=1-r\) has a fidelity crossing at \(r=1/2\).

notation.meaning: response at configuration x and fidelity r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-configuration construction showing that increasing fidelity need not preserve response order or improve every trace monotonically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,x_2\}\), \(r\in[0,1]\), \(y(x_1,r)=r\), and \(y(x_2,r)=1-r\). Then \(y(x_1,r)<y(x_2,r)\) for \(r<1/2\), equality holds at \(r=1/2\), and \(y(x_1,r)>y(x_2,r)\) for \(r>1/2\). Moreover, \(y(x_2,r)\) decreases with fidelity. Hence fidelity responses need not be pointwise nondecreasing, and low-fidelity rankings need not agree with the target ranking at \(r=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two linear fidelity traces crossing at one-half show both a decreasing response and reversal of the configuration ranking as fidelity increases.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Fidelity Response

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct, fully quantified, properly delimited, and fits Nonmonotone Fidelity Response: it exhibits both a decreasing trace and a ranking crossing. No citation or inspectable locator is supplied, however, so its use as candidate knowledge in this domain still requires a source.

children.title: Domain-Dependent Fidelity Crossings
children.top_down_role: Changes in relative source behavior across candidate locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Dependent Fidelity Crossings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise crossing criterion for deterministic source responses under a maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A domain-dependent fidelity crossing between sources \(i\) and \(j\) occurs when there exist \(x,x'\in X\) such that \(f_i(x)>f_j(x)\) and \(f_i(x')<f_j(x')\). Equivalently, \(f_i-f_j\) takes both positive and negative values on \(X\). Consequently, neither source has a domain-wide response ordering relative to the other; any ordering used for source selection must depend on the candidate location or on a specified subdomain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two fidelity sources cross when their response ordering reverses between design points, preventing either source from dominating throughout the domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty design domain.
\(f_i,f_j:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are deterministic source responses, with larger values preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x,x'\in X:\ f_i(x)>f_j(x)\land f_i(x')<f_j(x')\), so neither source dominates globally.

notation.meaning: Responses supplied by sources i and j

children.title: Local Source Orderings
children.top_down_role: Source rankings that remain valid only within restricted domain regions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is partitioned into nonempty regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\).
\(f_1,\ldots,f_s:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are source responses, with larger values preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each region \(R_k\) admits a source preorder even when no single preorder is valid on all of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Local regions forming the design-domain partition

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regionwise deterministic ordering; it does not assert that fidelity quality is globally monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of local source orderings is a collection of preorders \(\{\succeq_k\}_{k=1}^m\) such that, for every region \(R_k\) and sources \(i,j\), \(i\succeq_k j\) implies \(f_i(x)\ge f_j(x)\) for all \(x\in R_k\). The orderings are genuinely local when there exist \(k\ne \ell\) and sources \(i,j\) with \(i\succeq_k j\) and \(j\succeq_\ell i\), with at least one corresponding inequality strict somewhere in each region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local source ordering ranks sources consistently within each region while allowing the ranking to reverse across different regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Source Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regionwise preorder condition fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable citation supports this particular formalization of local source ordering.

children.title: Global Ranking Failure
children.top_down_role: Breakdown of a single fidelity ordering across the full search domain.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty design domain.
\(f_1,\ldots,f_s:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are source responses, with larger values preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No total preorder of the sources can represent their pointwise ordering on all of \(X\).

notation.meaning: Candidate global total preorder on sources

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a location-independent ranking induced by pointwise source responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global source ranking fails when no total preorder \(\succeq\) on \(\{1,\ldots,s\}\) satisfies \(i\succeq j\Rightarrow f_i(x)\ge f_j(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). A sufficient and pairwise sharp obstruction is the existence of sources \(i,j\) and points \(x,x'\in X\) for which \(f_i(x)>f_j(x)\) but \(f_i(x')<f_j(x')\). Any fixed ranking must then contradict the observed ordering at one of those points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global ranking is impossible when some pair of sources reverses order across the design domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Ranking Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise reversal obstruction and failure-boundary kind fit the container, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Parallel Bayesian Optimization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Resource allocation across simultaneous workers, pending observations, and heterogeneous evaluators.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Synchronous Batch Observations; Asynchronous Observation with Pending Experiments

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Asynchronous Batch Bayesian Optimisation with Improved Local Penalisation
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Asynchronous Batch Bayesian Optimisation with Improved Local Penalisation

children.title: Parallel Execution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Worker coordination patterns distinguished by when decisions are issued.

children.title: Synchronous Batches
children.top_down_role: Workers coordinated through batch barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Batches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronized parallel Bayesian optimization with a fixed batch size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the posterior from completed data \(D_0\). At round \(t\), select an ordered batch \(B_t=(x_{t,1},\ldots,x_{t,q})\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{B\in X^q}a_t(B)\). Dispatch all \(q\) evaluations and wait until every corresponding outcome \(y_{t,r}\) has returned. Set \(D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{(x_{t,r},y_{t,r}):1\le r\le q\}\), update the surrogate once at the batch barrier, and repeat until the declared evaluation, cost, or round budget is exhausted. No outcome from \(B_t\) is used to alter another member of that same batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each barrier, select and launch a complete batch, wait for every result, update the model once, and repeat without changing the batch using within-batch outcomes.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty design domain and \(q\ge1\) workers are available.
\(D_t\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}\) denotes the completed observations before round \(t\).
Completed observations are incorporated only at batch barriers.
\(a_t:X^q\to\mathbb{R}\) is the batch acquisition function, and its maximum over \(X^q\) is attained at every executed round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure produces complete batches \(B_t\) and never uses within-batch outcomes to alter the same batch.

notation.meaning: Completed observation set before round t
Ordered batch selected at round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the synchronous scheduling regime for parallel Bayesian optimization and distinguishes it from asynchronous redesign after individual completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Batch construction is synchronous when the results from the entire current batch are obtained before the next batch is designed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In synchronous batch construction, every experiment in the current batch must finish before the next batch is designed. By contrast, asynchronous construction may initiate a new experiment after an individual completion while other experiments remain pending.
assumptions_latex: \text{Multiple experiments can be executed in parallel.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{New experiments are designed only at completed-batch barriers.}

source_evidence.locator: Extensions and Related Settings / 11.3. Synchronous Batch Observations / Definition 11.3-extra-1

source_refs.locator: Extensions and Related Settings / 11.3. Synchronous Batch Observations / Definition 11.3-extra-1

children.title: Asynchronous Workers
children.top_down_role: New evaluations launched as workers become available.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Workers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven parallel Bayesian optimization with explicit tracking of pending evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize completed data \(D_0\) and fill up to \(q\) workers, recording their query points in the pending set \(P_0\). At completion event \(t\), let \((x_t^{\mathrm{ret}},y_t^{\mathrm{ret}})\) be the returned evaluation and define \(D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{(x_t^{\mathrm{ret}},y_t^{\mathrm{ret}})\}\) and \(P_t^-=P_t\setminus\{x_t^{\mathrm{ret}}\}\). Update the posterior using \(D_{t+1}\). If launching remains permitted, select \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X\setminus P_t^-}a_t(x;D_{t+1},P_t^-)\), dispatch it immediately on the idle worker, and set \(P_{t+1}=P_t^-\cup\{x_{t+1}\}\); otherwise set \(P_{t+1}=P_t^-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever an evaluation finishes, remove it from the pending set, update the posterior, and immediately launch a new pending-aware query if the budget permits.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty design domain and \(q\ge1\) workers may complete evaluations at different times.
\(D_t\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}\) and \(P_t\subseteq X\) are respectively the completed observations and pending query points before completion event \(t\).
\(a_t(x;D,P)\) is defined on eligible points, and every executed acquisition maximization attains a maximum.
The scheduler observes completion events and the current pending set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever a worker becomes idle and launching remains permitted, one new evaluation is dispatched without waiting for the other workers.

notation.meaning: Completed observation set before event t
Pending query set before event t
Pending set immediately after removing the completed query

children.title: Federated Evaluator Coordination
children.top_down_role: Evaluation resources separated by communication, data, or ownership boundaries.

children.title: Distributed Evaluator Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of evaluation resources across separate computational locations.

assumptions_latex: There are \(M\ge1\) evaluators with feasible sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_M\).
Evaluator \(m\) communicates only messages in an allowed class \(\mathcal{M}_m\).
The coordinator maintains shared state \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every dispatched query is evaluator-feasible and every coordinator update uses only admissible messages.

notation.meaning: Feasible query set of evaluator m
Allowed message class for evaluator m

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract coordinator protocol covering heterogeneous evaluators and restricted messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize shared state \(S_0\). At coordination event \(t\), the coordinator chooses evaluator \(m_t\) and query \(x_t\in X_{m_t}\) from \(S_t\), then dispatches \(x_t\). The evaluator computes locally and returns an admissible message \(z_t\in\mathcal{M}_{m_t}\), which may contain an observation or a permitted summary. The coordinator applies a specified update \(S_{t+1}=U_t(S_t,m_t,x_t,z_t)\). Events continue synchronously or asynchronously until the resource budget is exhausted; the coordinator outputs a decision measurable with respect to \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinator dispatches feasible queries to heterogeneous evaluators and updates shared state solely from their permitted messages.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Evaluator Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits distributed evaluator coordination, but this abstract protocol and its admissibility semantics are unsupported by any cited source.

children.title: Federated Data Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Optimization across evaluators that retain local data control.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated Data Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-flow boundary only; it does not by itself guarantee differential privacy or cryptographic secrecy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated data boundary is satisfied if, for every evaluator \(m\in\{1,\ldots,M\}\) and coordinator query \(r\), the transmitted message has the form \(z_m=T_m(D_m,r)\in\mathcal{Z}_m\), while raw records in \(D_m\) remain local. Every coordinator update must depend only on the prior transcript, public information, received messages, and any declared coordinator randomness. Under deterministic coordination, or conditional on the same coordinator random seed, two collections of local datasets that produce identical permitted disclosures for every issued query induce identical coordinator transcripts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local records remain with their owners, and coordination uses only declared disclosures; with coordinator randomness fixed, identical disclosures produce identical transcripts.
assumptions_latex: There are \(M\ge1\) evaluators, and evaluator \(m\) owns a local dataset \(D_m\).
A disclosure map \(T_m\) and admissible message space \(\mathcal{Z}_m\) are fixed for each evaluator.
The coordinator is deterministic or its random seed is included among the conditioned public inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditional on the same coordinator randomness, the transcript reveals only prescribed values \(T_m(D_m,r)\), not unrestricted local records.

notation.meaning: Private dataset owned by evaluator m

children.title: Communication-Limited Search
children.top_down_role: Decision making under restricted evaluator communication.

assumptions_latex: Optimization proceeds for \(T\) coordination rounds across \(M\) evaluators.
Round \(t\) permits at most \(b_t\) communicated bits in total.
Local computation and evaluations do not count toward the communication budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The protocol is feasible only if its transcript length satisfies \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(z_t)\le B\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-budget model for federated search; computation and evaluation costs are accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search protocol is communication-limited by budget \(B\) when every admissible execution produces messages \(z_1,\ldots,z_T\) satisfying \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(z_t)\le B\), with the stronger per-round constraints \(\ell(z_t)\le b_t\) when specified. Candidate selection at round \(t\) must be measurable with respect to local information and the transcript available before that round. The optimization output must therefore be computable from local states and a transcript whose total encoded length does not exceed \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A communication-limited search must choose candidates and return its output using a transcript bounded by the declared bit budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Limited Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bit-budget condition fits communication-limited search, but no cited source establishes the chosen transcript, measurability, and accounting model.

children.title: Ownership-Constrained Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Information aggregation limited by organizational or proprietary boundaries.

assumptions_latex: Evaluator \(m\) owns a summary \(s_m\) and declares an admissible transformation class \(\mathcal{G}_m\).
The coordinator uses a declared aggregation map \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate is valid only when it is computed from owner-authorized transformations of every contributed summary.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract authorization constraint on aggregation, without asserting a particular legal, privacy, or cryptographic regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An aggregation is ownership-constrained when each owner \(m\) authorizes a transformation \(g_m\in\mathcal{G}_m\) and the coordinator computes only \(S=A(g_1(s_1),\ldots,g_M(s_M))\). No owner contribution may be replaced by \(h_m(s_m)\) with \(h_m\notin\mathcal{G}_m\), and no intermediate value outside the authorized output of \(g_m\) may enter the coordinator transcript. If an authorization is withdrawn before aggregation, the corresponding contribution must be omitted or recomputed under the remaining authorized inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation may use each owner’s contribution only through an authorized transformation, with withdrawn or unauthorized contributions excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Ownership-Constrained Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but authorization, intermediate-value restrictions, and withdrawal behavior are model-dependent policy claims with no supporting source.

children.title: Batch Construction Families
children.top_down_role: Strategies for selecting diverse and informative collections of evaluations.

children.title: Joint Batch Acquisition
children.top_down_role: Direct optimization over a collection of candidate points.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty candidate domain and \(q\ge1\).
\(a_q:X^q\to\mathbb{R}\) assigns utility to an entire ordered batch.
Repeated points are either allowed by \(X^q\) or excluded by the feasible set \(\mathcal{B}_q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected batch jointly maximizes \(a_q\) over the declared feasible batch set.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct batch-space optimization, independent of the particular acquisition functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the current posterior and feasible batch set \(\mathcal{B}_q\subseteq X^q\), compute \(B^*=(x_1^*,\ldots,x_q^*)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{B\in\mathcal{B}_q}a_q(B)\). The acquisition \(a_q\) must evaluate the collection jointly, including any posterior dependence among its points. Dispatch all elements of \(B^*\) according to the execution regime. After their admissible outcomes are incorporated, rebuild the posterior and repeat. Stop at the declared batch, evaluation, or cost budget and output the incumbent from completed observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize one acquisition function directly over feasible point collections, dispatch the maximizing collection, update after observations, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Batch Acquisition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Direct optimization of a joint acquisition over a feasible batch set fits both the title and algorithm kind, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

children.title: Sequential Greedy Batch Construction
children.top_down_role: Batch construction through repeated conditional selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Greedy Batch Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic greedy batch construction using conditional or fantasized acquisition values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B_0=\varnothing\). For \(k=1,ldots,q\), select \(x_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X\setminus B_{k-1}}a(x\mid D,B_{k-1})\), resolve ties by the fixed rule, and set \(B_k=B_{k-1}\cup\{x_k\}\). The conditional acquisition may integrate over pending outcomes or use a declared fantasy rule, but that rule is fixed before construction. After \(q\) steps, output and dispatch \(B_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a batch of q distinct points one at a time, recomputing a fixed conditional acquisition after each provisional selection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a candidate domain containing at least \(q\ge1\) distinct feasible points.
\(D\subseteq X\times\mathbb{R}\) is the observed dataset.
\(a(x\mid D,P)\) evaluates a point conditional on observed data \(D\) and provisional batch \(P\).
At every step, the acquisition maximum over \(X\setminus B_{k-1}\) is attained, and a deterministic tie-breaking rule is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(B_q\) contains \(q\) distinct points selected by repeated conditional acquisition maximization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs a batch greedily by conditioning each later acquisition decision on fictitious responses at previously selected batch points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal D\), \(b\), \(\alpha\), and \(\mathcal X\), initialize \(\mathcal D'=\mathcal D\). For \(i=1,\ldots,b\), select \(x_i\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x;\mathcal D')\), set \(\widehat y_i=\operatorname{SIMULATE\text{-}OBSERVATION}(x_i,\mathcal D')\), and update \(\mathcal D'\leftarrow\mathcal D'\cup\{(x_i,\widehat y_i)\}\). Return \((x_1,\ldots,x_b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy the observed dataset into a fictitious working dataset. Repeatedly maximize the acquisition function, simulate a response at the selected point, and add that fictitious observation to the working dataset. Return the b selected points as the batch.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D\text{ is the initial dataset.}
b\in\mathbb N\text{ is the requested batch size.}
\alpha(x;\mathcal D')\text{ can be maximized over }\mathcal X.
\operatorname{SIMULATE\text{-}OBSERVATION}(x,\mathcal D')\text{ supplies a fictitious response.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_1,\ldots,x_b)\text{ is a sequentially constructed batch in which later selections condition on fictitious earlier responses.}

children.title: Diversity-Inducing Batch Construction
children.top_down_role: Diversity induced by suppressing neighborhoods of selected points.

children.title: Local Penalization
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood suppression around previously selected batch points.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Penalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative local penalization in which each selected point suppresses acquisition values inside a declared neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(B_0=\varnothing\). For \(k=1,\ldots,q\), choose \(x_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X\setminus B_{k-1}}a_{k-1}(x)\), set \(B_k=B_{k-1}\cup\{x_k\}\), and define \(a_k(x)=a_0(x)\prod_{j=1}^{k}\phi(x;x_j)\). For each selected center \(x_j\), values \(\phi(x;x_j)<1\) suppress the base acquisition within its declared neighborhood, while \(\phi(x;x_j)=1\) outside that neighborhood. After \(q\) selections, output and dispatch \(B_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select q points greedily while multiplying the base acquisition by penalties that suppress candidates in declared neighborhoods of earlier selections.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a domain containing at least \(q\ge1\) distinct feasible points.
\(a_0:X\to[0,\infty)\) is a base acquisition function.
Each selected point \(x_j\) has a declared neighborhood \(N_j\subseteq X\) and a measurable penalizer \(\phi(\cdot;x_j):X\to[0,1]\) satisfying \(\phi(x;x_j)=1\) for every \(x\notin N_j\).
At every selection step, the maximum of the current penalized acquisition over the remaining feasible points is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batch \(B_q\) contains \(q\) points, and every point after the first maximizes the base acquisition multiplied by local penalties induced by earlier selections.

notation.meaning: Local penalizer centered at selected point x_j

children.title: Distance-Based Repulsion
children.top_down_role: Batch diversity induced through separation among candidate points.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Based Repulsion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy batch construction using a fixed metric-separation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(a:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be an acquisition function, let \(q\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\rho:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) be nondecreasing. Initialize \(B_0=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), select
\[x_j\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X} a(x)\prod_{z\in B_{j-1}}\rho(d(x,z)),\qquad B_j=B_{j-1}\cup\{x_j\}.\]
The output is \(B_q\). If \(\rho(r)=0\) for \(r<\delta\), every selected pair satisfies \(d(x_i,x_j)\geq\delta\), provided each maximization admits a point with positive penalized acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct the batch greedily while multiplying acquisition value by penalties that increase with distance from previously selected points; a hard cutoff enforces minimum pairwise separation.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space and each displayed argmax is nonempty.
\(a\) is nonnegative.
\(\rho\) is nondecreasing with values in \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_q\) is a distance-repelled batch; under the hard-cutoff rule, \(d(x_i,x_j)\geq\delta\) for all \(i\neq j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source supports this particular multiplicative repulsion rule or its interpretation as a Bayesian-optimization batch method.

children.title: Uncertainty-Aware Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Exclusion regions adjusted according to posterior uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Aware Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion radii depend on posterior uncertainty around selected batch points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu,\sigma:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be posterior mean and standard deviation, let \(a:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)\), and fix \(\beta,L>0\). Initialize \(B_0=\varnothing\). After selecting \(x_j\), define its exclusion radius
\[r_j=\frac{(M-\mu(x_j)+\sqrt{\beta}\,\sigma(x_j))_+}{L},\]
where \(M\) is a reference upper value. Select the next point by maximizing \(a(x)\) over \(\mathcal X\setminus\bigcup_{i\leq j}\{x:d(x,x_i)<r_i\}\). Stop after \(q\) selections and return the resulting batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each selection, exclude a neighborhood whose radius combines posterior mean, uncertainty, a reference value, and a Lipschitz scale, then optimize outside all excluded regions.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric design space.
\(L>0\), \(\beta>0\), and \(q\in\mathbb N\).
Each constrained acquisition maximization is feasible and attains its maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned batch contains no later point \(x_k\) satisfying \(d(x_k,x_j)<r_j\) for any \(j<k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local placement fit, but the exclusion-radius formula is convention-dependent and cannot be validated without a direct source and locator.

children.title: Overdispersion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Quality loss when diversity pressure separates batch points excessively.

knowledge_statements.title: Overdispersion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Excessive repulsion can sacrifice acquisition quality and local batch refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal X,d)\) be compact and let \(a:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)\) attain its maximum \(a^*>0\). For a required separation \(\delta>0\), define
\[V_q(\delta)=\max_{x_1,\ldots,x_q\in\mathcal X}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^q a(x_i):d(x_i,x_j)\geq\delta\ \text{for }i\neq j\right\}.\]
Then \(V_q(\delta)\) is nonincreasing in \(\delta\). If no \(q\)-point \(\delta\)-packing exists, the constraint is infeasible; if every such packing contains a point outside \(\{x:a(x)\geq\tau\}\), then \(V_q(\delta)<(q-1)a^*+\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As required separation grows, the best attainable total acquisition cannot improve; beyond packing or high-acquisition-region capacity, diversity becomes infeasible or forces a low-value proposal.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is compact.
\(a\) is nonnegative and attains a positive maximum.
\(q\geq2\) and \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large separation can make batch construction infeasible or force acquisition loss, with \(V_q(\delta)\) nonincreasing in \(\delta\).

notation.meaning: optimal total acquisition under pairwise separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but compactness and attainment of the individual maximum do not ensure that the displayed constrained maximum exists without additional regularity such as upper semicontinuity. The domain and range conditions for tau are also unspecified, and no source supports the proposed formalization.

children.title: Posterior-Sampling Batches
children.top_down_role: Parallel proposals generated from sampled surrogate outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Sampling Batches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel proposals obtained by independently optimizing posterior sample paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given data \(D\), a posterior distribution \(\Pi(\mathrm df\mid D)\) on functions \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), and batch size \(q\), independently draw \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\sim\Pi(\cdot\mid D)\). For minimization, choose
\[x_i\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}f_i(x),\qquad i=1,\ldots,q.\]
Evaluate the objective in parallel at the multiset \((x_1,\ldots,x_q)\). If distinct locations are required, replace each argmin by an argmin over \(\mathcal X\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw independent surrogate functions from the posterior and propose each function's optimizer; optionally exclude earlier proposals when distinct batch locations are required.
assumptions_latex: The posterior \(\Pi(\cdot\mid D)\) is well defined.
A measurable optimizer-selection rule exists for posterior-almost-every sample path.
\(q\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditionally on \(D\), each \(x_i\) has the posterior distribution of an optimizer induced by \(\Pi(\cdot\mid D)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basic posterior-sampling batch algorithm fits the topic. However, after imposing sequential exclusion for distinct locations, later proposals no longer generally have the unconstrained posterior distribution of an optimizer, so the conclusion must be limited to the original unconstrained construction. A direct source is also absent.

children.title: Pending-Evaluation Models
children.top_down_role: Representations of evaluations launched but not completed.

children.title: Hypothetical Pending-Outcome Models
children.top_down_role: Pending outcomes represented through hypothetical observations.

children.title: Posterior Fantasy Sampling
children.top_down_role: Pending evaluations represented through sampled hypothetical outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Fantasy Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pending observations are sampled from their joint posterior predictive law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be completed data, let \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) be pending inputs, and let \(p(y_P\mid D,P)\) be their joint posterior predictive density. Draw a fantasy vector \(Y_P^{(s)}\sim p(\cdot\mid D,P)\), form \(D^{(s)}=D\cup\{(p_i,Y_{P,i}^{(s)}):1\leq i\leq m\}\), and compute a next-point acquisition \(a(x;D^{(s)})\). The single-fantasy proposal is
\[x^{(s)}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x;D^{(s)}).\]
The fantasy affects the decision calculation only and is replaced when the actual pending outcomes arrive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample joint hypothetical values at pending inputs, condition the surrogate on them, and optimize the resulting acquisition without treating fantasies as real observations.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior predictive distribution at \(P\) exists.
Fantasy outcomes are sampled jointly, preserving predictive dependence.
The acquisition maximization admits a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{(s)}\) is the next proposal under one posterior-consistent completion of the pending data.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm accurately describes a single posterior fantasy at a conceptual level and fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the stated construction.

children.title: Deterministic Outcome Imputation
children.top_down_role: Pending evaluations represented through fixed surrogate summaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Outcome Imputation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pending outcomes are replaced by fixed point predictions before acquisition optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be completed data and \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) pending inputs. Choose a deterministic imputation map \(h_i=h(p_i,D)\), such as the posterior predictive mean, and form
\[D_h=D\cup\{(p_i,h_i):1\leq i\leq m\}.\]
Fit or condition the surrogate on \(D_h\), compute \(a(x;D_h)\), and return \(x_h\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x;D_h)\). Imputed observations are temporary decision variables and must be replaced, not retained as independent data, when actual outcomes become available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily replace each pending result by a deterministic prediction, update the surrogate with those values, and optimize the resulting acquisition.
assumptions_latex: Each imputation \(h(p_i,D)\) is defined without observing pending outcomes.
The surrogate admits conditioning on \(D_h\).
The acquisition maximization has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_h\) is the proposal produced by the deterministic completion \(D_h\) of the pending data.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic-imputation algorithm fits the terminal container and is internally consistent, but it lacks a direct source with a specific locator.

children.title: Multiple-Fantasy Integration
children.top_down_role: Pending-outcome uncertainty represented across multiple hypothetical datasets.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Fantasy Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo approximation of acquisition averaged over pending outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_P\sim p(\cdot\mid D,P)\) denote the joint unknown outcomes at pending inputs and let \(a(x;D,Y_P)\) be an integrable acquisition after conditioning on those outcomes. The integrated acquisition is
\[\bar a(x)=\mathbb E[a(x;D,Y_P)\mid D,P]=\int a(x;D,y)\,p(\mathrm dy\mid D,P).\]
For independent joint fantasies \(Y_P^{(1)},\ldots,Y_P^{(S)}\), its Monte Carlo representation is \(\widehat a_S(x)=S^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^S a(x;D,Y_P^{(s)})\), which is conditionally unbiased for \(\bar a(x)\) at every fixed \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average the acquisition over the joint predictive distribution of pending results; multiple joint fantasies provide a conditionally unbiased Monte Carlo approximation at each fixed candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(a(x;D,Y_P)\) is integrable for each fixed \(x\).
The fantasy vectors are conditionally independent draws from \(p(\cdot\mid D,P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat a_S(x)\mid D,P]=\bar a(x)\) for every fixed \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and fixed-candidate conditional-unbiasedness statement are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no cited source supports their use as the designated multiple-fantasy integration construction.

children.title: Imputation Bias
children.top_down_role: Decision distortion caused by systematically inaccurate pending-outcome substitutes.

knowledge_statements.title: Imputation Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear decisions generally invalidate plug-in replacement of uncertain pending outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_P\) be an integrable pending-outcome vector and let \(g_x(Y_P)=a(x;D,Y_P)\). Mean imputation uses \(g_x(\mathbb E[Y_P\mid D,P])\), whereas correct integration uses \(\mathbb E[g_x(Y_P)\mid D,P]\). These quantities need not agree. In particular, if \(g_x\) is strictly convex on the conditional support of nondegenerate \(Y_P\), then
\[g_x(\mathbb E[Y_P\mid D,P])<\mathbb E[g_x(Y_P)\mid D,P].\]
Equality is guaranteed when \(g_x\) is affine on that support; otherwise deterministic imputation can change acquisition values and their optimizer ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plugging in the predictive mean generally differs from averaging over pending outcomes; strict convexity yields downward bias, while affinity guarantees equality.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_P\) is conditionally integrable.
For the strict inequality, \(g_x\) is strictly convex and \(Y_P\) is conditionally nondegenerate.
All displayed expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deterministic mean imputation is generally biased for integrated acquisition; affinity is a sufficient equality boundary.

notation.meaning: acquisition as a function of pending outcomes at fixed x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits the leaf, but strict convexity merely on a possibly nonconvex conditional support is insufficient for the stated strict Jensen inequality; convexity must hold on an appropriate convex domain containing the support and conditional mean. No direct source is supplied.

children.title: Integrated Pending Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Decision quality averaged over uncertainty in unfinished evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Pending Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayes decision criterion marginalizing unfinished evaluation outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be completed observations, \(P\) pending inputs, \(Y_P\sim p(\cdot\mid D,P)\), and \(U(x;D,Y_P)\) an integrable utility of choosing \(x\in\mathcal X\) after the pending outcomes are revealed. The pending-outcome-integrated decision rule is
\[x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\bar U(x),\qquad \bar U(x)=\int U(x;D,y)\,p(\mathrm dy\mid D,P).\]
Thus uncertainty about unfinished evaluations is marginalized under its joint predictive law before comparing current decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate each candidate by averaging its conditional utility over the joint predictive distribution of unfinished outcomes, then maximize that integrated utility.
assumptions_latex: \(U(x;D,Y_P)\) is integrable for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The joint predictive law \(p(\cdot\mid D,P)\) exists.
The argmax of \(\bar U\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) maximizes posterior expected utility after marginalizing all pending outcomes.

notation.meaning: joint random outcomes at pending inputs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pending-outcome marginalization representation matches the topic and is mathematically coherent, but the record has no inspectable citation for this decision rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-step asynchronous Bayesian optimization with pending experiments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step reduction only; the source warns that multistep lookahead must account for uncertain completion order and is generally much harder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be the current data, \(\mathbf x'\in\mathcal X^{b'}\) a batch already under evaluation, and \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal X^b\) a proposed batch. For their unknown outcomes \(\mathbf y'\) and \(\mathbf y\), let \(\mathcal D_1=\mathcal D\cup\{(\mathbf x,\mathbf y),(\mathbf x',\mathbf y')\}\). The one-step expected utility gain is
\[
\beta_1(\mathbf x;\mathbf x',\mathcal D)=\mathbb E\!\left[u(\mathcal D_1)\mid\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathcal D\right]-u(\mathcal D)
=\iint u(\mathcal D_1)p(\mathbf y,\mathbf y'\mid\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathcal D)\,d\mathbf y\,d\mathbf y'-u(\mathcal D).
\]
This is the synchronous one-step score for the combined batch \((\mathbf x,\mathbf x')\), with optimization restricted to \(\mathbf x\) because \(\mathbf x'\) is already fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-step asynchronous policy averages utility over the unknown outcomes of both the proposed and pending experiments. Its selection problem is the synchronous combined-batch problem with the pending batch fixed. This reduction is limited to one-step lookahead; uncertain experiment completion order makes multistep lookahead substantially more difficult.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D\text{ is the current data set.}
\mathbf x\in\mathcal X^b\text{ is selectable, while }\mathbf x'\in\mathcal X^{b'}\text{ is already pending.}
(\mathbf y,\mathbf y')\sim p(\mathbf y,\mathbf y'\mid\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathcal D).
\mathbb E[|u(\mathcal D_1)|\mid\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathcal D]<\infty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal X^b}\beta_1(\mathbf x;\mathbf x',\mathcal D)\text{ is the synchronous combined-batch one-step optimization problem restricted by fixing }\mathbf x'.
