knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tail-shift interaction occurs when a runtime-tail change between regimes depends on the evaluated design or operating context.
assumptions_latex: Both conditional survival probabilities are positive on the declared tail range.
The same runtime and context definitions are used in both regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonconstancy of \(\rho(t,x,z)\) in \(x\) or \(z\) identifies a regime-by-design or regime-by-context tail interaction.

notation.meaning: conditional runtime survival function in regime s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonconstant conditional tail ratios provide a checkable interaction criterion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonconstant conditional tail-ratio criterion is coherent and fits an interaction regime, but it is one particular multiplicative interaction definition and has no inspectable source establishing that choice.

children.title: Completion-Time Model Failures
children.top_down_role: Scheduling failures caused by inadequate runtime representations.

assumptions_latex: \(F_x\) and \(\widehat F_x\) are distribution functions on nonnegative completion times.
The tolerance \(\delta>0\) is fixed by the scheduling guarantee or application.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in A,\,t\geq 0}|\widehat F_x(t)-F_x(t)|\geq\delta\) violates any assumed uniform error bound strictly below \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes misspecification of the full runtime distribution relevant to scheduling decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)\) be the evaluation completion time, let \(F_x(t):=\mathbb P(T(x)\leq t\mid x)\) be its true conditional distribution function, and let \(\widehat F_x\) be the predictive distribution function. For a declared design set \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\) and tolerance \(\delta>0\), the predictive model is \(\delta\)-misspecified on \(A\) when \[\sup_{x\in A,\,t\geq 0}\left|\widehat F_x(t)-F_x(t)\right|\geq\delta.\] This boundary includes errors caused by incorrect tail decay, ignored censoring, or omitted dependence on launch time or context. Any scheduling guarantee assuming a uniform distribution-function error strictly below \(\delta\) is outside its stated assumptions when this boundary is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completion-time model is delta-misspecified when its predictive runtime distribution differs from the true conditional distribution by at least delta uniformly over the declared design and time domain; guarantees requiring a smaller uniform error then do not apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Time Model Failures

children.title: Irrecoverable Resource Commitment
children.top_down_role: Long evaluations that cannot be paused, reused, or cheaply abandoned.

assumptions_latex: Resource consumption \(c\) and reusable value \(V(c)\) share a common nonnegative accounting unit.
An incomplete evaluation produces no final objective observation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<c<C\Longrightarrow L(c)=c\), and restarting requires a fresh resource commitment of \(C\).

notation.meaning: reusable value after stopping at consumption c
recoverable value from outstanding committed resources

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero reusable value and zero recoverable commitment formalize sunk resource commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes evaluations whose consumed resources and committed capacity have no recoverable value after abandonment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an evaluation requiring total resource \(C>0\). If it is stopped after consuming \(c\in(0,C)\), let \(V(c)\geq 0\) be the resource-equivalent value of reusable intermediate state and let \(R(c)\geq 0\) be the recoverable value of outstanding committed resources. The evaluation has irrecoverable resource commitment when \[V(c)=0\quad\text{and}\quad R(c)=0\qquad\text{for every }c\in(0,C).\] Its consumed-resource sunk loss is then \(L(c):=c-V(c)=c\), and restarting requires a fresh resource commitment of \(C\). This definition excludes checkpointable or transferable evaluations having positive reusable or recoverable value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource commitment is irrecoverable when stopping an incomplete evaluation yields neither reusable intermediate work nor recoverable value from outstanding commitments, so consumed resources are sunk and restarting requires the full resource commitment again.
knowledge_statements.title: Irrecoverable Resource Commitment

children.title: Adaptive Observation-Scheduling Bias Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Bias induced by adaptive observation, replication, completion, censoring, or worker assignment.

children.title: Informative Evaluation Failures
children.top_down_role: Failure events correlated with objective or feasibility outcomes.

assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\) is well-defined even when the evaluation fails to report it.
\(H\) contains only information observed before the failure event.
The relevant conditional distributions exist, and successful evaluation has positive conditional probability where the observed-outcome comparison is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(x)\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(x)\mid(x,H)\) characterizes informative evaluation failure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dependence of missingness on the latent outcome is the standard informative-missingness criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines failures whose probability depends on latent objective or feasibility outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\) be the latent objective or feasibility outcome at design \(x\), let \(M(x)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that the evaluation fails to return \(Y(x)\), and let \(H\) be the observed pre-evaluation history. Failure is noninformative when \[\mathbb P(M(x)=1\mid Y(x),x,H)=\mathbb P(M(x)=1\mid x,H)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Failure is informative when this conditional-independence equality fails. Equivalently, \(M(x)\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(x)\mid(x,H)\). Under informative failure, conditioning on successful observation can alter the outcome law, so the observed-success distribution need not equal the latent conditional outcome distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation failure is informative when its probability depends on the latent objective or feasibility outcome after conditioning on the design and information available before evaluation; successful observations can therefore have a different distribution from the latent outcomes.
knowledge_statements.title: Informative Evaluation Failures

children.title: Informative Completion Times
children.top_down_role: Runtime carrying information about unobserved outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Informative Completion Times
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines outcome-dependent runtimes in asynchronous Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an evaluation requested at design-source pair \(a=(x,s)\) produce outcome \(Y_a\) and completion time \(T_a\in[0,\infty]\), conditional on the pre-request history \(\mathcal H\). The completion time is informative precisely when \[Y_a\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp T_a\mid(a,\mathcal H).\] Equivalently, there exist measurable sets \(B\) and \(C\) such that \[\Pr(Y_a\in B,T_a\in C\mid a,\mathcal H)\ne\Pr(Y_a\in B\mid a,\mathcal H)\Pr(T_a\in C\mid a,\mathcal H).\] Consequently, observing completion or noncompletion can update the posterior distribution of \(Y_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completion time is informative when, given the requested evaluation and prior history, runtime and the unobserved outcome are conditionally dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_a\) and \(T_a\) are random variables on a common probability space.
Regular conditional distributions given \((a,\mathcal H)\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_a\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp T_a\mid(a,\mathcal H)\).
review_flags: Exact source for outcome-dependent evaluation times is absent from the supplied locator hints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Informative Completion Times leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation or inspectable locator supports outcome-dependent completion times in asynchronous Bayesian optimization. A directly relevant source is required before the conditional-dependence formulation can enter candidate review.

children.title: Adaptive Early-Stopping Bias
children.top_down_role: Distorted evidence caused by selectively truncated evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Early-Stopping Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes selection bias induced by outcome-dependent truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an evaluation at \(a\), let \(Y_a\) be its full-fidelity outcome and let \(S_a\in\{0,1\}\) indicate survival to the reporting stage. If stopping is adaptive so that \(\Pr(S_a=1\mid Y_a,a,\mathcal H)\) is not almost surely constant in \(Y_a\), then the reported-outcome law is \[p(y\mid S_a=1,a,\mathcal H)=\frac{\Pr(S_a=1\mid y,a,\mathcal H)p(y\mid a,\mathcal H)}{\Pr(S_a=1\mid a,\mathcal H)}.\] Hence treating survivors as unselected observations generally targets a different distribution from \(p(y\mid a,\mathcal H)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outcome-dependent early stopping reweights the distribution of reported evaluations, so a model that ignores selection generally learns a biased outcome law.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\Pr(S_a=1\mid a,\mathcal H)<1\).
The displayed conditional density or corresponding Radon–Nikodym derivative exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(\cdot\mid S_a=1,a,\mathcal H)\ne p(\cdot\mid a,\mathcal H)\) unless the selection weighting is distributionally neutral.

notation.meaning: indicator that an evaluation survives early stopping
history available when stopping is decided

review_flags: Supplied sources do not specifically locate adaptive truncation or selection-bias results.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection-reweighting identity is appropriate to Adaptive Early-Stopping Bias, and the property content kind fits. However, no source is supplied for adaptive truncation, survivor selection, or the stated conditional law, so the record requires an authoritative, specifically located citation.

children.title: Preferential Replication Bias
children.top_down_role: Unequal replication changing which regions have accurately estimated outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Preferential Replication Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes design-dependent precision created by adaptive replication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_{x,j}=f(x)+\varepsilon_{x,j}\), where the noises are conditionally independent with mean zero and variance \(\sigma^2(x)\). If an adaptive policy assigns \(N_x\) replications to design \(x\), then, conditional on \(N_x=n>0\), the sample mean has variance \[\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_x\mid N_x=n,x)=\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{n}.\] Thus unequal replication produces unequal precision. Moreover, if \(N_x\) depends on previously observed outcomes and that adaptivity is ignored, the joint observed sample need not have the fixed-design sampling law used by the surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preferential replication gives favored regions smaller observation variance; outcome-driven replication can additionally invalidate a surrogate model that treats replication counts as fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_{x,j}=f(x)+\varepsilon_{x,j}\) with conditionally independent, mean-zero noise.
The variance calculation conditions on a realized replication count \(n>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_x\mid N_x=n,x)=\sigma^2(x)/n\), so spatially varying \(N_x\) induces spatially varying precision.

notation.meaning: number of replications allocated to design x
mean of the replicated observations at x

review_flags: Variance identity is standard, but the preferential-sampling claim needs a directly supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and unequal-precision theme fit the leaf, but the displayed conditional variance is not justified when the replication count is selected adaptively from the same observations: conditioning on N_x=n can change their joint law. A source and corrected hypotheses, such as replication-count independence or a pre-allocation condition, are required.

children.title: Resource-Allocation Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where apparent cost savings reduce effective information acquisition.

children.title: Cheap-Source Overuse
children.top_down_role: Persistent allocation to inexpensive but weakly informative evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cheap-Source Overuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies allocation policies dominated by cost rather than decision-relevant information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let source \(s\) have cost \(c_s>0\), and let \(I_t(x,s)\ge0\) denote its conditional information gain about the optimization target at time \(t\). A policy exhibits cheap-source overuse when some source \(s_0\) satisfies \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{s_t=s_0\}}{T}>0,\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty} I_t(x_t,s_0)=0,\] while an available source has information gain bounded away from zero infinitely often. The policy then spends a positive asymptotic fraction of evaluations on vanishingly informative observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cheap-source overuse occurs when a policy repeatedly selects a low-cost source after its information value vanishes, despite informative alternatives remaining available.
assumptions_latex: All source costs satisfy \(c_s>0\).
Conditional information gains \(I_t(x,s)\) are well-defined and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive asymptotic evaluation fraction is allocated to a source whose realized conditional information gain tends to zero.

notation.meaning: conditional information gain from querying x at source s

review_flags: This asymptotic formalization is not supported by a source-specific locator in the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the appropriate content kind, but the proposed asymptotic criterion has no supporting source and never requires s_0 to be cheap relative to alternative sources despite the title. The exact boundary and its cost condition require sourced reformulation.

children.title: Replication Balance Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Poor balance between exploration and variance reduction.

children.title: Under-Replication
children.top_down_role: Insufficient repeated evaluation for reliable uncertainty reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Under-Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines insufficient replication relative to a target estimation precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At design \(x\), suppose independent replications have variance \(\sigma^2(x)>0\), and let \(\bar Y_{x,n}\) be their mean. For a required standard-error tolerance \(\epsilon_x>0\), replication is insufficient whenever \[n<\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{\epsilon_x^2}.\] Indeed, \(\operatorname{se}(\bar Y_{x,n})=\sigma(x)/\sqrt n>\epsilon_x\). For a sequence of designs, persistent under-replication means this inequality holds infinitely often at decision-relevant queried designs, preventing their Monte Carlo uncertainty from meeting the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A design is under-replicated when its replication count is too small to reduce the sample-mean standard error below the required tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Replications at \(x\) are independent with common finite variance \(\sigma^2(x)>0\).
The estimator is the arithmetic mean of \(n\ge1\) replications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n<\sigma^2(x)/\epsilon_x^2\) implies \(\operatorname{se}(\bar Y_{x,n})>\epsilon_x\).
review_flags: Supplied variance-reduction locators do not specifically establish this replication boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard-error calculation is correct under the stated independence assumptions, and failure boundary fits the leaf. The designation of this threshold as the Under-Replication boundary is nevertheless uncited and needs a specifically located replication-allocation or simulation-estimation source.

children.title: Over-Replication
children.top_down_role: Excessive repeated evaluation at the expense of broader search.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines replication whose marginal precision gain is below its opportunity cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent observations at \(x\) with variance \(\sigma^2(x)\), the variance of the mean after \(n\) replications is \(V_x(n)=\sigma^2(x)/n\). The marginal variance reduction from one additional replication is \[\Delta_x(n)=V_x(n)-V_x(n+1)=\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{n(n+1)}.\] Given a minimum worthwhile reduction \(\tau_x>0\), design \(x\) is over-replicated at count \(n\) when \(\Delta_x(n)<\tau_x\) while another feasible evaluation has marginal decision value at least \(\tau_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-replication begins when another repeat yields less variance reduction than the required value threshold while a more valuable evaluation remains feasible.
assumptions_latex: Replications are independent with common finite variance \(\sigma^2(x)>0\).
Marginal values are compared in the same variance-reduction units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma^2(x)/(n(n+1))<\tau_x\) marks over-replication when an alternative achieves marginal value at least \(\tau_x\).

notation.meaning: variance of the n-replication sample mean
marginal variance reduction from replication n+1

review_flags: The opportunity-cost threshold is a local formalization requiring a dedicated replication-allocation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The marginal variance-reduction identity is correct, and failure boundary fits the container. The opportunity-cost criterion is an uncited local definition, and the alternative evaluation's marginal decision value is not formally introduced beyond an asserted common unit. A dedicated source and precise value definition are required.

children.title: Replication Balance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Resource regimes governing the balance between repeated measurement and domain coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication Balance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitions replication by marginal variance reduction relative to a value threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_x(n)=\sigma^2(x)/n\) and \(\Delta_x(n)=V_x(n)-V_x(n+1)\). For a target standard error \(\epsilon_x>0\) and marginal-value threshold \(\tau_x>0\), the replication count \(n\) lies in the under-replication regime if \(V_x(n)>\epsilon_x^2\), in the balanced regime if \[V_x(n)\le\epsilon_x^2\quad\text{and}\quad\Delta_x(n)\ge\tau_x,\] and in the over-replication regime if \(V_x(n)\le\epsilon_x^2\) but \(\Delta_x(n)<\tau_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication is under-balanced before the precision target, balanced while precision is adequate and another repeat remains valuable, and over-balanced after marginal value falls below threshold.
assumptions_latex: Observations at each design are independent with finite variance \(\sigma^2(x)>0\).
The thresholds \(\epsilon_x\) and \(\tau_x\) are fixed and positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicates based on \(V_x(n)\), \(\epsilon_x^2\), and \(\Delta_x(n)\) specify the three replication regimes.

notation.meaning: variance reduction from one further replication

review_flags: The supplied sources discuss variance reduction generally but not this three-regime taxonomy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a suitable kind for a regime classification, but the three-regime taxonomy and its two thresholds are not sourced. The plain statement also uses 'under-balanced' and 'over-balanced' where the LaTeX statement defines under-replication and over-replication. A sourced, terminology-consistent version is required.

children.title: Variance-Reduction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions where replication fails to deliver commensurate uncertainty reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when replication fails to deliver vanishing estimator variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_{x,1},\ldots,Y_{x,n}\) be exchangeable replications with common variance \(\sigma^2(x)>0\) and pairwise correlation \(\rho_x\). Their mean satisfies \[\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_{x,n})=\sigma^2(x)\left(\rho_x+\frac{1-\rho_x}{n}\right).\] Consequently, replication yields the usual \(n^{-1}\) variance decay only when \(\rho_x=0\). If \(\rho_x>0\), the variance has the nonzero floor \(\rho_x\sigma^2(x)\); if the effective replication count remains bounded, variance likewise cannot vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication ceases to provide vanishing uncertainty when repeats remain positively correlated or when the effective number of independent repeats stays bounded.
assumptions_latex: Replications are exchangeable with common finite variance.
Every distinct pair has the same admissible correlation \(\rho_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_{x,n})=\rho_x\sigma^2(x)\), giving a positive variance floor when \(\rho_x>0\).

notation.meaning: pairwise correlation between replications at x

review_flags: The exact exchangeable-correlation formula must be checked against the cited section.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exchangeable equal-correlation variance formula is mathematically standard and failure boundary fits the leaf. However, the cited generic variance-reduction section has not been shown to support this exact correlated-replication formula or the effective-count claim. Full-text verification or a direct locator is required.

children.title: Batch Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Parallel points providing largely overlapping information.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures overlapping Gaussian information within a parallel batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given history \(\mathcal H\), let a batch \(B=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\) have Gaussian predictive covariance matrix \(K_B\), and let observation-noise variance be \(\sigma_n^2>0\). Define its joint information gain by \[I(B)=\frac12\log\det\!\left(I_q+\sigma_n^{-2}K_B\right).\] For tolerance \(\eta\ge0\), the batch is \(\eta\)-redundant when \[\sum_{i=1}^q I(\{x_i\})-I(B)\ge\eta.\] The nonnegative gap quantifies information counted repeatedly by evaluating strongly correlated points in parallel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch is redundant when the sum of its points' individual information gains substantially exceeds their joint information gain because their predictions are correlated.
assumptions_latex: The conditional predictive distribution over the batch is Gaussian.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian noise with variance \(\sigma_n^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i I(\{x_i\})-I(B)\ge\eta\) is the batch-redundancy condition.

notation.meaning: conditional predictive covariance matrix for the batch

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports parallel Gaussian batch information or the redundancy gap.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gaussian information formula and redundancy gap are coherent under the stated covariance and noise model, and condition fits the leaf. No source supports this particular batch-redundancy definition or threshold, so a directly relevant Gaussian-process batch-information citation is required.

children.title: Parallel Utilization Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Poor utilization or delayed batches eroding wall-clock gains.

children.title: Worker Starvation
children.top_down_role: Loss of throughput when available workers lack useful assigned evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Worker Starvation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines persistent idleness caused by an insufficient ready-task supply.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(m\ge1\) workers. Let \(A(t)\) be the number of active evaluations and \(Q(t)\) the number of evaluations ready for dispatch at time \(t\). The idle-worker count is \[J(t)=\bigl(m-A(t)\bigr)_+.\] Worker starvation occurs on an interval \(I\) when \(J(t)>0\) and \(Q(t)=0\) on a subset of \(I\) having positive measure. It is persistent when \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac1{mT}\int_0^T J(t)\mathbf 1\{Q(t)=0\}\,dt>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers are starved when capacity is idle because no evaluation is ready to dispatch; persistent starvation consumes a positive asymptotic fraction of worker time.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\) identical worker slots.
The processes \(A(t)\) and \(Q(t)\) are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent starvation is equivalent to a positive limsup of unavailable-task idle worker-time per unit capacity.
review_flags: The supplied source inventory contains no queueing or parallel-scheduling locator for this definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary fits Worker Starvation, and the utilization integral is internally coherent as a definition. The precise positive-measure and asymptotic-limsup criteria are uncited, so a queueing or parallel-scheduling source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Straggler Dominance
children.top_down_role: Elapsed-time degradation caused by exceptionally slow evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Straggler Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes synchronous batches whose makespan is dominated by the slowest task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a synchronous batch of \(q\ge2\) evaluations with completion times \(T_1,\\ldots,T_q>0\), define makespan \(M_q=\max_i T_i\) and total work \(W_q=\sum_i T_i\). For \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), the batch is \(\alpha\)-straggler-dominated when \[\frac{M_q}{W_q}\ge\alpha.\] If batches satisfy \(M_q/W_q\to1\), asymptotically one evaluation accounts for nearly all work and determines the synchronization time. In particular, all other workers wait after completing their assigned evaluations until the straggler finishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous batch is straggler-dominated when its slowest evaluation contributes a large fraction of total work and therefore controls batch completion.
assumptions_latex: The batch waits for every evaluation before advancing.
All completion times are finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_q/W_q\ge\alpha\) is the stated dominance condition; the extreme regime has \(M_q/W_q\to1\).
review_flags: A direct source for this chosen straggler-dominance metric is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the leaf, but the completion-time list contains malformed LaTeX ('\\ldots'). More importantly, the claim that all other workers wait requires an assignment model connecting q evaluations to workers, which is not stated. The chosen M_q/W_q dominance metric is also uncited and requires direct support.

children.title: Utilization Collapse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operating regimes where effective worker use falls substantially below capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Utilization Collapse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies asymptotically vanishing use of available parallel capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) workers, let \(A_m(t)\in\{0,\ldots,m\}\) be the number active at time \(t\), and define horizon-\(T\) utilization by \[U_m(T)=\frac1{mT}\int_0^T A_m(t)\,dt.\] Temporal utilization collapse occurs when \(\liminf_{T\to\infty}U_m(T)=0\) for fixed \(m\). Scaling collapse occurs for a family of systems when \[\lim_{m\to\infty}\limsup_{T\to\infty}U_m(T)=0.\] Either regime means that asymptotically almost all available worker-time is idle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Utilization collapses when the active fraction of worker-time approaches zero, either over long time for a fixed system or as worker count scales.
assumptions_latex: The active-worker process \(A_m(t)\) is measurable.
Worker capacity is constant over each measured horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed temporal or scaling limit equal to zero defines the corresponding utilization-collapse regime.

notation.meaning: active workers at time t in an m-worker system
average capacity utilization through time T

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports these temporal and scaling utilization regimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary fits the leaf, but liminf_{T to infinity} U_m(T)=0 only guarantees arbitrarily low-utilization horizons, not that utilization approaches zero or that asymptotically almost all worker-time is idle. This conflicts with the plain statement and conclusion. A source is also needed for the temporal and scaling regimes before selecting the correct limit formulation.

children.title: Batch-Completion Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Progress limits caused by dependence on the slowest evaluations in a batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Completion Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous Bayesian-optimization batches whose next decision waits for every evaluation in the current batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a synchronous batch of \(m\ge 2\) evaluations with positive completion times \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\), the batch duration, throughput, and realized worker utilization are respectively
\[
B_m=\max_{1\le i\le m}T_i,\qquad Q_m=\frac{m}{B_m},\qquad U_m=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^m T_i}{mB_m}\le 1.
\]
Thus completion is bottlenecked by the slowest evaluation. For a sequence of batches indexed by \(m\), utilization collapses whenever
\[
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^m T_i}{m\max_iT_i}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
In particular, this occurs if \(\sum_iT_i=o(m\max_iT_i)\); increasing batch size then fails to yield proportional effective parallelism despite all workers being assigned evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous batch advances only after its slowest evaluation finishes. Utilization collapses when total useful worker-time is negligible relative to worker count times the longest completion time.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 2\) workers execute one evaluation each without preemption or reassignment.
The optimizer begins its next batch only after all \(m\) current evaluations complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_m=\max_iT_i\) and \(U_m=(\sum_iT_i)/(m\max_iT_i)\); hence \(\sum_iT_i=o(m\max_iT_i)\) implies \(U_m\to0\).

notation.meaning: Completion time of evaluation assigned to worker \(i\).
Wall-clock completion time of the synchronous batch.
Fraction of available worker-time spent performing evaluations before the batch barrier.

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports synchronous batch barriers, order-statistic completion time, or utilization collapse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the finite-batch identities are mathematically correct under simultaneous starts, one job per worker, and a barrier before the next batch. However, no citation or inspectable locator supports the synchronous-batch model or utilization-collapse characterization. In the asymptotic claim, completion times should also be indexed as a triangular array, such as T_{m,i}, because both the batch and its size vary with m. A source and corrected asymptotic indexing are required before acceptance.
